Other than the previously mentioned connection problems I face, some people think the DLC policy is pretty bad, and it is, but it is possible to unlock the important things fairly easily just by playing, every matchmaking game you win you get 50 "fight money," every time you level up a character you get 1000 FM, you can get 6000-10,000 FM weekly doing challenges, winning survival on each difficulty for the first time on each character also grants you fairly large chunks of FM. Basically, play everything the game has to offer and characters suddenly seem easy enough to just unlock, with some patience.
I reccomend if you want a good fighting game to play against others with.

This game is everything wrong about a point&click game.
For starters, I do not hate point&click games, I actually like them. I have a high level account on aqworlds and I enjoy getting on sometimes.
Let's get back on track, and I will describe each aspect of this game.
1.Controls:
This game has decent controls. The idea is a point and click. You click an enemy to attack; you click on the ground to move there. One thing this game actually did right.
2.Graphics:
For a game thats around 300MB, the graphics are alright. For basing it on games around the time period it was created, the graphics are terrible. The environment looks like it's been pooped on and the NPCs look like stiff old grandparents.
Your character looks ugly. He is a scruff, tall black haired man with an eyepatch. Who would want to play a game as a character like that? And no, this is definitly NOT a pirate game.
3.Logic
This game has no logic. The NPCs in the beginning say how your character is the only one who can defeat the aliens. There are many problems with that. If the NPCs depend on you, they would give you gear and money. You start off with no money and just your fists.  YOU HAVE TO KILL ALIENS THAT SHOOT AT YOU WITH YOUR FISTS. You will have to go back and forth between the environment and your base in order to heal over and over. If you die once, you have to go back to your last save point. The game only autosaves between maps, and going to your base is NOT an autosave point. Finally, everything in the base looks futuristic with machinery and such, right? Your main weapon is a BOW. WHY?!?! This game should have you using energy swords and epic gauntlets and plasma weapons, not clubs, swords, and a BOW. A normal ol' BOW!
4.Gameplay
Horrid, repetitive and boring. The enemies drop so little money you have to grind for hours to buy one little weapon. In order to use weapons, your level has to rise. I farmed for an hour and still haven't past level 1. Drop rates are horrendous and you're likely to get a weapon that doesn't even work for you. This game is a clone for Path of Exile I believe, so play that, and not this pile of garbage.
5.Replayability/Multiplayer/Local
You cannot play with more than one player. This is a one player game, with an MMO system. What's so good about hitting max level if there's no one around you to show it off too? No replay value with no new mechanics or anything if you win(I got too bored to even try to win). Also, this game never updates so there's no point in playing any more, and no DLC. No new character models. NOTHING.
Final Score: 2/10
The only reason it gets a 2 was that I got this game for free(1), and the fact that it's a game(1). It's the worst of the worst, and unless you won this in a giveaway(I understand why it was given away), don't buy this.

As a major AvP geek who collected the comics from the very beginning... I even had issue 0, I can safely say that this is the last semi-decent thing made in the franchise(EDIT: I have not played Alien Isolation). But... there are no surprises here and some huge disappointments. If you like to be scared, the human single player campaign has it's moments. If you are interested in the single player, give it a go. I think it's worth the money--if it's on sale. This was the game, by the way, that introduced me to Steam since it required a Steam account to play. Whether or not that's a good thing, I'll leave for you to decide. I never finished the campaign, however, because I just didn't find it that compelling. If you like the franchise a lot and for some reason haven't yet tried this game, maybe you should see what it has to offer yourself the next time it goes on sale.
The reason I stopped playing, and my greatest cause for hesitation in recommending this title, is that the multiplayer is broken in terms of balance. When playing online, my typical experience as a player attempting to play as an alien would be that a few predators would essentially wipe the map clean in no time. Again and again. In order for the alien game to work in multiplayer, you have to have a well-coordinated team working together, like in the comics and movies. Otherwise you get what you have in the mp games online--too many predators, not enough aliens, or even marines. Also, I don't usually whine about cheats and hacks, but I have some concerns because of the (albeit limited) interactions I experienced online. If you have a large group of friends or a clan, this could be a lot of fun with clear limits set forth on how many players per species to keep things balanced and in proper ratio. So, with those concerns stated, If you like this franchise, give it a go if you don't think you'll mind the problems I've stated here. One more thing, the last few times I played online it seemed that the mp community was dying, probably for some of the very same reasons I've mentioned here. So you may or may not have much chance to experience online play depending upon the current state of that aspect of the game.

, and
once. It's a big world to explore, and it takes a lot of time to actually see it all, but the moment you try to replay anything, the illusion breaks.

Second is  in "horror" genre.  It is fairly claustrophobic and tense at times.  This game keeps on spawning Imps and stuff behind you, or when you open the door there is always something jumping.  It just gets too repetitive. Deadspace got more wacky and frustrating towards the end, but this one is better than 'Deadspace' series.   I also feel that although Doom 1 and 2 were far older tech, they definitely had a more disturbing and hellish environment.  But within the genre, I still like Amnesia far more.
Third is FPS - while it has good mechanics, I don't like the guns much.  The monsters shaking and hitting you from all around is a bit too much.  Imps were too strong compared to before and I couldn't enjoy Cacos or Pinkys as in previous versions.   Also it is mostly closed area combat whereas in Doom 2 it was open space.  You could run around and start getting them to shoot each other- it was a frenzy.  This one is basically being boxed out to a spot.
Fourth, is Doom 3 vs. Doom 3 BFG Edition.  I did not see a huge graphics upgrade between them but flashlight being turned on in addition to the gun is a huge plus.  Why would you fight hellish creatures with a flashlight in one hand, but turn it off to shoot???  Also, Doom 3 plus Ressurection should have been a single game.  It is a single story and I think they got too greedy with this.  10 hrs of gameplay plus 5 hours DLC?? But at least they follow each other.  However Lost Mission DLC is definitely a lost cause- It is by far the worst DLC I have seen in any game.  This is the definition of 'linear game' because you have no choice other then move forward.  And this is dull.  It feels like they gave this to their Juniors to develop - many of the same maps reused and just monsters respawning.  So if you played Doom 3 and or Resurrection, you don't need BFG Edition.  But if you start from scratch, I would go with BFG but not play Lost Mission.
Last is the enjoyment factor. Do you really want to waste 20 hours of your life here?  Comparing it to other games like Bioshock Infinite, Tombraider, Skyrim etc, this is just not fun enough,  You know that something will jump or spawn somewhere but basically that is it.  I turned to Godmode after a while not to lose time anymore and that was a right decision.
So overall as a game it is OK and playable for horror seekers, but I think in 2014 we have far more options to enjoy.   It is not a bad game but you just want it to end after a while :)

Despite it initially having amazing potential to be a near-flawless modern equivalent of Moo2 (Master of Orion 2 - the quintessential 4x strategy game from the 90s), the developer has effectively ceased meaningful work on this project.
I, like many Steam members, purchased this game during the so-called "beta" stage with the intention of ultimately playing the game in a fully-functional completed state. Unfortunately, this will never happen as the developer (a guy going by the name of "Zero") simply proclaimed the same beta-level product as "final" and proceeded to publicly state that any future progress will be solely at his own personal "whims".
At the time of this writing (10/10/13), the game is known to be *extremely* buggy with large swaths of functionality crippled or non-existant. Past promises of additional features go unfullfilled (multiplayer, etc.). Further, anyone with the gall to complain about the situation (however civil they may be) on the developer or Steam forums is promptly banned and any associated content is deleted (I know this because I have similarly been banned from the StarDrive Steam forums). NOTE: My specific offense... The action that immediately prompted my banning... was that I noticed that a particular thread which was critical of StarDrive was deleted and so I asked why. I suspect that the aggressive action being taken against anyone who complains is a result of the game currently being on-sale, advertised on the Steam main page as a "daily deal" (Zero surely wouldn't want customers' 100% valid concerns & complaints to negatively affect sales of this very dead project).
Check the StarDrive forums on Steam for yourself and you will certainly come across content from angry customers who (rightly) feel cheated - that is, if you get to it before said posts are deleted. As I write this, StarDrive is being advertised & sold on Steam's front page. I sincerely pity anyone unfortunate enough to purchase this steaming pile only to inevitably find out how they've been robbed.
What's most offensive (aside from the literal theft which is being perpetrated - that is, the game being advertised as beyond beta and fully functional), is the *EXTREME* arrogance displayed by the developer. Observe a snippet from a forum post on the official StarDrive website (before it was deleted):
"Zero: I'll be as clear as I can be... I think StarDrive vanilla is a fine game. I'm happy with it. I'll be patching it here and there as my whims take me. If you feel cheated by StarDrive, kindly scroll up to the upper right portion of your browser screen and click the "Logout" button. I don't want to hear it."
There you have it, directly from the horse's (Zero's) mouth. The game, in its currently crippled and bug-riddled state will only be worked on if Zero's "whims" allow. Further, if you purchase the game only to find out that it's unplayable in many ways, don't bother complaining because he absolutely does not care (after all, he already has your money).
Would *you* knowingly purchase something from a person or company which displays such a low opinion of the customer's (absolutely valid) concerns? I didn't think so. Neither would I. Do not support this developer. Such behavior in business should absolutely not be rewarded.
DO NOT BUY THIS GAME!!!
Update (10/11/13): Immediately following the end of the StarDrive front-page sale on Steam, I found myself no longer banned on the forums. While I guess it's a "good" thing that I'm no longer banned, it speaks quite loudly for the theory that the recent aggressive ban-hammer usage was indeed due to the developer not wanting negative forum posts to affect sales (regardless of their validity). In addition, the forums are back to being predominantly full of complaints where as yesterday such threads were being deleted as fast as they could be posted.

Did you like Silent Hill 2?
Do you like fetch quests and point & click adventure games?
No? Then♥♥♥♥♥♥off, 'cause you're gonna hate this game. If you love that stuff, then this is your game of the year right here. And that's your tl;dr.
For those of you that are still here, this game is amazing and more than worth the seemingly hefty fifteen dollar asking price. I mention Silent Hill 2 for a reason, because this game evokes that same concept of partaking in a macabre adventure in an effort to overcome grief and some other spoiler-y emotions, and come to some sense of self-realization. Without spoiling, this is a game where you need to take everything you see with a grain of salt, because it deals very heavily with methaporical imagery and situations.
The writing, probably the cornerstone of every adventure game, is actually childisly simple and frank, but in an endearing way rather than the 'the writer looks up to George Lucas as a role model' kind of way. It's certainly appropriate, considering you're playing a ten-year old girl. Despite being dialogue-heavy, this is one of those cases where there's a lot of showing rather than telling, i.e. the good way to do video game story-telling. To get a firm grasp of the plot. paying attention to the visuals and environment is just as important as actually reading what characters are saying. None of this is to say the characters are poorly written and realized, though; Fran's interactions with her kitty and various other people are charming enough that you'll very quickly warm up to both her and whoever she's talking too.
But to go back to how this game compares to Silent Hill 2, what's the other fundamental pillar of an adventure game? Yeah, get ready for some ♥♥♥♥ing fetch quests. This isn't one of those 'baby's first point-and-click' games that Telltale likes to make so much, where your key to progression is in plain sight and practically begging you to pick it up. Oh no, get ready to wear out you left mouse button as you furiously pound on every object in the game that could conceivably cough up some sort of item.
It's admittedly almost parodic how much characters refuse to help you unless you give them some dumb ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t; the game is hardly subversive in the gameplay department. There's no 'moon logic' at work here, though, as it's never ambigious as to what you're fetching or how you can get it. This might actually let some veteran adventure gamers down, because your tasks are never particularly difficult to fulfill. Still, there's something to be said for how insane some of the fetching can get. There's one point in the game where you need to do four fetch quests in order to complete another fetch quest, which turns out to be the key for another fetch quest. The layers of fetch quest in this portion of the game are insane, and definitely the low point of the experience. Still, it's in the middle, and leads to some of the best portions of the story.
And to wrap up some miscellanious stuff, the artwork is so good that it can easily portray both the grotesque and the cute stuff without either looking too out of place in the game. The art actually reminds me a lot of Broken Age, and as an aside, holy♥♥♥♥♥♥is this the level of imagination and thematic intelligence that Double Fine should've been aiming for with those fat stacks of Kickstarter money, instead of the garbage they actually put out. The music is pretty good for what it is, which is setting up the mood and atmosphere. The sound design is amazing as well, and like Silent Hill 2 (you probably should be taking shots at this point), highlights just how important good sound design can be for games like this. Every drip of water, every creak, every distant moan, and every naseuating squish helps build tension in all the right places.
Oh, and in case you couldn't tell from the screenshots, trailer, or my review, this game isn't for the faint of heart. Don't let the age of the protagonist fool you: there is some seriously ♥♥♥♥ed up♥♥♥♥♥♥here, and I'm not just talking about gore. That's ♥♥♥♥♥ stuff. I won't spill any details, but by Chapter 2 Part II you'll know exactly what I mean.
All this to say, it's a phenomenal game concerned with the heart-breaking exploration of the mind of a broken little girl, but it juxtaposes the gloom and doom with some levity and hope. It's only really hampered with an overreliance on fetch quests, but that's hardly a detriment to people who like this sort of game. If it weren't for the Witcher 3, this would easily be my Game of the Year; as is, it certainly is the Best Indie of the year, and the best in a long time as well.

What is SFV in a nutshell? I'd say it's pure disappointment.
I have played probably every accessible SF title out there and to me, SF 3rd Strike was the pinnacle of 2D fighting games. Seriously, if no other Street Fighter came out, I'd be content with 3rd Strike for the rest of my life.
But then they announced SFIV. I got my hopes up, waited patiently and... Huge turn off. The fancy graphics were a plus. Still, I couldn't bear the clunkiness and lack of the strategic potential 3rd Strike had to offer. After all, I was expecting the next sequel to be only better than the previous. No luck there. I was left with a bad taste in my mouth.
Then came SFV, although I wasn't expecting it. Just like any other silly fighting game enthusiast, I grew hopeful again. I even ignored the online emphasis (which I usually dislike in any game, because I like to play by myself and have a few bouts with a friend every now and then), the whole character unlock system and all those microtransactions. Hell, the game came out half done and I even ignored that. And what did I get? Another whole mess that was even more simplified than its predecessor.
No need to go on and on about it. This game is a huge letdown. I will just go ahead and revisit 3rd Strike, which is still immensely better than V and IV. Too bad I am unable to ask for a refund, because I happened to buy it from a retailer. Money wasted. Enough said.

Only having about half an hour invested into the game there isn't a lot I can say about things in terms of story, but I can say that even at the game's exceptionally low price, I find it hard to recommend to all but the most dedicated hack n' slashers.
Why?
Mostly because the game is rather un-intuitive, and has a very high difficulty curve right off the bat.
It took me restarting 3 times before I realized there was a pile of loot on the floor right at the start (as opposed to starting with it in your inventory? Why?) and without that loot, you're basically screwed from the get-go since punching aliens in the face really isn't a viable option. Once you get past that initial issue you'll run into the second one, which is that the game's aliens deal massive damage, 3 or 4 hits wiping you out even in the starting zone. This wouldn't be so bad if money was more common or upgrades were cheaper, but no: getting any kind of significant armor or stocking up on healing items is an exercise in grinding (non-respawning) that gets old before it even begins, since even with your most powerful starting weapon the most basic enemies take 3-4 hits to take down.
Space Hack isn't all terrible. The interface is simple, controls are responsive, and other than some quirks of being a true 3D semi-isometric hack n' slash (no enemy highlights behind objects, areas where there's just no good camera angle) the game looks fairly nice for its age.
I just wish it were a less punishing experience.
If you're a hardcore hack n' slash player, or looking for a challenge, take a look at Space Hack: for the price, you can't really go wrong. On the other hand, if you're looking for a more easygoing Diablo II-ish experience, pick up a Torchlight game and steer clear of this masochist.

If Starbound was a Simulation game, it would be called "False Promises: The Experience"
At first the game was very promising. It had quite a bit of content to start with, and there was more coming.
Then the promised content got delayed. Then it got delayed again. Any updates we got were just filler to make it look like the game was actually going somewhere. On top of that, those updates constantly killed mods, servers, and save files. I revisited the game recently, and I can safely say that it is not any better than it was when it originally launched, in some ways it's even worse than it was originally.
The game falls under the same problem that a lot of Early Access games have, where the devs say "Hey we aren't going to be like all the other Early Access people, we care about who buys the game and will make a lot of updates!"
In short, they are exactly like those people. Games like Starbound are the exact reason that the Steam refund feature exist. If I could refund the game now, I would do so without any regrets.

You know that key you use all of the time? When you're like looting entire vaults and just about anything? That Use key? Well if you hold it longer than 0.2 seconds you will literally pick up the item and flail the thing around. So in order to loot you have to hit our loot button so awkwardly and stupidly fast so that youre not left flinging a dead roach around instead of getting its meat. The mouse wheel changes your POV and distance but is not listed as a bindable control. Is incorporating weapon switch so hard? I was randomly sprinting at times if I walked over a body (I guess they're slippery?). There's no option to have a toggled ironsights (most games with weapons have this) which I'm used to so do I really want to learn to hold and shoot just for this game? The gameplay and UI that fallout is known for is absent right from the start. When trying to design your character you have to do some awkward Spacebar to Add, E to accept thing even though it appears like it works when you click it. So point being, the gameplay and the feel of this game have blaring faults.
The story? I don't want to spoil anything so I'll just say that one of my favorite parts of fallout was those first few missions based in the vault where you kind of get the feel for the transition from pre to post apocalyptic world. Fallout 4s vault story takes like 10 minutes with no missions, the crucial pip boy is barely noticeable and there is stuff that happens to seemingly significant characters that even Shakespeare would think was over the top. Oh and in a RPG game where dialogue is ever constant, if you hit enter too fast or activate the next part of the dialogue somehow (picking up something, etc.) both dialogues will literally play at once. So even after I'm rushed out of the vault and I try to talk to someone they're literally talking two lines at once and I have to answer like I have any sort of clue what they just said.
All of this could be fixed with some Steam Workshop community mods but I'm not even going to get into the fact that Bethesda charges for community made content along with the nice ol' modern trend of microtransactions and charging people for lavish stuff like functioning use buttons and non awkward customizeable controls. There's literally like 25 bindable buttons in this game people. We are in 2017.
Respect to the devs, I can see some love and labour in this game but it just seems like Bethesda decided to focus on the frivalous parts of the game and not the game itself. You got nice graphics, elaborate opening scenes, a quality studio name in Bethesda and you just put out this stuff and basically sell out the companies good name to people. If you're looking for a quality post apocalyptic game with great gameplay, story and characters I recommend Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas.

MINDNIGHT is a short and addictive secret identity game that will pit 2-3 traitors in a group of 5-8 players. Each game takes about 15 mns
The gameplay itself is simple; each player takes turn to suggest a team for the next mission. Everyone votes to accept or reject the suggestion. Once the mission starts, the hackers can sabotage it, without revealing who it was. They can also choose to let the mission succeed to gain trust among the team, and hack the next mission.
First team to reach 3 points wins. It's as simple as that, but all the exciting bits are in the chat. Agents don't know who to trust, and have to rely on observing how people vote, how they talk, and ask the right questions to see if they can uncover the hackers before it's too late.
Hackers can use the chat to sow discord, throw accusations at other players and play mind games with the Agents.
All and all a fast paced timed game of wits, charm, deduction, logic, accusations and betrayal. Oh and it's free! The only paid options are cosmetic.

Sanctum 2 is a Tower Defense/FPS hybrid game.
1. Choose a private or public match (solo, with friends or/and strangers)
2. Chosse your map. (4 regions, each region have 4 stages).
3. Choose from four unique character (four classes).
4. Choose your weapons (primary and secundary).
5. Choose your perks, (max of three) affecting your caracther, the core, or the gun.
6. Manage your resources (walls and towers).
6.1. Build your maze (You gather new walls each wave).
6.2. Place you towers (You gather scrap each wave).
7. Fight hordes of enemies (various waves).
+ With multiple players monsters become more powerful but also more recourses are avaliable, making the maps more easy.
+ Plays like the best FPS(s), controls are smooth (very important IMO).
+ Monsters show damage taken which is nice.
+ Sound and music suits the game (actually the music is really really good).
+ There are interesting Easter eggs.
+ The chat features Text to Speech (sounds silly, but is amazing).
- In public matches people can hop in and destroy your walls and towers (trolls).
- Sometimes you could find yourself trapped in the environment requiring you to suicide.
- Screenshots make justice, but bould be better optimized. Please turn off the Bloom.
- Some towers are simply sub-par to others.
Sincerally, I'm more excited for Sanctum3 than other blockbusters.

9 months in and a competitive season down, the game feels much more complete than it did at the start. What it was at the start was barebones enough that you could believe it was a demo, but it has certainly put on weight since then.
What we have now is a game with a lot of content behind paywalls (which wasn't that big of a deal when PC players could unlock them through certain means), but at least it has the content. Even at 130+ hours I've still not unlocked most of the earnable stuff via in game fightmoney.
Everytime I close the game it says the exe crashed, but that hasn't proven to be a real problem. I use a x-input fightstick (hori rap v), so I'm lucky enough for it to work natively, but I hear others with ps controllers aren't so lucky. The game has a yet to be resolved ragequitter problem, network wise, playing online with 4+bar opponents has been reliable. Random match making takes a bit of time but it seems to have gotten better since the earlier days.
Gameplay wise, it's street fighter. It feels simplified compared to previous games, but I still enjoy it. How good it really is as an installment in the series is a point of contention for a lot of people, but I trully do have fun playing the game. For anyone who's on the fence, I just can't objectively recommend a full price purchase as money well spente.
I think anyone who loves street fighter and is invested in the series will probably buy it anyway regardless of how much they hate this installment, but everytime I play KoF14 I kinda wonder how much more resources and effort Capcom could have put into making this game so much better.

Sanctum 2: A Review
You might be wondering, why am I reviewing it now, why not 6 months ago, or even when it came out? The simple truth is this. Sanctum 2 has been out for a little more than a year now and in that time the game itself has gone though many changes. So much so that it is hardly the game it was whence it first arrived on the market. Sure it's always been a FPS/tower defence, but in such a different way than when it was first released that a whopping 3 whole days after it's release, the Devs released a patch that set in motion the game you see before you today.
Now, your time is precious, and I understand that, so for those looking for just the short answer to the question: "Should I buy this game?" That answer is, unequivocally, and without a doubt in my mind, wholeheartedly, seriously why haven't you just pushed the add to cart button and checked out already?!?!
For those of you who are of the more discerning...Steam...Steam-inites? Steam-ies? What suffix do we use to classify the people of our wonderful Steam Community? Hmm I wonder... In any case, for those of you wanting to be convinced, there are several reasons why this is the game for you, your mother, your brother's dog, and that pen-pal Geoffrey who you wrote to and exchanged letters with in primary school from Uzbeki-beki-stan-stan, that always said he was going to come visit, but never really had the means to do so; still it was nice to see someone from the other side of the planet and who had just as many gramatical and spelling errors in their writings as third grade you did back in the day. Yeah, remember Geoffrey? Well even though he wont be visiting "Amerika", he probably now plays this game and if you play this game too, the both of you have the option of text to speech chat! Ah yes, you heard me correctly, TEXT. TO. SPEECH. In an almost Stephen Hawking like manner (until you select your character that is), you can wow the masses with literal pronunciations of the written English language which is always good for a laugh, but terrible for poor old Geoffrey who's been desperately trying to learn how to pronounce words that he couldn't learn from his Speak&Spell.
"Ok, so what's so great about that", you ask as you feel so very smug in your smug chair, wearing your smug bathrobe, listening to smug jazz, sipping your imported smugness coffee/tea/caffinated beverage, and occasionally adjusting your monocle...smuggly. Listen here Smuggy, have you ever heard Stephen Hawking sing the theme to the A-Team? No, you haven't? WELL I HAVE. And this game has let me do that, it sounded much like I thought it would if Stephen Hawking were part of the A-Team. "Big deal", you say? Well a little known fact about Stephen Hawking is that he has relatives, that's right, relatives! And whether they're actually related or not there's a player here in our very own Steam Community who goes by the very similar name of Tiger Hawkins.
*(Flashback)*
Long ago, in a galaxy far far away... he very bravely (and without the use of right pinky) fought off hordes of Lumes (the game's monsters) in a Survival challenge set forth by the Developers in Sanctum 1 with the promise of everlasting fame, fortune, and imortalization within their games. Alone on the battle field his war raged on, until finally, he cleared the threshold of damage being able to be dealt and beat the Devs at their own game! (Actually he just survived the most waves out of anyone...ever) He was imortalized in both games just as the Devs had promised, and he lived happily ever after.
*(End Flashback)*
Feel like the game has been out far too long for you to bandwagon onto? Not a chance! With every new Steam sale, a horde of eager beavers, not unlike yourself, flood through the gates of Elysion One Core Guardian training grounds and look like a bunch of fools until someone with a little more knowhow plays a map with you and corrects the error of your ways. To which you feel a little butt-hurt about it and you go off and play single player for a while until you realize that "HOLY CRAP, THIS ISN'T LIKE OTHER FPS GAMES IN WHICH THE ONLINE COMMUNITY IS JUST FULL OF RUDE ASSHATS AND TROLLS, AND THEY WERE JUST TRYING TO HELP ME LEARN!!!!" (*cough* sorry, accidental capslock and whatnot)
Seriously, the co-op community in Sanctum 2 is very quick to come to the defense of someone who is 1.) New. 2.) Under Attack. or 3.) Being yelled by someone who they themselves aren't pulling their own weight.
Want to be UBER L33T 360 NOSCOPE 420BLAZE-IT and go charging in head first, not a care in the world, complete disregard for your own safety for the sake of your own team mates? Go right ahead, so long as you have the right perks equiped. "Wait a minute, there's perks too?" Yes, there are. There are TONS of them, and you get to pick a few per map to help customize your own play style. Don't feel as though you need to be the guy mentioned above as you would rather spend your time building a map so that your towers do all the hard work? Sure, that's possible too! Find that you're at neither extreme and would like to join the rest of us under the Bell-curve? Great, see you there! *high five*
Character skins, DLC maps, guns, perks, DEATH, Sanctum two has it all! But wait, order now in the next immediate time frame and CoffeeStain studios will supersize your order by throwing in their trademark easter eggs! Ever wanted to occupy your character with some rad-arcade-gaming action while you wait for your online friends to decide whether to upgrade this tower over here, or that one over there? BOOM! Wish granted! There are game stations that you can find in game maps that will allow you to play games within the game! Game-ception! (Except that I really hate this trend of adding "ception" to anything that happens within itself. Yes the movie started it all, but the title when way over your heads. Inception, was what it was called because of the plot point of planting the seed of an idea, not because they needed to go 12 billion layers deep! Whatever, Game-ception!)
If that last point hasn't convinced you then there's not so much more I can do to convince you other than letting you know that this game has a super chill soundtrack, significant amounts of replay-ability, and you get to shoot things in the face/back/butt/weakspot, causes you to think and then punishes you for making bad decisions, and when you finally manage to beat it, you enable the Feats of Strength, and relearn every single mechanic the game has with expert precision, timing, and bragging rights per wave when the MVP status is awarded.
Buy the game.
Buy the DLC.
And maybe, just maybe, this wonderful game will reunite you with Geoffrey.

This game was one hell of a pleasant surprise and deserves more recognition!  I got this game in a sale with frankly only minor interest, the only thing that interested me at all was its setting and scenario.  There's something that deeply appeals to me about Hong Kong and its night life and the criminal underworld and let me say right now this game absolutely nails it.  Sleeping Dogs' Hong Kong is intoxicating and while I may not have indulged in any of the criminal stuff (And probably wouldn't...) in real life, I have been to Hong Kong twice and can say that of all the games to present a fictional Hong Kong, Sleeping Dogs has come the closest to representing the atmosphere and life of the city.
As far as the gameplay itself, try and imagine if Grand Theft Auto added in martial arts and focused on melee over gunplay, action movie inspired stunts and physics, and a story that wouldn't feel out of place in a John Woo film.  If you can imagine that, you'd have a good idea of what "Sleeping Dogs" is like.  While it's story isn't anything massively nuanced or even that new to its particular genre, it is told well, has plenty of style, and entertaining characters that keep you immersed in an already engrossing world.
It really is a shame this game didn't do better, I really liked it and if you want a slightly more serious crime game than Saints Row but want something a little more action focused with a more exagurratedstyle than what GTA offers - this game is well worth a look.

A great concept, FPS meets tower defense, in up to four player co-op going against hoards of aliens trying to destroy your precious white orbs that float in the corner. The artistic style in this game is unmatched, particuarly the future city levels, and the comic book style taken between levels. A major advancement of the first, it offers four playable characters, and a fifth DLC, along with a hoast of different map sizes, layouts and routines to challenge even the most competitive and prepared teams.
The level of strategy comes from the types of towers that are placed in the arena, As you level up your character, you unlock new weapons and towers, with each one being more or less useful against the dozen or so different types of enemies. There are a number of modes, but the best action comes from the frantic end stage bosses that leave teams struggling to survive and defend the last of their resources.
The reload mechanic is odd, with no actual ammo being required, rather you just wait or change weapon for stock to reload. Careful balance of shooting, dodging and tower preparation and location are crucial to survival.
A truely unique, enjoyable tower defense game.

With 100+ hours and being around for many of the critical updates I can say this game has never been better than now. Before I tell you the things that make starbound incredible here are some things I dislike;
Touch Damage is annoying and can cause you to lose large amounts of pixels. Luckily a
has been developed for that and it allows for more focus towards building and exploring.
Quests are still a tad tedious, later quests ask for you to find certain structures. This is good as it allows for players to explore new planets and collect loot; the problem is that such structures are not very common and can take a lot of fuel and time to find, sometimes without even containing the quest item.
The frequent changes to crafting recipes for key materials can be annoying but are becoming less frequent as the games nears the end of Beta.
Things that make the game incredibly fun include;
Planets are diverse and filled with mini-biomes and dungeons for you to explore as well as get loot.
Combat although annoying with the new touch damage mechanics can be fun with new special weapon abilities that vary and are fun to explore how each one can be used.
Soundtrack is amazing, only a few tracks can truly be considered "okay".
Endless ways to play, different races along with different armor sets, weapons, planets, etc. provide for countless hours of fun exploring every aspect of the game.
Farming can be fun too.
Building is extremely detailed along with countless building blocks.
Updates are packed with content to keep the game alive.
A bunch of other stuff I forgot to mention.

A decent Diablo clone in space, worth it if you can get it for less than 5USD, in my case I got it as part of a giveaway so I can't really complain, but a few hours in there's two things that make this game a little annoying to play
• Stamina system: for an rpg where you have to walk long distances and sometimes escape from enemies it seems like a pretty bad design choice to include an stamina bar that depletes really fast an only recharges at a barely reasonable rate when you stand completely still. A few times I've had to escape from a horde of aliens only to find that I had to walk away while dodging projectiles at the same time
• Health system: the medkit drop is extremely low, specially for a game where even on easy 3 or 4 hits will kill you, and where monsters are generally organized in clusters
• Ammo/Currency: just like in Metro 2033 you use ammo to pay, this time in the form of energy cells, this forces you to focus at least a bit on melee combat, which is a little complicated considering the two previous limitations I mentioned
If you feel like you want a challenge and you have nothing else to play, and specially if you can get it on a sale, I'd say it's a pretty decent "diablo clone" in space, otherwise I'd advice you to put your money somewhere else.

Ok. I really should have known better.
This game ... Have some issues, lets put it this way.
You start your magical journey, creating YOUR character (picking one random hideous face, out of 4 (from 300+), and one random hideous background (same way). You can change 4 of the images you choosing from (randomly), but "smart interface decisions" are just starting.
You also should pick one of like 20 classes (standard battle types, mages, etc., and even traders, vampires and angels).
I am jumping slightly ahead, but all it changes - one active/passive ability and like + or - 10-20 % to speed of learning particular skill groups (battle, defensive, magick or recovery).
Then you appear in world (like a square) and take small "tutorial", wich shows you main game loop.
It goes like this:
You go to some "region" (by clicking) once or several times. on "global map".
You fight some monster (stat check). (Click auto atack and wait). (If you will try to be "mage" - you just need more clicking)
You collect "loot" - some more clicks.
You manage inventory space and bring "loot" back to town.
You exchange loot from monsters to skill exp.
Rinse and repeat.
On town square (all game is bunch of global square grid) - you click several times to get "quest" - Kill 5 mobs of collect 5 "bear asses", or kill obligatory "boss" of region (meatsponge that hit hard).
You get more exp, when you done.
Of cause there are some equipment options, with depends on you skill levels and wealth.
And there are like 200+ skills...
Good right?
Actually not.
You see - all skills can be leveled in two ways. - Active and passive.
Active - you choose which particular skill to level (lets say parry), and all exp, you get in its dirrectory (defence) goes to this skill.
How do you get the exp?
By "burning" monster loot at "church".
There are monster loot for combat skills (mele / archery / defence / pets).
There are monster loot for magic (white+green / black / blue)
What about crafting skills? Well - you can craft. Theoretically.
Or you can just pick this skill to "passive" leveling.
What passive leveling? You might ask.
Oh, it is qute simple.
You pick one (of 100+) skills, and it just slowly grows each second. Even when you are offline.
How the hell they will ballance that? You may ask (case there are PvP in game).
Oh - very very simple.
Skills do like + 20% to this, or that. At level 100.
And +10% at level 0.
To give you most hilarious (for me) example - skill to "raise up" my "class proficiency".
My class was adventurer.
At level 0 of "class proficiency" I get swooping +3% to all exp I get.
If I will pick this skill to passive leveling, in mere year, or so, (standart geometric progression in exp, required to level up skill with each of it 100+ levels), I will get ... + 6% to all exp.
Neet, right?
Lets talk about biggest "bugbear" I found, and finish with this topic.
Remember how I did say, that there is "merchant" class?
Well - you simply can't sell anything on the auction, if you don't pay devs "monthly".
People said, that later in game I can buy this "pass" with ingame money.
I can. It costs millions (at auction at least).
Why this is a big deal?
Because of "Crafting" part of the game.
You essentially need to create "living production lines", from people, to craft even simplest of thing. And each step will take inventory space and particular skill proficiency.
Example:
You killed first boss and got fishing rod.
You fished some fish (each attempt, after random battle), and want to do something with it.
You can sell it to NPC shop, for like 4 gold.
You can buy a fish skinning dagger and get fish scales, getting + exp in fishing, and then sell them to NPC.
You can use fish to make oil (dont know how though).
You can't sell this to people, that are noobs, case they came to "play for free".
You can't sell this to "old guys", case they dont need stack of 5 fish scales, from starting location.
Your only option - is to sell it to NPC, or just destroy it (case it takes space)
Example №2
You want to craft anything "from other end".
You get any "recipie" - lets say lvl 0 harpoon, from buying it at town, and breaking it apart.
You cant even see materals, needed to produse it, case first you need to do - is to make "working copy" of this "master recipie", which requires you to get pen (NPC sells it), and also ink, and paper. Of course there are different professions, to produse bouth of this, and I dont even know in which city NPC sells "tools", to level them (not in first 2, I can tell you for a fact).
Did I mention, that all this information I got, pestering people is chat, and reading forums, case game does not explaing sh*t?
Only possitive thing I can say - "old" people in chat are super chill and nice, but it is, in no way, a game fault.
Try it "for free", tread with care, and watch for youself.

Doom 3: BFG Edition is a re-release of all Doom-Titles by id Software with some new content.
It uncludes Doom 1 and 2 as well as a new episode called "no rest for the living", which was previously released on XBox. Doom Masterlevels and the Final Doom episodes "Plutonia Experiment" and "TNT Evilution" are not included. The classics haven't been touched, they are still the same fast-pased, burtal fps games we all know and love. The resolution can be set up to full-hd resolutions and they scale up niceley. The new episodes takes advantage of newer hardware (Doom was ment to run an an 486) with more enemies on screen and more detailed level design. It fits nicely into the collection. Sadly, the multiplayer for the classics that is available on the console releases is missig in the pc version. But the wad-files are available and can be used in new ports like Zandorum. Still, they provied a good experience for new and veteran players and is still highly enjoyable for those who enjoy classic first person shooters.
Doom 3 is a reimagining of the first game, but instead of fast action in focuses on slow progress and horror. Also included is the addon "Ressurection of Evil" as well as the new "Lost Missions", which were orignially cut from the game. But Doom 3 is a game that hasn't aged well. Back when it was released the dynamic shadows were new and impressive, but today they are nothing special. They also cannot hide the 2004 low polygon models and low resolution textures, which cannot complete with modern titles by any means and are not reworked. Sadly, most of the High-Def-Mods for Doom 3 don't work with the BFG Edition. Additionally, stuff like demos spawning behind the players and waiting behind doors are getting boring an wear off quiet quickly. Some scenes are still quiet impressive, like when through the right placements of lights a demons' shadow is visible first - but those are far and few. For the most part, Doom 3 is a classic FPS, but way slower than its predecessors.
Given that most of the stuff is still available, I don't think the BFG-Edition is worth its full price if you own already those games, because just the new content is not enough. And the old titles are still available and have tons of mods and makeovers. Especially the missing multiplayer for the classics is a big let down. If you don't own anything, it might be a good start.

Mildly entertaining racing game that gets old really fast.
For a 2009 game the graphics still hold up fairly well, and it performs smoothly at 1920x1080 resolution. It's fun to race and take down opponent cars by slamming them into obstacles, but the experience grows stale too quickly.
The environment is limited to one city so you'll see the same roads and scenery over and over again. The cars all handle pretty similarly so there's not much variety there, either.
Where things get really frustrating is the user friendliness. The game doesn't do a very good job of showing where to go, so you can easily get lost while trying to race ahead of your opponents. Who wants to constantly be looking at the map while driving? It's easy to lose races because of this, and when it happens there's no way to quickly retry. You have to drive all the way back to the beginning, which can sometimes take a good 5 minutes. Given how repetitive this experience is, the game feels torturous and you feel like you are getting punished for not memorizing the city's layout.
There are cars that you can't unlock because the online servers are dead forever, so they're just there to tease you.
There's really not much here to recommend, to be honest.

The artistic style in this game is unmatched, particuarly the future city levels, and the comic book style taken between levels. A major advancement of the first, it offers four playable characters, and a fifth DLC, along with a hoast of different map sizes, layouts and routines to challenge even the most competitive and prepared teams.
The level of strategy comes from the types of towers that are placed in the arena, As you level up your character, you unlock new weapons and towers, with each one being more or less useful against the dozen or so different types of enemies. There are a number of modes, but the best action comes from the frantic end stage bosses that leave teams struggling to survive and defend the last of their resources.
The reload mechanic is odd, with no actual ammo being required, rather you just wait or change weapon for stock to reload. Careful balance of shooting, dodging and tower preparation and location are crucial to survival.
A truely unique, enjoyable tower defense game.

It's so sad seeing a solid fighting game being sacrified for the idiocy of its publisher. I can understand why some people are♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥with this game. It is priced 60$ yet it did not bear enough content at launch to be worth the price tag. While it did deliver the promised content gradually (DLC characters, Challenges, Missions, Story DLC, Versus CPU Mode, In game Shop, DLC stages and stage transitions) it still has some unsolved issues like poor matchmaking, no proper controller support and NO ARCADE MODE! This is a disgrace for a game that was born in the arcades...The matchmaking works random for me. Sometimes it takes less than 30 seconds to find a match but sometimes it takes 30 minutes! Because of that I can't find enough games to rank up! Crossplay between PS4 and PC works buttery smooth! This should become the standard for all future fighting games.
In terms of execution and mechanics, SF5 has gotten a lot easier compared to previous games. Those insane 1 frame links, thunder knuckle cancels and other execution heavy stuff are no more. Therefore, newcomers will get used to the game a lot faster than SF4. Yet, there are still some characters that require execution such as: Urien, Guile, Chun-Li, Ibuki and Juri.
Despite everything, there are many things that this game got right. Variety of lovely old and new characters, stages, music and character themes (dat Guile, Zangief, Nash, Ken theme and etc.).  If you're fan of e-sports, SF5 can still deliver hype matches! Akuma's reveal teaser at Red Bull Battleground was hype AF! In conclusion, I am a Street Fighter fan and I will continue to support this game. If you are a fan of Street Fighter or Fighting games in general, definitely grab this game when it goes on Sale.

I'd heard many of the horror stories and held out on purchasing until I felt like there was enough of a game there to justify the purchase price, and I feel like I can say now that there definitely is.
The game is gorgeous, though not without a few awkward graphical glitches (even when running at MAX settings/full fps), and gameplay is smooth and flows well. The fighting engine is well made and though I feel like it's a bit overly defensive compared to the SF2/SF3:3S meta, it's an understandable reaction to the SFIV:U meta and definitely a step up. The netcode works well and I've had no issues with lag so far online, and the title is pretty consistently active--the crossplay with PS4 definitely helps it from becoming a wasteland like the STEAM version of SFIV:U quickly did.
The biggest issue is the DLC BS. It feels like a full game if you include all the season pass content, but you're paying for a full game for just the incredibly limited "starting" roster. If anything the original game should have cost what the "Season Pass" does and the "Season Pass" cost the same. Or, you know, just sell a full game or don't charge full price, but it's 2016, what you gonna do?
Over all I'd say if you're a Street Fighter fan, go for it, it's definitely Street Fighter and finally feels like a full game if you count all the new characters. If you're not a die-hard, wait for it to go on sale or get it on discount somewhere. I paid less than the retail price of the core game for the whole package and feel like I got a good value, but normal asking price is ridiculous for what is offered. You shouldn't have to pay for two games to get one full game.
As a side note to hardcore fighter players: your arcade sticks won't work on this title still without work, which is ridiculous. Even with an arcade stick with native Windows 10 drivers you'll end up having to use a controller mapping program to fool the game into thinking your stick is an Xbox controller. Thankfully it runs very well once you get one set up, but again, native arcade stick support should be something you expect from a AAA full price fighter so it's a bit ridiculous the burden is on the player to rig some workaround up.

This isn't a GTA clone, nor is it trying to be; it's a dark, realistic, gritty story about a Hong Kong cop who goes undercover as a gang member to take revenge on his sister's death. Sure, you steal cars; the world is open with lots of side-quests and easter eggs; you have a warrant level; you do missions and progress through the story - but this isn't a GTA clone and I can't stress that enough.
The combat system is based on martial arts rather than blazing gunfights, which is very refreshing. Through combos and upgrades (training in the dojo) you unlock new fighting techniques which helps you take on multiple enemies. It's a very fluent combat system, of which GTAIV (amongst others) was lacking. The driving is very smooth and intuitive. The story is compelling and wonderfully written; I find myself justifying horrible actions for the greater cause, as Wei uncovers corruption and hidden agendas.
9/10 - I totally recommend this if you like GTA-style games. The only downsides are that the world is too big to have so little "hidden" content. I've come to expect a certain amount of easter eggs and sidemissions in these types of games, but it only takes the grade down a little bit.

A Mortal Kombat game with a good story, how about that ? This new Mortal Kombat is great fun. The story has a good pacing and lets you play with all your favorite characters. Only downside in the Story mode is the fact that there are no Fatalities. Because of that it sometimes doesn't feel like the Mortal Kombat we all know. But I guess that can be ignored, because otherwise they weren't able to pull off the story anyway. The characters look pretty detailed, especially when damaged and the new X-Ray feature is pure eye candy.
There are plenty of characters, and a whole batch of secret characters as well. Moves are relatively easy to pull off and especially Fatalities are easily performed. Gone are the days of 10-button combos, now it's just 4 or 5. It makes the game fun, not frustrating like older MK titles. Defeating enemies and completing missions will earn you coins which can then be used to unlock outfits and things like artwork and background music. There's more than enough replay value here.
And even though this new Mortal Kombat is already 2 years old, it still is good value for your money.

This is a pretty awesome open world GTA style game. It is beautiful to look at and just great fun to walk around and explore. The missions are diverse and plentiful. The story is compelling and very well written. I really felt connected to the characters and invested in what happened to them. And the entire immense story was topped off by a pretty awesome finale.

There are a lot of vehicles and each one drives very differently.
The combat is great, so much variety and with many ways to beat the hell out of people you won’t get bored. Plus with the ability to learn more skills you will find the fighting even better the further you go. The game also feature contextual take downs, want to slam some guys face into a fan or a window? You can do that and it feels immensely satisfying
There are also tons of side missions to do such as street racing, gambling and a fight club that you will be busy for hours before even delving into the story itself. Plus with all the available DLC and now the definitive edition you will be able to delve even deeper into what Hong Kong has to offer
This version is no longer available but if I would recommend the definitive edition as it contains even more stuff. If you play this game you will have a great time, it is far superior to its spiritual predecessors and a great intro to a new series.

It's an ok game.
The first person fistfighting, which isn't great, is forced prominently into the spotlight. Most painful are the 'trophy' and 'stealth' kills which are very slow. They might look cool before you've seen each for the tenth time time but they also disrupt gameplay and tend to allow for the enemy to gently remind you of their presence with bullets and claw whilst you , ignoring injury,  recite hamlet.
The writing itself is average and i failed to see what was so amazing about bishop from the movies returning (other than the wasted budget). The marine versus android battles in the late game were awful and the three races have this absurd amount of durability to compensate for how slow they are.
There are some things that are good; the multiplayer could be pretty scary if you were playing marine. The sound and atmosphere of some of the earlier levels were of high quality. The AI is better than expected (although worse than what could be hoped for) and some of the fights were both intense and fun. The game just doesn't  feel polished enough and the slower pace of the game doesn't work well in comparison to the faster AVP games from over half a decade ago.
Recomendation: if you want a better AVP game; Try AVP gold or , even better, try 'AVP2'. It was made by monolith, the guys who made the first fear games.

When I was playing on Easy, I wanted to get a lore victory, but won by trade anyway. This time, I was concentrating on gold and I won anyway.

Remember the FPS games of old? Think back to the years of the early '90s (there were other ones in the '70s that were First-person and sort of involved shooting things but thse were arcade-only and didn't really revolve around the First-Person view) people were just checking out this kickass game called Wolfenstein 3D, a game largely credited as the Grandfather to all FPS video games. Wolfenstein 3D was focused mainly on the shooting of nazis (nobody would hate on that) and had revolutionary 3D graphics, kickass themes, etc. After the huge success, id Software created another FPS a year or two after Wolfenstein 3D. That game was DOOM, the FPS, where you are a nameless space marine on Mars battling demons from hell, as well as possessed corpses/marines, and cyborg-demons. It featured a radical soundtrack, impressive graphics (which still hold out to this day) and tight gameplay and action. It was non-stop, balls-to-the-walls action that made the players feel like a badass. After that, id software released DOOM II which still featured the main mechanics that made the original a success. It featured an improved visual, new items and weapons, and a larger soundtrack, yet was not as outstanding or culturally effective as it's predecessor. Then after many years, on August of 2004, DOOM 3 came out. It was more focused on horror and careful strategies then the run-and-gun idea of it's predecessors. It was praised for it's tension-rising atmosphere and horror, yet got negativity and criticism for it's lacking of the run-and-gun mechanic (which many loved about in DOOM 1 & 2). The entire trilogy is well-loved and enjoyed constantly. Hell, people would play this all the time AT WORK. This is the collection of not only DOOM 3 (a remastered version with some things being improved or taken out and improved graphics), and the collection also features the first and second DOOM games! If you want sci-fi horror with action sequences and gun-usage, go to DOOM 3. If you want to run-and-gun and venture through the bowels of hell and return with your life and soul intact while being titled as "the dude that killed all the ♥♥♥♥ing demons on mars and beat the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of some huge demons with cybernetic attachments", then go to DOOM I or DOOM II for that matter. This collection improved on what we loved about the franchise, and allows us to re-immerse ourselves into it all over again.

Mindnight is a game that has really suprised me. It is a very simple game that allows anyone to play, but has a ton of depth for people who are more advanced. Granted these are things you have to find out for yourself. Whether you like a more agressive or passive playstyle, you can play both and still do fairly well. The game, in my opinion, is bettter than Town of Salem in all regards. The game, while having less total content, makes up for it by giving you much more room to experiment by not including a role system. This gives the players the choice of how they want to play. It is also completely based around how good you are at deducing using the little information that you have at your disposal if you're an agent, or how good you are at throwing a wrench into the agents ideals if you're a hacker. It is all about how good you are at spotting inconsistencies, which makes the game much better than towns semi-luck based system. Deffinately one of the best free to play games I've played

EDIT: There is no mod support for this version of Doom 3. If you're into modding, I'd recommend getting the normal Doom 3 on Steam. If not, then snag this version up!
PROS:
- New chapter, The Lost Mission, is difficult and a welcome challenge for those looking for a little more in Doom 3. (Despite some assets being reused)
- Some new graphical changes.
- Plays almost like the old Doom 3
- Shoulder mounted flashlight!
- The Hell Level in the Lost Mission. Quite possibly the most well-done Hell in all three parts of Doom 3. The design honestly reminds me of Doom 2's Hell levels.
CONS:
- Shoulder mounted flashlight is mounted at a seriously weird angle. Always felt like I was leaning the wrong way.
- NO ZOOM (Seriously, where's the zoom keybinding?!)
- Censorship of Doom 2 (Come ooon, that's what MADE the Wolfenstein levels Wolfenstein.)
- Skylines in the skybox for the Hell levels in the Lost Mission. Seriously. I have a screenshot of that laziness.
- No co-op. Yes. This game needs co-op. It deserves it at the very least.
Summary: Great game, and the extra Doom 3 campaign is fun, if not short. If this is your first foray into Doom 3, snag this up. If not, get it for The Lost Mission's Hell levels. It's about as close to Doom 2 as it's ever gotten on that level and the one following it.

This Version of the game has its ups and trade-off compare to the non-BFG edition. On this version you get widescreen support, support for 120hz monitor, Doom 1 and 2. which both are a good games and i highly recommend playing first if your new to the Doom franchiese and play with a keyboard instead of a controller.
The only downside of those two games are if your into story  and having the game tell you why you are there nd why they are attacking you. as you will be disappointed as there is none. Doom 3 trys to throw in the story to exsplain why (mostly through PDA which hides the code to unlock storage containers and some doors).
Resurrection of Evil contenue where Doom 3 left off, and introdues new enemys and weapon from Doom 3. you play as a different character (though you will still be called marine for your un-named character you play as). and have to destory an artifact before the demons get it.
The Lost Mission is levels that where cut from the orginal doom 3 and got brought back on the BFG edition. You play as one of the last remaining survivers from the bravo team and without revealing too much of the story in this review.
The draw back is no mod support and if mods your thing, then this isn't for you. the other downside (or upside depend on how you look at it) is compare to the non BFG edition. your flashlight is strap on to you instead being part of your weapon list and it recharges so you never run out (which is also funny how the Duct tape mod for the orginal is one of most popular mods and it does the same thing minus the recharge).
now does this game worth $20? not really, i would wait till it goes on sell as you are playing a 10+ year old game that been re-re-ported from console (from pc to console as BFG edtion and back to pc as BFG edtion). But if you never played doom or own any previous doom games then get this one as you save $2 compare to buying the games that are included in this edition seprately.

Originally advertised as the next, great addition to the Street Fighter series, SFV has instead delivered nothing but dissapointment. From an extremely lacking launch that left many wondering why they payed $60 for a game that was clearly incomplete, to an online community that discourages new players, SFV is everything that a gamer would describe about a bad game.
From personal expierience, I can say that SFV is clearly a step down from SFIV, which was a praiseworthy, well rounded fighter with an immense cast to choose from, making every online match a new expierience. SFV's extremely short roster encourages repetiveness, and with repition comes boredom, and with boredom comes uninstillation.
I have found myself playing less and less of SFV since its lackluster launch, and only recently decided to try really going hard in ranked online, and quickly found myself trapped in the Silver and Super Silver ranks. What would occur is that unlike SFIV, which rewarded victories and punished losses by an exact calculation of the number of Player and Battle Points one had, SFV does it by your rank, which can have thousands of League Points difference between players. To win three matches and earn 55 LP each, but then to lose 87-97+ after one loss to a Super Silver ranked player, doesn't do well to encourage one to keep playing.
Whomever at Capcom thought it would be fair to reward and punish those with 1500+ difference in points the same clearly didn't understand the types of skill levels present in each Rank. While I tried very hard to enjoy SFV at first, seeing what new features and playstyles I could use with my main, Bison, I came to realize that the game was simply too dumbed down to truly enjoy. It's obvious Capcom hoped to draw in sales with less hardcore gamers by lowering the skill level required to pull off flashy combos and including a plethora of eye candy tier characters, instead of polishing the fantastic game that was SFIV into something greater. I did feel dissapointment when I finally decided I no longer desired to play SFV, but I'm happier knowing that I can genuinely enjoy myself playing SFIV.
Perhaps Capcom should listen to why SFV has 'mixed' reviews next time they want to appeal to a larger audience.

Left 4 Dead 1 & 2 Reviews
Both of the Left 4 Dead games are great examples of what the zombie survival genre is like. Two of the greatest zombie games created. Although some time has passed since their original release dates, Left 4 Dead (2008) and Left 4 Dead 2 (2009), they are both high quality survival games. One flaw with both games is the sheer repetitiveness. There are several different campaigns in both games, but in Left 4 Dead, the outcome always seems the same: Wait for someone to rescue you. Although Left 4 Dead 2 has more to do, it always seems the same. However you can find yourself playing the campaigns several times, playing survival mode countless hours and killing thousands of zombies as soon as you pick up a copy. Since they were made nearly five and six years ago, the graphics are no longer considered high quality, but are in no way an eye-sore. Both Left 4 Dead 1 and 2 have a great replay value, and are easy to learn, making them fun and exciting games.
Both games feature four players whether it is offline or online with a common goal in mind. Keep moving, kill everything that moves, and get to the next safehouse or escape route. The weapons are fairly simple, in Left 4 Dead there are assault rifles, snipers, shotguns, pistols and submachine guns, whereas Left 4 Dead 2 has all the same, plus a variety of melee weapons. The stories of both games are fairly simple but overlooked, you will find yourself being more interested in killing hordes of zombies rather than who is on their way to save you.
Personally I would like a third game to be made, just like every other L4D fan, including fellow editor Wilson2234 who has logged in more than 22 hundred hours into these games on Steam. I myself have played both versions on Xbox 360 and PC and have to say they run well on both and are a great purchase on either system. Perfect game to play with friends to either waste some time, or play on Expert and strategize how to make it out alive.
Overall Left 4 Dead 1 & 2 are two of the greatest survival games on the market. My Rating 8/10

TLDR: Clever use of simple design, creature building is incredibly fun and hilarious, crafting/farming a bit minimal, but fun already so the future looks bright.
11/19/16 Dev Wishlist Update (may or may not be implemented at the time of this writing):
- Ability to pause the single player game. Esc goes to the options screen, but all continues to happen in the background
- Map feature
- Mining/Digging
- Armor Crafting
- A larger selection of weapons (I know that the creature you build can take the brunt of the combat, but a bit more ability to defend yourself wouldn't hurt this)
- A few more options in house building: alternate construction materials, some static defenses (spikes, etc.), and some eye candy never hurt
Understand: I know this is not 7 Days to Die. It's 7 Days to CHKN.
Did I just use CHKN as a verb? Maybe.
Maybe.
A few clicks of a few screenshots or a quick view of of a youtube clip will tell you what you probably already suspect and what many beautiful and brilliant gamers have already indicated: Minecraft and Spore had a baby. An adorable, engaging baby with a mean, unforgiveable streak. Let that sentence settle for a bit, I'll wait over here.
Part survival game, part God game, part gotta-catch-em-all game, CHKN drops you on a beach surrounded by fruit. Near you are a couple eggs that you can either leave alone (for some reason), or crack open and scoop up (what looks like) a toppled bucket of Mr. Potato Head: Kentucky Fried Chicken Edition parts. With any of these in hand, point it at the sky, click, and assemble your first friend/pet/protector.
Feed it melons or squash, just like any new chicken beast. And seek others. Others to subvert, assemble, eat, or any of the above in any order you like. The parts I have thusfar discovered are (in no order of discovery or assembly): Pigs, llamas, dragons, cows, beetles, tarantulas (SCREAMLOL), sheep, giraffes, elephants, goats, alligators, cranky hooded jerks with dart guns and two-legged robo-lizards, and, of course, chickens.
There are several harvestable resources - nothing surprising or new there. Though, of course, there really need not be. The craftable side of things is simple and fun, though it is the lesser part of the game, or at least what I have seen so far seems to indicate this. Again, the standard constructs of stone, wood, and iron apply, but I think this may be intentional as it is more fun to build a chicken-legged, goat-lipped, elephant-tusked beetle-sheep than a porch.
...I re-read the above and it seems a bit unfair. Let me rephrase: the house/tool/weapon crafting side of things is simpler than the beast-building aspect, but it is not lacking at all. There.
I have only found three types of non-beast made food: Melons, squash, and apples. The first two you can find in the wild and then plant their seeds in the ground with a hoe, the other drops from apple trees, (from which you can harvest seeds and plant in the ground with a hoe). All of these you can feed to herbivores to keep them fat and happy. This seems minimal, but it does not truly detract from the game.
I think that will do for now. Come, chicken-legged, goat-lipped, elephant-tusked beetle-sheep. We have much to do.

I've managed a little over 10 hours on this game so far. I’ve won with every clan to date multiple ways. I like the early release content but I am not satisfied with how much I paid for it.
PROS:
•	I like the unique idea of not being able to build all your buildings in one central location. It forces you to expand and explore. It also makes you strategize as to where you gather resources, fame, and happiness. This also means you cannot fortify but neither can the enemy.
•	Wildlife. I like the idea of wildlife blocking expansion or causing issues from areas you can’t see as they roam into your territory. Also, the interactions with the giants, the dragon, and the gate. I’d like to see more of this.
•	Stone. If you’re not expanding, you run into issues quick maintaining a working economy. Stone helps by allowing you to upgrade your buildings. However, because stone is a limited resource, it forces you to think strategically, or buy a market. While I’d like to see more stone on a map, I like the idea of limited resources. I definitely wouldn’t limit stone any more than it is though.
MEH:
•	Multiclan selection. Nothing substantial changes between clans. This is true with most RTS games apart from visual differences. This game lack visual differences. There are some perks with each clan but not as substantial as I would like. Visual differences would improve this greatly.
•	Metal. Metal is essential for upgrading units once, but that’s all it’s good for. I would like to see either a second upgrade, or some other use for metal like tower upgrades since you can only have 1 per plot.
•	Healers. You must be on your own land to be healed. What I would like to see is limited range of healers instead. This allows forward bases to become more relevant. Placing a tower and a healer hut, expanding the range of healing to nonconverted lands. This may not be a decent fix however because fully upgraded healers, lore, huts, and 3 healers can do serious healing through damage. The reason this is most troublesome is with explorers. They are not healed when they take damage from exploring. You must rotate them out, or have them stay put for a period which means you must pay attention to them.
•	Fame. It’s only relevant until you get to 500 but you can win with fame. I’d like to see more rewards, even minor ones, going up to 1,000.
CONS:
•	The maps are relatively small. Expansion quickly becomes problematic because everyone must expand. This means quick skirmishes to fight over resources early. Especially if you run into wildlife issues. I would like to see more wildlife on larger maps. Not so large it becomes difficult to win by domination but perhaps a map size editor added to single and multiplayer options in the future. I feel this is a con because your starting point becomes so important. Even on easy, maintaining an economy seems more to do with how many troops you need, and how quickly.
•	As of right now, there are still bugs. The map can get this crystalloid (it looks like a crystal shooting off rays) bug that blocks the view of the map and gets worse the longer you play. I don’t know what triggers it but you must save and load the game to get rid of it.
•	No campaign. No multiplier. ‘nouf said.
•	It’s too easy. Single player does not take long. If the enemy is in a great location with plenty of resources, you’ll probably lose quickly from lore, trade, or fame. However, if you get a great location, the game is over in about an hour. I think the overall difficulty of winning, other than by domination, should be harder.
Because of a lack of campaign content, lack of visual differences and adequate lore differences, bugs, inability to alter map sizes, resources that become obsolete, and healer mechanics. I’d rate this game 2 of 5 stars for early release. Subtle changes could improve this substantially.  However, I am excited to see the full extent of this game. I hoping for a long and generous campaign for every clan with objectives focusing on their strengths. An ability to change map size. Fixing the bugs. Even larger lore differences, or visual differences. This game could be well worth it’s money.
