Doom is one of the most famous FPS games of all time. Hell I used to play Doom back on a Windows 3.11 system using a bootup disk to load the game in HighMem. That and editing the modems ATT dial up script for a low latency connection to play Coop with friends. Oh those were the days. Well lets get back to Doom 3!
Doom 3 BFG Edition, upgrades to the graphics (somewhat) and it now includes a flashlight on the guns. Before you used to have to download the flashlight mod otherwise you would have to switch back and forth from gun to flashlight. I was really eager to get this game on Steam when it was announced.
The starting to the game really sets the stage for a dark and eerie game. You arrive on Mars as a new recruit and have to make your way to the commander where he sends you on a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t mission to get some scientist, why? Well because your the newbie soldier (kinda like in real life, trust me I speak from experience). This is all a good lead in for whats to come.
There is always something to over hear with when listing to the other soldiers converse or the maintenance guys talking about whats going on and there speculations of whats its all about.
While playing you will come across some audio logs, PDA's and locked cargo containers. Listening to the PDA's audio logs and reading the emails on them will get you the access codes for the lockers as well as the locked rooms you will come across with all that awesome weaponry!
One of the PDA's will tell you to go to a website (you do this in a web browser outside of game, at the time this was an interesting idea but these days there are integrated web browsers in game or something similar) like
! Unfortunately that website is no longer running. If you want to see what the website was like there is
that has it archived so at least you will get to see what everyone else did when Doom 3 was originally released in 2004. There is another website but I don't recall the address for it anymore.
The game itself plays just like it always did. Running and gunning at times, hunting for ammo, health and armor boosts. The music and sounds to the game that give it its eerie feel and scares you when playing at night in the dark was done by Nine Inch Nails.
I played the game with a keyboard and mouse originally but the BFG edition I play with an Xbox360 controller and it plays very well. The game was also made to accommodate the controller without any issues.
I have to say that the BFG edition was defiantly worth the price and even more so when you get it on a sale because it includes all the Doom games and the Doom 3 expansion as well.
The biggest disappointment for me was that the Doom 1 and Doom 2 games that are included don't have Coop play option like they did when originally released. I really don't understand why Id Software decided not to include this option of play as it was one of the best things about the Doom games! Being able to play together with a friend and beating the game was so much fun and you could set it on the higher difficulty settings and play the whole night.
I give this game 4 stars because for everything it has it should have had Coop as well but was taken out for some reason.

Coming from someone who loves these creepy point and click adventures, I definitely recommend this game! The game holds a very creepy dreamlike atmosphere and doesn't use the basic jump scare tatic to keep it unsettling. I will say certain parts of the game are a little cliche, i.e: insane asylum,creepy little girl, shadow monsters. But it also introduces very interesting "creatures", and game mechanics that help separate it from others. The pill mechanic being one of the more prominent mechanics, allows the player to see the game in two different perspectives. The game is also very linear, when given a choice in a conversation it will usually give you the same "ending" without much diversity, with the exception of a couple. But I don't feel that really detracted me when playing the game. The campaign takes about 5-7 hours long to complete and it took me about 10 to get 100% complete. That being said I recommend getting the game while it's on sale as they are asking $15 bucks for the game.

I would really like to reccomend this game...
The sense of scale is AMAZING. Going from tiny tanks in the begining of a match, to playing interstellar baseball with moons  near the end. In consept, this is an awesome idea for an RTS. Admitingly, it was super fun crushing my enemies with huge lasers.
However, the game has several flaws that make it frustrating to play: pathfinding, balance, camera and preformance
When I played Supreme Commander 2, one of my prefered RTS's, I loved to amass huge armies, and with proper unit diversity and placement, wipe out a whole base. One of PATs units, the nanobots, were probably made for such tactics. The problem of pathfinding then makes units and armies like this useless, because only two hunderd of your four thousand nano-swarm made it to their target because the rest are suck on the scenery with their fingers up their nano asses. I threw two games because I was to frustrated too make more.
The balance was also lackluster. The only units that can be interplanetary are orbital or land, and the only ones that can target orbital units were other orbital units with the exception of a handfull of land units. This really leaves air to be used early game for their speed, and almost never use any naval units, because they can only travel in either open and empty waters, or tiny lakes. Not to mention that most planets don't have any water.
The camera was almost one of the more tollerable parts, but still had issues. Because planets are round, you won't ever be able to see everything on the screen. You'll have to be constatly be poping around the system trying to get where you want to be. Sure, you can save several views so you can pop back to them, but you can onlt have so many, and works not nearly as well as it should, and makes it rather nausiating when your constantly changing angles.
The last problem I had was preformance. When I had large amounts of units, the game became frequent to crashing. Luckly, the game had a reconnect feature for when you crash, but makes me think that rather then fix the issue, they added the function for you to reconnect and inevitably crash again.
Summed up, I love the scale of the game, but doesn't quite focus on aspects that make a good RTS in my opinion. Also, not a ton of people are talking about the modding community in their reviews, which was one of the best parts of the game. Each one added a new level of complexity, and some changed how you played

Another entry in the booming "4x Space Strategy" genre being populated by both established development teams and indies, StarDrive comes to the table burdened by a negative reputation but with more than a few strengths in its corner.
No one will deny that StarDrive was released way too early to the public. It was buggy, incomplete, and, as a result, it entirely deserved the low scores it received.
Since release, however, the developers have worked hard to plug the holes and fill the gaps. The game is now, especially on sale, one that I would recommend to anyone who enjoys this genre.
The strongest differentiator that sets StarDrive apart from competitors is the ship design. While some games allow you to choose your ship's weapons or shields, in StarDrive you build a ship from an empty hull to a bristling space cruiser. You select exactly where you want bulkheads, power plants, command centers, weapon banks, and sheild generators to be placed. As the research tree fills in, you'll open up even more opportunities to build new, larger hulls or moditfy your existing blueprints.
Another area I enjoyed in StarDrive was the factions. Each faction is extremely unique in design and carries with it a lot of flavor. Whether your negotiating with the honorable but militant pandas or the robotic faction that's enslaved a race of owls - you'll find interactions to be a lot more interesting than the sterile diplomacy of many other games in this genre.
In the end, StarDrive is exactly what it sets out to be: a 4x Space Strategy game with a robust ship builder and real time combat. If that sounds like it's up your alley, then I think you won't be dissapointed.

I love driving back and forth along streets to try and beat the preset record. And I love crash animations, even if they do get a little tiring sometimes.
If you love racing games, you will love this game. It has something for everyone. Just do yourself a favor and buy it.

The game is still getting updates, but it's hard to justify a fullpricetag.

I'm only recommending this if you have played L4D2 already, if you haven't played/bought that, please buy L4D2 rather than L4D1 since they cost the same amount anyway.
Anyway, ever since when the campaigns from L4D1 got ported to L4D2, this game got more and more less played. For a reason, it's more enjoyable though to play a single game as a party with campaigns from two games, rather than always switch between 2 games if you want to play different campaigns.
Campaigns itself and the whole scenario in L4D1 are better though, probably they aren't really that much different from what they are in L4D2 though to some people, so in case if you don't already see any difference between them yourself, you should just stick to the sequel.
The versus game on this one has more idea than in L4D2, since on L4D2 you just run to the safe room and that's it, with this you all have to maintain your health as good too rather than crawl to the safe room as a group.
Still, with that there's the one problem you would notice if you have played both games, there's half of the special infected that you can use in versus since there are more added zombies in the sequel. It's kind of like a preference if you don't like Chargers, Jockeys or Spitters, but I would find 2 Hunters, Smokers or Boomers a bit unfair altogether.
There are some things that you might miss from L4D2, like special weapons or throwables, or even some of the gamemodes. Making mostly only the Campaigns the core of this game, which it mostly is though of course. I don't think you would be able to get more than 4 people to get to play this in these days anyway now.
This is still a great game though, but I don't see any reason to spend money on this for the story, since as said, all the same campaigns are already in L4D2. There's even more story between The Sacrifice and The Passing than almost at any other part of the game and those both campaigns were added to L4D2 in the first place too.
Only thing that this has what L4D2 doesn't, is a one survival map. So if you're dying to get that, feel free to spend 20€ to get that rather than to search a custom map file for it somewhere for L4D2.

I just finished the game, so all of this is kind of a recent pile of thoughts.
The story:
Wei Shen, an undercover cop has to get into the Sun On Yee, one of the triads in Hong Kong. Old friends, new friends, lovers, enemies, and bitterness is what follows his mission to the very end, which is one of the greates cliamxes in any games I've ever played so far. It's like a really awesome TV series coming to a satisfying end.
The base of the story is a dolig one, which we could see a hundred, maybe a thousand times. But man...they did a wonderful job for making it work better than anything else that follows the same path. You'll feel the friends in the game are truly your friends - and their betrayal will hurt you even more. You'll find yourself cheering when something turns out great, and feel anger you never thought you could ever feel. While you don't have much choices storylinewise, the one you get will be usually the best. You'll kill when you need, but feel guilty for it, when you did not. And what makes it all possible?
The characters. Wei Shen is a really great protagonist for a game like this. A cop, who has lots of friends from his childhood in the triads, but his supervisor gives him the orders. You'll feel the weight of the things he has to go through, and you'll even feel sorry for him some times. And thus, the payoff will be the better because all of this. Then you have people who knew Wei from his childhood. Jackie, who appears to be the comedic sidekick, but he is indeed much more. A loyal friend, a brother in arms who'll be by your side every time. Then there's Winston, the Red Pole (triad rank), who was first a bit skeptical about you, but he'll become a good friend too. You'll understand him, and you'll ultimately feel sorry for him. And that was just two of the many great and memorable characters from the game.
The writing is really good. It's logical, the interactions between the characters are genuine, you know that it was written by someone who can create good characters, and instead of making them do what needs to be done, he or she just creates them, puts them into Hong Kong, and watch what do they do. There are fillers in the discussions between the characters, but they feel anything but forced. They are chatting, enjoying themselves, nothing serious. Just what you'd do if you were roaming the city with your best friend riding shotgun.
Overall the story, characters, game concept, and writing gets a 10/10 - really enjoyable, and I'm sure even folks who are not into the moral dilemmas of being an undercover cop will find the game interesting.
Gameplay:
It follows the road GTA has set up (or at least as far as I know, but it could happen that it wasn't the first game like this), third person view, open world, sandbox feeling, etc. If you played any GTA games, from III to V, you are familiar with the concept. But instead of guns, the emphasis is more on the fistfights. Wei can learn tons of new moves, each associated with a "reputation tree", one for the Triads, one for the Police, and the third for your old martial arts master, Sifu. You get experience in each mission for both factions, depending on your accomplishments - if you didn't break anything, and didn't kill or hurt any civilians, you get more Police XP, while killing more enemies, especially with enviromental kills will reward you more Triad xp. For Sifu, you need to find his jade statues, and he'll teach you a new move for every one of them.
The melee system is not too complicated. You have a bunch of combos, and about four buttons to use. It's like the melee system of Batman, but without the gadgets, and with more brutal fightning moves. Roundkicks, breaking arms and legs, throwing them off a building, you get everything you need. I mentioned enviromental kills, which need some explaining, I'm afraid. When you grab an enemy, you can see some items with blinking red lights. You can perform enviromental kills on them, like throwing the poor guy on a bunch of swordfish heads, or roasting his head on an oven.
Even tho there aren't as much emphasis on the guns, they are still present. They aren't too many of them, but they are a great deal of fun. You can use covers, and go all John Woo on your enemies' asses. Slow down time, jump through tables, and earn more time slowing for shooting them in the head. Firefights will play like an action movie, such a shame there aren't a bit more of them in the game. Most of the big turning points of the game involve a lot of guns and enemies, which will make the blood run faster in your veins.
The open world is wonderful. I've never been to Hong Kong, and haven't seen too much pictures of it, but if it looks like this, then hot damn, what an awesome city. It looks really good. And with all the people going aroudn, doing their daily routine, it becomes even better. In the daytime the streets are crowded, while the night is relatively quiet, and only a few people are running around. And most of them belong to one or another gang, so be careful.
There are lots of hidden, or not so hidden altars around the city. Pray at them, and for every 5th you visit, your health will increase a bit. A great fun, and they feel the part of the city.
Also, there are a lot of minigames, which I haven't discovered in their entirety. You can race with cars, bet on chicken fights, play mahjonng poker, etcetera etcetera. They are worth checking out, and maybe you'll find them as engaging as the main game and storyline itself.
Overall, for gameplay, I'd give a 9/10 - only because I'm sure there are mistakes here and there, but it's so recent i'm still under the effect of the game.
Graphics:
I don't want to talk about this as much as the other parts, as I don't really watch the graphics of the game. It's in harmony with the other parts of the game, and this is awesome. The characters' animations are great, you can spot really lifelike impressions on them.
Let's say non-rated/10, I haven't got the hardware to see it's full potential.
Sounds:
Various radio stations in the cars, and great enviromental sounds when you are not in a vehicle. Both of them are good, and I'm sure everybody will find a radio station he likes. From techno, to J-pop, from classical to death metal. They got your taste covered.
10/10
Multiplayer/co-op:
Non-existent, you can only see if in specific areas you did better than your friends or not. Longest time driven without accidents, and so forth. I don't think that's necessary, but could have been a welcomed addition to the game.
Overall? I'd give this game a
. A joy to play, and I didn't get frustrated at any part on normal. It was a fluid game, that really worth my money. I got it on a sale, but if you don't want to wait to try it, get it for the full price - you won't regret it. Many hours of fun, with minigames, side missions, or just plain exploring.

Even for 2005, this is far from a decent game. Action RPGs can already be a really dull and boring genre without any interesting aspects thrown in. Space Hack adds nothing, and what it does attempt is so underwhelming that it gives the player absolutely no reason to keep going through all of its mediocrity.
The plot is as uninspired as you can imagine. It's as if the developers were being forced at gunpoint to add a story to this game. The graphics are cheap looking and boring, as the game world and alien design are far too generic and bland for a game that came out in 2005. The sounds and special effects are terrible, and you will feel like muting the game after the first few hours. The music is probably the best part of the game, as it does provide a moody and atmospheric backdrop to what is being attempted onscreen. As for the gameplay itself, there is barely any action and barely any role playing elements here. What is there feels almost like a placeholder for something that was underdeveloped and not thought of for very long. The repetitive clicking stereotype of the action RPG genre is here, but even further stripped away of special abilities and different classes. In order to perform more than the normal attack, you will need to manually select the ability from another menu and right click if you want to use it. This limits the gameplay even more than what you should come to expect from the average action RPG game. Everything about Space Hack is so low quality, so boring, and so dull, that there is no reason at all to play it if you have access to the better action RPG games available. There is nothing redeeming and nothing interesting to be experienced in this game. The entire playthrough feels like a complete waste of time. In addition to all this, the game is also prone to crashing and suffers from extremely low frame rates.

With 100+ hours and being around for many of the critical updates I can say this game has never been better than now. Before I tell you the things that make starbound incredible here are some things I dislike;
Touch Damage is annoying and can cause you to lose large amounts of pixels. Luckily a
has been developed for that and it allows for more focus towards building and exploring.

Things that make the game incredibly fun include;
Planets are diverse and filled with mini-biomes and dungeons for you to explore as well as get loot.

Soundtrack is amazing, only a few tracks can truly be considered "okay".
Endless ways to play, different races along with different armor sets, weapons, planets, etc. provide for countless hours of fun exploring every aspect of the game.
Farming can be fun too.
Building is extremely detailed along with countless building blocks.
Updates are packed with content to keep the game alive.
A bunch of other stuff I forgot to mention.

The Binding of Isaac is on it's surface a rather childish narrative of poop jokes and weird body horror, but upon further reflection and piecing together of the non-linear story, one comes to realize that Isaac is a wholly unique, fairly depressing, and highly important narrative. Isaac is a child with everything stripped from him, his ability to choose, his ability to move around, his very humanity is offered up in the name of sacrifice. But unlike so many other narratives about child abuse, Isaac is a game that does not end with a child falling to the knife of his authoritative figures, but rather making his own choices, whether to live or to die.
Isaac's struggles are given serious attention even amidst all the giant poop monsters, and I truly believe this game can absolutely be a cathartic experience to some of us out there who maybe didn't always have the chance to make our own fight in life.

MINDNIGHT is a game in the vein of 'Mafia' and 'Werewolf,' with a group of players attempting to secure nodes for the 'Agents' while trying to deduce which players are the 'Hackers' to stop them from hacking the nodes. There are five nodes, and first to secure/hack three wins.
The game has a very strong foundation to go off, emulating the 'hidden killer' style of table-top games, but I feel it's a little too simplified to function properly 100% of the time. There's very often that you'll end up in a game that really comes down to a coin toss about who is/isn't a hacker, and for me at least that's not very fun.
From my experience most games played out extremely similar in the early game, with around 98% of games having the first two nodes secured and hacked in the exact same manner. I feel there needs to be more ways to gather info than simply the votes and who was/was not in any given node as, like mentioned above, this is a very fast way for games to end up as a coin toss.
Over-all fun for the short while I played it, and I'll 100% be keeping my eye on it for interesting updates.

I usually don't bother writing reviews, but Fran Bow delivers one of the stronger experiences you can get out of a game.
Gameplay-wise, it is a well written point and click adventure with puzzles that are reasonably challenging, but not to the point you will get stuck often. The music and audio work well to set up the atmosphere, and the graphics have a peculiar character and beauty. The puzzles, audio and, especially, the visuals, are good, although they don't reach the heights of modern masterpieces, such as Machinarium. However, one should consider that this game was actually made by two people and it does illustrate what indie game developers can do.
These factors alone would make a good game, but Fran Bow stands out in two ways. First, it introduces a unique mechanic which consists of visiting alternate realities or seasons which are crucial to the puzzle solutions: In one chapter Fran can move through time by controlling the seasons, while in another three chapters she can move between what might be called a waking world and a world of shadows, the latter being a dark and haunting place where a dinning table full of candy can be replaced by mutilated bodies.
Second, and most important, Fran Bow's story and atmosphere is like a slightly more coherent Alice in Wonderland, but darker, scarier, twisted, and occasionally more dreamlike and touching, where the limits between reality and hallucination are blurred. It is set in a surprisingly rich world with five realities, peculiar creatures and places, and even a made up alphabet which you can decipher thanks to an in-game book. It easy to get engulfed in the story and share Fran's fears, sorrows, and hopes.
This is an experience you will remember for a lifetime.

This is a postive review, if you wish to know about the game, read on, if not, just know that its' a great game, and the only problem I have with it is that it's too short.
For the rest of you:
Pros:
1) This game has an amazing story that really draws you in.  You speculate what's going on, why you are in this world, and what really happening.  It honestly kept me on my mental toes the entire time.
2) The horror and thriller side of the game is definitely there.  It makes the player feel that in this world, bad things are going to happen, and they usually do.
3) The controls are easy (as to expect by a point and click game), but I honestly didn't feel that they got old or overused.  It was a great choice for a game like this.
4) The music and voices (when there are some) are definitely on point.  I found myself being more aware of my souroundings whenever weird music or noises would appear.  It really puts the player in the world.
5?)Cats are cute :D
Cons:
I only have three problems with the game.
1) I thought it was too short.  I wanted more of the story.  More things to click on and maybe even more interaction with characters.  It had an awesome world, and I don't feel that there was enough in it to fill it.
2) Some of the puzzles were actually too hard for me.  I had to end up looking up guides online just to find something I didn't click on that was totally obscure or to find out the my ideas weren't working even though it seemed like they would (common sense stuff).
3) With that in mind, I think there should have been a "Choices matter" system that way the player could feel more in control of our creations and consequences.  At times it felt linear, "do this puzzle, get this whatever".  If they added in different endings or different choices/consequences, it would have really addded depth to this already great world.
With all of that said, I give this game a strong 7/10.  I would definitely play it again, and my friends loved watching me play this as well.  I just wish there was more to find out!

This is a very fascinating yet horrific game. It takes inspiration from Alice in Wonderland and twists it with horror aspects and gore to paint a terrifyingly beautiful picture. You play as a little girl named Fran Bow, who is trapped in a mental asylum after the brutal death of her parents. Your only goal is to escape and find your pet kitty Mr. Midnight. The question is how to do it... and figuring out the meaning of seeing things no-one else can see. Let's just say you need to take the red pill every once in a while.
The story from what I've gathered after three straight hours of play thus far is fairly simplistic, almost like a children's fairytale... albeit a fairytale definitely made for adults and NOT kids (seriously do NOT buy this game for your kids! Despite its cutesy artstyle there is a ton of disturbing/bloody/gory imagery throughout that can be very frightening.)
Some of my favorite aspects of the game are the little nods to various old school games found within minigames played throughout the point and click tale. There's a maze minigame similar to Pac-Man, a river crossing game that's basically a repaint of Frogger, and a few others I have yet to see. As the game is a point and click adventure there is no customization or RPG style elements aside from collecting various items and combining them in various ways to help you throughout your journey.
What truly makes this game unique is the mix of disturbing gore and story elements with the adorable, storybook artstyle. The result is a beautiful game with tons of little details that require a couple playthroughs or so to understand everything. However once clues are pieced together you'll find yourself going "Ah-hah!" and even getting surprised at some of the twists and turns.
Then there's the truly disturbing parts; the blood, gore, and the true fate of the children in the asylum. Many of the children housed there have very sad, very creepy backstories which can be discovered by using the red pills to see the true insanity beneath the surface. Sometimes the results can be nauseating to say the least. This is a game that doesn't pull punches with the gore though what makes it frightening is how it makes you think. The fear in this game is all psychological - which is quite fitting considering the setting.
Overall this is a game that I recommend to both horror fans and those looking for something a little different from the norm. I'm not sure if it is worth the $15 price tag, but the art is a definite selling point as is the detailed story. Give it a try, and always be aware that YOU CAN SEE.

Forget what anyone says about this game being a GTA clone.
Sleeping Dogs perfectly performs free-roam gameplay by making the environment extremely interactive and scattering collectibles and things to do all around the map. The side missions are plentiful and enjoyable, and the story missions are incredibly interesting.
The story itself puts you in the role of an undercover cop, Wei Shen, working with the Hong Kong PD and disguised as a Triad to help uncover the Sun On Yee and take out their leaders. Throughout the game, you work under both an official officer role, busting criminals and staking out crimes, and as a Triad, extorting shops and business and running protection rackets throughout Hong Kong. The story itself is well-done for an Eidos game, and will keep you entertained and wanting to play.
The gameplay itself and the combat is phenomenal. The melee combat is a very fluid, addicting system, allowing the player to chain together light and heavy punches and kicks to make deadly combos. Additionally, the game allows you to grapple foes and tackle them against objects for environmental kills, making for fun, deadly killcams. The gunplay on foot is standard, but good, however, the gunplay in vehicles is incredible. Shooting at enemy tires nets incredible killcams while in vehicles, and the play is smooth and solid.
Graphics are very nice for when this game was made, but nothing INCREDIBLE. Easy on the eyes.
My only qualm with this game is the awkward controls. The phone works very oddly, and requires you to uncomfortably press backspackes/up and down arrows. Equipping melee weapons and holstering guns also requires the use of arrows keys. Along with the awkwardness of driving at times, it can really clutter up. Nothing gamebreaking, just a nusiance.
Overall, this game is a solid 9/10, if not 9.5. The gameplay is phenomenal, solid story, and plenty of content. An addition of multiplayer and fixed controls could easily make it one of the best games of all time, in my opinion.

In short, Sleeping Dogs is the best gta sandbox style game I've ever played.
Pros
- Great melee/ranged combat
- More graphical detail in city life and night city life, than in any other game out there.
- A lot of things to do besides the main story missions.

There are more pros I could list, but the above sum it up pretty up well.
Cons
-Occasional camera glitches while driving, nothing game breaking. I don't know why, but IGN gave this game an 8.5 simply because of the camera glitch while driving (sometimes).
- The combat, while being as interesting and immersive as it is, is a bit too easy a lot of the time. You can take on and beat 20 guys easily if you played the game for atleast 5h.
- There could be more 'dating' related missions. (This is probably the perv me complaining, rather than a 'con', but I found those to be fun and I would like more of them).
- The cops are too easy to escape.
- If you don't get immersed and don't like meleeing guys all the time like I do. You may find the game repetitive sometimes, although not while doing the story missions.
These cons  are more complains than cons, but I did not want to simply write that this is the perfect game in my review.
Anyway, I recommend this game, for anyone who is thinking about getting it.

If you're a fan of the original AvP and AvP2 on the Monolith Engine, then you will love this remake. The game sports the same episodic style based on the three races, telling the same story but from different perspectives. This is what made the original AvP2 such a good game, and it works quite well for this game. The game controls much like the original, but with many improvements, and the graphics hold up quite well even by today's standards (its a 2010 game and we're in 2014, but a lot has change in video game graphics in 4 years).
If there's one complaint, its that the Alien and Predator missions seem shorter than the Marine missions. This was a problem with the original games also. The other is the lack of more multiplayer modes and maps which allows players to really take advantage of the strengths and weaknesses of the different races. Not a lot of people play the multiplayer in this game anymore and that's a shame because the modes that do exist are still pretty good. The maps are limited but they're still good. Stalking prey as a predator is a feeling like no other, and dropping down on an unsuspecting maine as the alien is pretty awesome. The multiplayer of this game needs a revival.
Overall, I'd recommend this to anyone who was a fan of the movies and especially a fan of the original Monolith Engine games. Buying this game is definitely a good investment, especially when its on sale, but the lack of active games in multiplayer may turn a lot of people off. If you guy this game, you'll be getting it most for its single-player experience which is good, but the story isn't exactly the best. Neither was the story of the original, so what can I say.

Isolation, vulnerability, dread… Not only does it cover the basic survival-horror elements, it also applies to what made Aliens vs. Predator such an undeniable hit in 1999. Although Rebellion decidedly never attempted to elevate the element of story-telling, providing a coherent plot rather than a series of detached levels, it was the superb level design, terrific environments and effective lightning coupled with relentless dread that reinforced an already satisfied gameplay in a believable setting that through implicit presentation was faithful to the famous movie franchises.
The sequel by Monolith, however, expanded and surpassed the original by far and the release of Aliens vs. Predator 2 turned out to be one of the best (shooter) games of 2001. The three compelling campaigns that not only took place simultaneously but also intersected at certain points were just as distinguished as the complex underlying structure of the story. Truly capturing the essence of a faithful Alien and Predator movie, the careful attention to detail and coherence against the elegant script was outermost outstanding. The frequent use of engaging voice-overs and excellent music only strengthened the overall impression that Aliens vs. Predator 2 very much unfolded like a great movie. Furthermore, all campaigns were just as terrific and consistent, with the exception of the marine that, by obvious reasons, kept most of the first-rate suspense intact and exceeded the game’s ability.
The return of Rebellion, however, is questionable regarding inconsistency, gameplay issues and uninspiring plot. Out of three campaigns, one is solid, the second mediocre and the third bad. Since there is a sense of story attached to at least one of them, the marine is the given highlight.  Dark, moody and overall good-looking surroundings, presenting a loyal (yet pretty much recycled) audio direction and amazing music, is a fairly good start. Besides, decently dramatic voice-acting (somewhat ruined by poor dialogue) and a sweet return of veteran actor Lance “Bishop” Henriksen are always considered strength.
There are a few decent levels of solid tension and the occasional sequences of narrative, but the lack of dread is remarkable and the brutal violence, although spectacularly atrocious to witness, does rarely compensate the absence of fear and substance. The straight forward story of the marine suffers from routine-like clichés without finesse and is mediocre at best, and it only goes downhill in the remaining campaigns. If predator has a less intriguing part except being a pretty much pointless hunter, then the aimless alien is utterly useless.
Although not as prominent, mediocrity also applies to a quite linear level design as well as inconsistent AI. Sudden, inexplicable limitations tend to appear in the surroundings for no apparent reason and stagnated civilians prefer to be killed rather than escaping. The mention of awkward controls seems inevitable too. While the marine campaign works fine, the command of both predator and alien feels clumsy and uneven at times, causing unnecessary retries (advising not to play on hard difficulty unless having a great patience…), but being a magnificent creature might suppose to be that harsh.
The striking brilliance of Monolith’s masterpiece is hardly recaptured in Rebellion’s addition, despite good intention in an actual overall decent presentation. Certainly too much mediocrity and too few substantial shortcomings cannot become as classy and characteristic, but lesser cons ultimately means more pros. And yes, last year’s Aliens: Colonial Marines definitely had more cons than pros.

Comparing this game to Town of Salem. This game is definitely more challenging, you actually need to use your damn brain to find the hackers. You don't get the privilege to rely on an ability that will assist you in finding out who the hackers are.
The good thing about that is everyone is basically on the same playing field. No one has an ability that over powers another person to make the game unfair for anyone. There's no immunity or any special ability that gets in the way of thinking. This game just straight up needs brain power, and you REALLY gotta pay attention to the chat and peoples actions to really figure out who the hacker is.
But with that, there's also some negative parts to the game. Since it IS basically all about thinking and good guessing. You're gonna come across a lot of people who either Cheat, Troll, or are just bad at weeding out the hackers. (if you're an agent)
If you're going to play this game i'd suggest you be EXTREMELY patient and level headed. Cause you're going to come across many people who will ruin the game for you by either not listening and shooting your opinions down, or you'll just be accused of being a hacker when you're an agent for literally no reason what so ever.
The negative side to the game really shouldn't be looked at TOO much, over the fun and positive side to the game. Cause its kinda obvious you're gonna experience it when its a game about GUESSING and THINKING who's bad. But it is only a warning as to what you'll probably experience in the game.
But I personally think a really good way of avoiding all that stuff is by grabbing a group of friends or other serious players you'll find in the discord. And hosting custom game with those people, knowing they'll also play how it should be played and not ruin it for anyone else.
Overall its a well balanced game with its High's and Low's.

This is a very fascinating yet horrific game. It takes inspiration from Alice in Wonderland and twists it with horror aspects and gore to paint a terrifyingly beautiful picture. You play as a little girl named Fran Bow, who is trapped in a mental asylum after the brutal death of her parents. Your only goal is to escape and find your pet kitty Mr. Midnight. The question is how to do it... and figuring out the meaning of seeing things no-one else can see. Let's just say you need to take the red pill every once in a while.
The story from what I've gathered after three straight hours of play thus far is fairly simplistic, almost like a children's fairytale... albeit a fairytale definitely made for adults and NOT kids (seriously do NOT buy this game for your kids! Despite its cutesy artstyle there is a ton of disturbing/bloody/gory imagery throughout that can be very frightening.)
Some of my favorite aspects of the game are the little nods to various old school games found within minigames played throughout the point and click tale. There's a maze minigame similar to Pac-Man, a river crossing game that's basically a repaint of Frogger, and a few others I have yet to see. As the game is a point and click adventure there is no customization or RPG style elements aside from collecting various items and combining them in various ways to help you throughout your journey.
What truly makes this game unique is the mix of disturbing gore and story elements with the adorable, storybook artstyle. The result is a beautiful game with tons of little details that require a couple playthroughs or so to understand everything. However once clues are pieced together you'll find yourself going "Ah-hah!" and even getting surprised at some of the twists and turns.
Then there's the truly disturbing parts; the blood, gore, and the true fate of the children in the asylum. Many of the children housed there have very sad, very creepy backstories which can be discovered by using the red pills to see the true insanity beneath the surface. Sometimes the results can be nauseating to say the least. This is a game that doesn't pull punches with the gore though what makes it frightening is how it makes you think. The fear in this game is all psychological - which is quite fitting considering the setting.
Overall this is a game that I recommend to both horror fans and those looking for something a little different from the norm. I'm not sure if it is worth the $15 price tag, but the art is a definite selling point as is the detailed story. Give it a try, and always be aware that YOU CAN SEE.

Northgard. What an amazing game, Northgard is an RTS that lands somewhere between civilization and age of empires, and boy does it land there wonderfully. The gameplay it self is a very nice balance between some multitasking and city management. The game itself revolves around colonizing pre arranged territories which cost a specific amound of food in order to take them, you also can't colonize a territory in which there are other units beside ours (or none at all you don't have to send units over unless there is something to kill). As of right now the army choices are very few, namely you can have warriors a warlord and you can bring a few more like the berserker and a giant by completing certain tasks. Also each territory has a certain number of buildings so you must choose what to build where and how to balance your resource management and your peoples happiness population and lore (research in other words).
Over all the game has a very nice balance there are a lot of enemies and feats to achieve which all give you different rewards helping you win in anyway you prefer, for example you can kill the wyvern to earn fame to achieve the fame victory etc. I also really like the aesthetic of the game the grafics are nice and smooth, the art style is really nice a little cartoony not too realistic but still works perfecttly fine with the game. Over all the game is really nice and has a huge room for improvements and the potential of becoming an amazingly great game

For a video review and rundown of how it works:
The game reward system has severely been overhauled with the last few updates:
Previously when you completed a game you won 5 TP (townie points). A win doubled this amount. When you accomplished achievements you were also awarded varying amounts of TP.
You could then spend said TP for new skins, houses, maps, etc. Nothing needed in any way, just allowed you to be all sexy around other players.
Now... the system was changed. Previously you could speed things up with money (purchasing this via steam gave you a healthy amount of said TP), but it wasn't needed if you just spent time playing it.
But now you no longer earn TP for playthroughs. Instead you earn merit points.
What do merit points do? The same thing. Kind of.
TP costs were 560-4800 per item.  Merit points are about the same... but only the 'older' items are available. So about a quarter of the store is now purchasable for free. While this means that to get all 'the really cool new stuff' you have to spend cash... it also means that those items are now 'even more coveted'.
Lets discuss this logically. There has been seriously alot of backlash:
The devs made this game for free, with some help from kickstarter. They have been rebalancing some classes (honestly the witch is a monster now, but still they are trying)... and so it's not just cosmetic updates for money. Alot of what I've seen shouted were obviously insults at the devs because they feel this is a cash grab.
But also realize they are now focusing on mobile. And the account works on all devices.
So because they are on mobile, and that doesn't come cheap to design for (properly, not the junk crap everyone throws up en masse), it requires some cash.  And this is how they are funding it.
By asking you to pay for cosmetic stuff that doesn't impact the game.  If you 'buy the steam system' you get double the merit points. It's not alot, but over... 2ish... weeks I've earned roughly 1600 merit points. I could buy some scrolls to get to play a role more often, but overall I'm not worried about it much. I have the skins I want so I'm just playing the game to murder people.
If you want to buy skins for free, then this game just alienated you. If you want to murder people quietly and get away with it, the game didn't change. It just rewards you differently.

Space Hack is a very old looking Diablo throw back, “Sci-fi, RPG/Action” game. This game simply has the feeling of an “old game”, mostly because of its inspiration from Diablo. This game was released in 2005, so do keep in mind that, that reflects on the controls and the graphics.

Basically you are humanity’s old hope for survival, you start the game standing inside an enclave called a “biosphere”, it’s your job to help these other humans to be able to survive this strange new world. Naturally, in a sci-fi game the enemies you encounter are various form of Alien.
You can equip different weapons, and armor, as well as use various other types of items that are pictured up as loot from aliens you kill (or objects you find). This game also utilizes a questing system to help give you tasks and keep you active.
Something should be mentioned about the controls of this game. I have never adjusted the camera angle in a 3D game with my scroll wheel before, additionally there are several other key bindings that confused me, if you intend to try this game out, I highly suggest checking out the bindings BEFORE you jump into the game; Or else you’ll find yourself out of laser charges and franticly trying to find your inventory to equip a baseball bat to murder with.

There are no steam achievements for Space Hack.
Space Hack is $0.99, what else is there to say? Usually I say wait for a sale, but this game is already purchasable by shaking down a little kid for his lunch money. No further comments.

This type of game will appeal to a very select “flavor” of gamer, again, the game was released in 2005, the graphics reflect that, I haven’t been able to figure out if the majority of the people who played the original Diablo like or dislike this game, it seems pretty much split even.
To be honest, most people on steam have tons of games in their steam library, most people will probably enjoy playing other games then this one, but if you’re feeling retro, and liked Diablo (or the dungeon crawler genre in general) this might be worth picking up.

I would like to give CHKN a very good score. It deserves more to be honest. I mean 150+ people purchasing such a creative game? It deserves more to be honest. CHKN is an open world sandbox game where life itself is your strongest tool. Bring creatures to life by assembling them from body parts. With Creative, Adventure, and Multiplayer modes, there is an abomination for everyone. The main point of the game is You have the power to bring creatures to life by slapping blocks together, in whatever shape, size, or combination you want. These blocks of intelligent life give your creature unique personalities based on the combinations you make. No two creatures are alike...unless you make them alike. In which case, an egg will pop out of one of them. Even if it’s a cat. Because SCIENCE.
Now i have 4 things. As a developer, as a gamer, as a graphic designer and as a gameplay reviewer.
As a developer, I love the wacky physics in the game. The physics and building code is unique. I decoded it into a simple notepad which, just saying, i will not use for a CHKN mod unless i have permission. I do this for almost every game. The code is unique and the variables are outstanding. I love how you can just make anything and it will react differently. The programmers must have taken months to make the combinations work. Heck! I have made my own mod. Now i did make a mod but i am not sharing it publically. I used the assets (textures and monsters) to make my own 3-D Story Rich Standalone game. I will NOT sell it without permission as I respect these developers and they are awesome!
As a gamer, I love building games. I love building settlements, I love building my own fake pets. Now i can make real pets that move and its amazing! I love crafting and open world games the most out of all the other games like Call of Duty, CSGO etc. The crafting and open world (Free roam) games catch my eye and this game is exactly that. You can do whatever you want. Creative mode, you can obviously build and do whatever. Adventure, you can craft hatchets, Gates, fences and its incredible. This is a one of a kind game and can never be cloned a better way.
As a graphics designer, the game is amazing. It is almost flawless. It only lags when there is a new bit of terrain generating and thats about it. The fastest is really fast, No doubt!
As a gameplay reviewer, i can say this game has not got much content and could get boring within a matter of hours. Thats in my view. But i keep exploring new areas and i hope you guys get a lot. I have reviewed a lot of games like SEUM: Speedrunners from hell and Gameguru. HECK! This is the best so far!
In conclusion, You should buy this game no matter what. If you hate EA games, DO NOT BUY IT! but if you have imagination and have an amazing list of things you have ever wanted to do and you like playing god, go for it! It's amazing. Ok, this is my first steam review so I think I'll just break it down into pros and cons.
Pros: I guess It's a good deal considering you also get Doom, Doom 2 and Doom 3 plus some expansions. Higher resolutions and slightly higher res textures. The game runs better.
Cons: (This was a con for me, other people might like this) the game is much shorter and easier since you can now use a gun and a flashlight at the same time plus there is much more ammo and the game is brighter (why add a shoulder mounted flashlight when the game is already much brighter?). There is no mod support. Remember the cool Wolfenstein levels in Doom 2? Well they have been censored way too much, look up doom 3 bfg censorship on youtube to see what I mean. If you want 16x AA you need a NVIDIA graphics card.
So all in all, you could just mod the original to look way better than this. The only reason I recommend it is because it doen't have that weird glitch with the graphics settings that forces you to run it in low settings (anyone else get that glitch?) and it runs really smoothly.

Doom 3 is the masterpiece of survival horror adventure and technological masterpiece of ex generation (ps3,xbox360). You can see how many titles out there (Half Life 2, Resident evil 4, dead space) r in fact influnced by the horror design featured within doom 3.
This remaster version enhanced the experience which I could not possibly before. It runs so smooth like no other fps out there on low spec modern machines.

In my memory, I could not have the right hardware to run the game at medium setting back to 2004. The mainstream monitor scale was 4:3. I bought the world first 16:9 widescreen laptop Sony Vaio in 2004. After several years release of doom 3 , I read everywhere people r buying new hardware to build a high end pc to run doom3 in ultra.It is nearly 10 years after the epic release. Now I am able to run it on a laptop with 650m 1gb vram at 1440p max at 60fps.
One thing worth to mention is that I did NOT play doom 3 much deeper than 30minutes progress in 2004. I was scared by the ultra realistic creepy monsters.
In 2014, it is still scary as hell but due to better maturity mind now I can play the game without hiding underseat. Another factor could be my soul has already survived through other horror games these years (eg.resident evil 4, dead space 3).
As an epic masterpiece,  Doom 3 is still providing an authentic scary experience and fresh if you did not play it (much) before like me previously.

Well... i purchased that game only because it is Hack`n`Slash and it cost 0,19 euro... I am little surprised! I expected some♥♥♥♥♥♥that will be uninstalled after 10 minutes, but it is quite good game. If you compare it to other h`n`s, you will never purchase it, but otherwise you need to be prepared to more than 7 hours of good, slightly repetitive gameplay that has some features that are not spotted frequently in this genre. Laser weapons using mana... ekhm "energy"? Why not. Spells that needs to be found as droppable items? Quite interesting. I am impressed that Space Hack even support my native (1366x768) panoramic resolution.
How about gameplay itself? Well... it is not so differential, but it is solid. We have our protagonist, our protagonist has tools of justice and we need to bring that justice to everybo... everyalien on sight. It is hard to write something else here... I do not encountered many bugs, crashes never happened.
Its solid 6/10 from me. It is not AAA production, but if you look at it as low-budget... indie game, you will be satisfied. Compared to some other "lower class" h`n`s like Fate, or even older superproductions like Diablo 1, it is solid game that only lacks some variety of gameplay, but may take some hours of your life.
Do not even try to compare it to Titan Quest/Diablo 2,3/Path of Exile, because it will be just stupid.

I don't know what the No Moon devs were drawing from to create Mindnight, but the game sessions just -flow-. The node missions, voting patterns, and chat are your tools when deciding who's lying (or, if you're a spy, they're your tools for avoiding any/all suspicion of wrong). With a group of experienced players, a session becomes a game of logic and patience.
Currently the community operates from the discord server advertised on the main menu of Mindnight. There, you can set up a game, report bugs and bad players, and suggest things that you'd like to see in the game. The devs are highly responsive to input and seem to enjoy interacting with the members. It's not unlikely to find out that one of the devs hacked all your nodes in a session!
Overall a fun game and a fun community.

MINDNIGHT - a game based around hackers lying to all of their friends faces and deceiving everyone in the game, and agents trying to figure out who is really trustworthy and how they can secure 3 nodes to win the game...
At first, the game seemed okay, but I didn't think I would get addicted to it. Oh boy, was I wrong.

First time I opened the game, the first thing I noticed was the incredible graphics, the style was very pixelated, yet so detailed, it's an amazing combo. This is a game I had seen quite a long while back. A peer of mine was playing it at school (before classes started, don't worry) and at the time it was not very big. It had a couple different species parts and an interesting little editor. At the time I hadn't played to much attention to it, but lately I found it again but this time on steam. Looking into it I saw it now included an adventure mode taking a less serious approach to survival games in a way.
Now, from playing a decent few hours I can say the game is by no means done, after all what else does 'Early Access' mean? But, what I can say is that the game has some really great developers working on it. They are the first I have ever seen that make full use of the steam discussion boards to get bug reports and suggestions for the game - they even have the change log and future plans up there.
Seeing how they were fairly reactive I made a post to organize the bugs I found into a new post as a few of the other discussion boards seemed less organized and had more of a personal voice than a journalistic voice as I would have written it. It just seemed more logical to list the bug finding the same way someone would report findings from research. So I did that. Within an hour the devs thanked me for posting my findings and encouraged me to keep them informed if I found more. Never have I personally been able to have this kind of interaction with devs before. This kind of interaction I feel is what is necessary to take a game like CHKN and turn it into something quite significant later on in its development. This is in contrast to what I have seen developers with good games that had great potential do when they stepped away from the community for too long. Cube world and Starforge come to mind when I say this, and such a pity too.
So if you like the idea of an adventure/creative sandbox where you can make your own multi-species creatures piece by piece to ward off attackers and ride them around, build structures, farm, and in general a survival game that admits it just wants to be fun and not ultra-realistic, then add onto that the odds of your suggestions being seen are very high, I'd say CHKN is a very worthwhile game to get in its current stage.

Let me start off by saying I ♥♥♥♥ing love Doom. I do my best to share it with and introduce it to my friends because I want other people to discover this amazing series. Let me tell you a story about Doom 3, a true story.
Doom 3 did not tickle Scaramouche in the pickle department. No, sir. He wanted it very bad, but when he saw the reviews he was very easily turned off. The game did not seem close enough to older Doom games and when you have a gap like the massive gaping wound between Doom 2 and Doom 3 there has to be some connection, and here everything seemed awfully different.
Years later, Scaramouche actually bought this game during a summer sale - the Doom 3 BFG edition, not the standard. At this time all Mouche had was a laptop from 2008 but he figured that would be enough to run a game that came out around that time, especially with utilities like HiAlgoSwitch and whatnot. To his dismay, however... the game did not run at all.
Doom 3 and Doom 3: BFG Edition will only (ONLY!) run on computers with graphics cards that support OpenGL. While this does promise some decent graphics this is pretty uncool for people like Scaramouche.
Well finally Scaramouche got a desktop computer with much better specs, installed Doom 3: BFG Edition, and ran it.
It was nothing like the Doom 3 that Scaramouche had dreaded. This game was a different beast. Doom 3 standard seemed more like it would fit in with more generic modern horror games but Doom 3 BFG Edition was different. It had all of the spooky scariness of modern horror gaming and the spooky scariness of older horror gaming - Like old Doom. Scaramouche was very pleased and proceeded to play through it all as fast as he could as he went about comparing the two versions. The better flashlight and the tweaked balance were both great in his opinion. He was compelled to finish the game, and a few months later, he finally got around to recommending it.
Okay so... during our little story here we already talked about some stuff I liked about this game and honestly that's all I liked about it and it was enough for me to give it a solid rating. The old Doom feeling, the new updating lighting and graphics, the flashlight change (In Doom 3 you can't use a weapon while you have it out but in BFG you can) and the slight changes to balance all work in BFG's favor.
... This game... brings a massive change in style to the Doom franchise. The enemies look oh so EXTREMELY different from the classic Doom games. They all have a more demonic look but... it... the enemy design didn't feel like Doom. It wasn't all cartoonish and badass, it was just... real♥♥♥♥♥
For example, I spent all game looking for Barons of Hell/Hell Knights and didn't see any - until I realized that I had, when I looked through the Doom wiki for stats on the Baron of Hell in Doom 2, ironically. They look SOOO different. They aren't big red guys with super cool giant horns wearing khakis. They're huge, buff Doom 3 Imps. And yeah they were supposed to be like huge, buff Doom Imps in Doom 1 and Doom 2, but they didn't just look like strong imps, they looked like Barons of Hell.
You saw it out of the corner of your eye and thought "Oh god, now he's gonna shoot green♥♥♥♥♥♥at me right?" but you don't in Doom 3, you see it out of the corner of your eye and think "Ah okay just an imp, I'll dodge that♥♥♥♥♥♥while I kill this Revenant because it's more important" and he ♥♥♥♥s your♥♥♥♥♥♥
And that's not all the change in look for all of the monsters does. The harder difficulties are recommended for Doom veterans so I was like "Well I've beaten Doom on Nightmare a couple times this shouldn't be too bad" but I got rekt on like the just barely over normal difficulty because I didn't know what the ♥♥♥♥ the enemies were gonna do because they LOOKED DIFFERENT BUT DID THE SAME DANGEROUS THING.
Also, even if you do have all of the badass weapons and speed and strength of the Doom Guy lineage, it doesn't really fit if the art style doesn't make you feel like a
, it just makes you feel like... a guy. And it's not just the art style, other things contribute to it. The entire time they keep calling you "MAHREEN," not "Soldier" or "Hero" or anything like that. It's always "MAHREEN, YER FINALLY BACK FROM HELL, NOW GET IN THIS AIR DUCT AND CRAWL TO THIS POSITION!"
You are treated like♥♥♥♥♥♥in this game.
Halfway through the game they give you a major decision and ACTUALLY LEAVE IT UP TO YOU to decide based on what you know (Don't worry you actually do have a lot to work with in the thought department), and there is a right answer and a "wrong" answer, but either way, they treat you like you didn't just BLOW THROUGH A HOARD OF DEMONS AND FIX A BUNCH OF♥♥♥♥♥♥ALL OVER THE FACILITY TO MAKE THIS HAPPEN, ALL BY YOURSELF PLUS LIKE TWO LITTLE ROBOTS THAT SHOOT THINGS A LITTLE AND THEN DIE. Like SERIOUSLY it's like if your parents leave you at Grandma's for a week and she keeps dropping♥♥♥♥♥♥and like she can't take care of herself so you have to help her with everything and after a week of ♥♥♥♥ing pain sweat blood and tears helping your grandma who you love she doesn't even thank you one time, she just gives you more♥♥♥♥♥♥to do and doesn't let you play Doom 3: BFG Edition at all, even though it's like your favorite game or something.
And the entire time one part of you wants to tell her that she's a ♥♥♥♥♥ but the other part of you enjoys it because it feels good to work for something, even when you don't know what it is.
And then your parents come pick you up and they're like "Did you have fun?" and you tell them you did anyway because hard work makes you feel good and then they're like "Thanks for putting up with this" because they know how hard it must've been, and you gotta smile thinking about it because even though she is a ♥♥♥♥♥ you got to bond with your dear old grandma, and while she's senile and cruel, you understand what it's like kinda and you know what SHE has to deal with.
Doom 3: BFG Edition fixes the problems of Doom 3 and still delivers the excellent Bethesda-grade storytelling and the kind of gameplay that only id can deliver. While it may he hard and unrewarding/unforgiving, it's a bit of a long haul to the end that
will take up a lot of your time, and it doesn't feel as cool, quirky, and stylized as older Doom titles, it delivers an engaging experience that keeps you drawn in the entire time, regardless of opinions you have about the standard edition.

Northgard
Early Access
Shiro Games
Shiro Games
3D Real Time Strategy
8th of March, 2017
Singleplayer
You might say I’m a bit biased in Northgard’s case. This title fondly reminds me of The Settlers IV, one of the first strategy games I ever played. The game I’m reviewing today is still in Early Access stage, but it is a stable and entertaining experience nonetheless. The dev team have already proven their creativity on Steam with their successful Evoland series and even now with their third project, they still seem to focus on fusing two or more gaming genres into hybrid titles with few flaws between them. Northgard attempts to revive not just the long lost glory of the Settlers franchise but also Cultures, among other similar titles.
Sadly I cannot discuss about a storyline since it hasn’t been implemented yet in the Early Access version. From what I could gather in-game and by examining the game’s Store Page, I’m sure we shall have a captivating story filled with danger and adventure. We are talking afterall, about Norsemen. Scandinavian colonialism is uncontestedly accurate as both Iceland and Greenland were settled centuries before other European cultures would set foot on them.
Vikings or not, Norse explorers such as Erik Thorvaldsson and his son, Leif Erikson have left their mark upon history and their exploits most certainly deserved to be adapted for video gaming. So Northgard can currently be played in sandbox/skirmish mode and doesn’t include a campaign or a set of individual scenarios. Once it gets fully released though, expect a coherent plot and a natural scale of progression. Evoland I and II haven’t disappointed in that regard and I have no reason to doubt Shiro Games now.
The game looks great, with diversified assets and the option to zoom in, quite a lot. Fully 3D graphics that show clear signs of attention to details, from animation and even the dynamic weather effects. I do wish the dev team might also include a day/night cycle eventually. One thing I noticed and bothered me a bit (not enough to count it as a weak point) is that all the settlers are male and once they get assigned to a certain profession, they look like clones of one another. 2002’s Cultures: Northland had female settlers too and even children since it fully simulated the family life as well. And they didn’t look exactly the same.
It’s a game design choice, I know, but when addressing the topic of colonial life at least aim for a bit more realism, ok? The current building roster and the jobs they imply, offer sufficient variety for now but there is always room for improvement. The islands players get to settle could sure use more terrain diversity and perhaps more wildlife as well. I think that most of the minor issues I mentioned above can be ameliorated within several more months in development.
Both the soundtrack and sound effects are nothing spectacular yet they alternate pleasantly between a relaxing tone and a more alert one, once combat is being initiated by either the player or AI opponents. Honestly, very few strategy titles I played over the years could rival the sound scores of the Age of Empires or Blitzkrieg series and unlike action-packed shooters or role playing games, I know that real time strategy doesn’t need music to “assist or further the plotline”.
I already mentioned The Settlers and Cultures, as clear inspiration for Northgard’s gameplay, yet the title uses one of its most crucial mechanics in an entirely different manner from the aforementioned models. Territorial expansion is more close to the Civilization series, with (non-hexagonal) plots of land which first need to be individually explored and only afterwards, colonized if your settlement can afford the ever growing Food requirement.
Since Norsemen were known as both ambitious and resilient people, it should come as no surprise that the ultimate goal in Northgard isn’t simply to annihilate your rivals but to outsmart and especially, outlive them. Survival plays center stage, in a game which simulates some of the harshest winter conditions seen in strategy titles. The kind of unforgiving weather which will deplete both Food and Wood stockpiles if you weren’t paying enough attention to the rapidly shifting seasons.
If you think you can win in this game by mustering a large warband and swarming your opponents as soon as you see the window of opportunity, I have some bad news for you. Northgard is more static than it seems at first glance. You need to “turtle” not Zerg Rush the other clans which might not even offer a stiff resistance if you learn to properly defend before trying to attack them. Trade shall offer you both the ample supply of goods to survive and prosper, so long as you focus on the resource gathering closer to your Town Hall (the HQ, if you will).
Land patches offer different opportunities as some may contain rich soil (which could enable wheat harvesting) while other colonized parts might host the type of woodland which shall never leave you short of timber for construction, survival, and even trading with the other clans. A skill tree handles the unlockable perks which can considerably decrease the challenge, so I rarely bothered with them.
I keep mentioning rivals, but it’s time I explain the strengths and weaknesses of each “faction”, so to speak. The current game stage features four not-so-distinct clans so far. The combat-oriented Clan of the Wolf, prefer the aggressive approach and shall gain bonuses to their warrior training and damage they can inflict. The more balanced option is being represented by the Clan of the Stag, which prefer the more peaceful way of Fame towards the ultimate Victory. The “easy mode” appears to materialize within the Clan of the Goat, which have very useful bonuses to food production and consumption. Lastly, the Clan of the Raven represents the master traders of Northgard and can hire mercenaries to bolster their armed forces.
Indeed, I have won on Normal difficulty on a randomized scenario (procedural generation is implemented every time you start a new game) with the Goat Clansmen by trading food to the Jötunn (Giants) tribe in exchange for kröwns, the monetary resource in Northgard. Not all in-game creatures from the Norse mythology are as friendly and open to trade as the Giants though. Draugr (undead), valkyries and wyverns can lay waste to your warbands unless they have received adequate training and the leadership of a warchief unit.
Northgard’s a promising and polished game already, while it also proves that Steam didn’t fail completely with the implementation of the Early Access program. Being a hybrid of multiple genres and with an equal number of inspired gameplay mechanics, the title I had the chance to review today couldn’t have failed. I consider its price tag justified and I urge all strategy fans who prefer slower paced progression, to purchase Northgard even in its current stage. I personally can’t wait to see the campaign, Shiro Games has in store for us!
EDIT: Trading Cards have been finally added.
+ Pleasant graphics and relaxing sounds.
+ Steam Achievements & Steam Trading
+ Interesting mix of RTS combat with colonial settlement & survival.
- Not enough cultural/technological diversity between the rival Clans.
- No campaign or story missions in this Early Access stage.

This is a really fun game and is great to dip in and out with but unfortinately has some big bugs that can cause you to lose games.
It's a great resource manager/conquest game, with a few twists, often taking some of the best aspects of other space games and building them into a single package but then randomly, stuff fails to work.
Graphically it's very sweet with a kind of pseudo-cartoon effect and these give a sense of scale. Paradoxically they remind me a little of a violent version of Le Petit Prince by Exupery, it's that kind of scale. I'm sure there was an element of inspiration. We travel the galaxy with our mechanoids, sweeping all before us.
PVE.. well the difficulty seems to be huge steps. It's either easy or hard with very little middle ground. Beat it or lose. There's few games where I've felt like I was in a big fight. I either win big or get overwhelmed.
PVP is very good generally, you're at the mercy of another player and it's often down to the skills and experience that will decide who wins.
But occasionally stuff just absolutley fails to work, and this seems to be especially when trying to expand. It's as though the AI has decided that you aren't able to expand your empire while your oppent can. This is a huge thingand has happened to me a few times recently so I am fairly convinced there's a problem with the game's engine. It's a shame because it could be excellent otherwise.
My only other cricisism is that updates are few and far between. I suspect there's a very small dev team but if they could fix some bugs and add more content this could really rock.

I first saw this game back in 2013 when Markiplier played the demo of it. I had forgotten about it, until 2015 when Jacksepticeye had begun playing it. After deciding to buy the game, I found myself enjoying the dark yet simple story of Fran bow's journey to find her pet, Mr. Midnight. The positives of the game are the story, which manages to take you to fantastic worlds, and sceince-bending rules. Despite this, the story manages to keep itself relevent and together. Other positives include how, as a horror game, the jump scares aren't cheap, and the few end up mostly being fran battling her demons, or the medicine you take. The only real problem is the same problem that plagues most point-and-click games, if you miss something, you will get stuck for a while. However, for $15 with 15+ hours to completeion, I most certainly recommend this game.

I didn't know what to expect when I started this game but its rather amusing. One thing I didn't expect going into this game was a creature creation system and when I stumbled upon it I yelled out look its the HOLY chicken! As for the gameplay man this game will rock your socks off never in my life have I created an army of one legged chickens to do my bidding. Nothing was as satisfying as having a flock of twenty chickens maul a tree and then watching them eat all the fruit that falls to the ground. This of course was shortly lived after finding a dragon...
If the game is as fun in coop as it is in single player this game is going to be a great blast not to mention all the silly looking things running around dropping eggs all over the place. While the building system needs some work before its really ready for release the gameplay as of early access is SOLID I would recommend this game if you enjoy games such as minecraft but focus more on rolling around with a horde of killer block pets. I can really see this game being a blast in coop.
As for bugs I must say I expected a few bugs being early access but the game itself was flawless I couldnt even find a bug when I attempted to. I had a few graphic glitches but nothing that broke gameplay this all being said I plan on getting a lot more hours in on this game. Another thing I noticed about this game is just how much work the dev team is putting into updates that being said I am expecting great things from this game and will keep playing and checking back to see what progress the game will be making.
If you have the money for this game and are on the fence about it I personally would recommend it and if you have a friend with it or someone to play with you shouldnt pass this one up it will pull you in and suck all your time away while you coop the world with a killer army of chickens or even a horde of really messed up looking animals. Guess What? F*ck the towers and take care of it yourself. Forget a tower for taking out air units, shoot them yourself. Target only weak from behind, either get the unit's attention and turn its back to your turrets of destruction or go up behind it yourself and kick it in the♥♥♥♥♥ There are 5 classes to choose from, each with their own weapon specialization unique buffs and a nice little story being told through comic book cutscenes. The game offers lobbies up to 4 players so send copies to your friends and get to it.

Earlier I've rated this review positively, hoping that it would improve. Sadly Capcom has brought disappointment after disappointment. PC community has always been big on modding, and of course they restricted it. I can understand why, but how they executed it is just awful. The best way to do implement it is to implement it the exact same way Techland did for Dying Light. There should be an option for modding. Where modders will only be able to play with modders, and not with PS4 and Vanilla Users. Sadly they don't see that. Instead they try releasing a Rootkit (which at most time is considered a backdoor for viruses.) Apparently they took it off to avoid legal trouble but the damage has already been done.
Now am I saying its a bad game? No. In fact, I love the game and still prefer it over other mainstream fighting games (Except for tekken and guilty gear). And it's helluva lot better than Mortal Kombat. But I can't say I recommend it. Or at least for full price. I would say this. It's a great game to start fighting games, but do yourself a favor. Just wait for a better rerelease of the game.
At that time, like always, the game would be fixed, everything would be present and you get your money's worth.
