Northgard or also known as: "The Settlers but with vikings" is a simple strategy game. You're playing the leader of one of 3 clans that are currently playable: The Wolf; the Stag and the Goat. Each starts with different advantages and bonuses.
To win the game you can either play offensive by dominating up to 3 AI players by distroying their headquarters or defensive by gaining a minimum of fame, money or knowledge before anyone else. One game normally takes about 2 hours.
The maps are divided in small areas that first needs to be explored by scouts before they can be taken in exchange for food. Some areas however will have enemies on them, those arears first have to be cleared by your military force which should be acquired as soon as possible.
To conquer new areas, populating and defending them, it all makes alot of fun. However, it's easy to tell that the game is currently in an "Early access" state. Just a short list of buildings are available and the maps are also tiny and overall the game is way too short. This makes the game boring after about 2 games and I hope there will be added more to it.
This game definitly has its potential, it's a decent and enjoyable game, however with the little content it currently possesses, it's not worth the 20$. I would recommend to wait a little until the campaign and the multiplayer modes are added to the game.

I'll immediatly take this off of my chest:This game is much better than street fighter 4!
No more combo system based on one frame links, so you don't get mashed reversal as soon as you mis-time a split second.
No more 50/50 wake up situation all the time, because you have quickrise in this game and most of the moves don't result into a hard knockdown.
No more vortex characters.
Better art style.
Good audio,at least most of them especially when compared to the horrible tracks in SF4.
Less emphasis on fireball zooning.
Much better balanced tier list resulting in a great variety of chosen characters,even though ryu and ken are still predominant online, but then again not as much as sf4, at least the vanilla version.
The gameplay basicly feels more dynamic, much less turtle oriented and more aggressive.
So...is this game perfect? Not by a long shot, the online mode is not as good as SF4 at least in the state it is now and this is aggravating for everybody, on top of that the single player is really poor with the abscence of arcade mode(yeah you read this right), this is bad especially for casual players but it will be fixed in the next updates.
Another unfortunate thing is the 8 frame lag, if you are an harcore player, this is somenthing not to take lightly, it doesn't ruins the game by any means at least not in the strict sense of the term but it's still bad, some moves will be hard to avoid on reaction and you will notice more responsivness in most other fighting games, SF4 included.
If you want single player content and missions and dont care about the competive aspect of fighting games and want mostly to play only online then this, like most fighting games, but especially this is not the game for you. Mortal kombat X would probably be a wiser choice ( apart the online..)
I can recomnend this game to all harcore street fighter player or people interested in becoming harcore especially by playing it with people offline. Dont misunderstand me though... I still think like most people that is not good to release a game so barebone and rough and the online is still a very important thing anyway, casual player or not, but i believe that like a rough stone with the next updates this game can become a shiny diamond.Still a good game even with the problems that could' ve been avoided by capcom.
Anyway...If the game doesn't change for the better in the next updates especially for the online this review may change for the worst, I like the core mechanichs but again I can tolerate some mistakes made by capcom,but only temporarily. Sort it Capcom!
Edit 16/11/2016
The online is fine now, but not because capcom fixed anything, but because I opened the NAT of my router towards steam so I guess in my case the problem was on my end, now everything works really well and I can find games fast in spite of seaching only for people with 4 or 5 bars connection (europe).
Now I can recommend this game even more!

this is a game of deception. there are really 3 categories of teams that you are randomly placed in
and each role has abilites for e.g. doctors can stop their target from being killed at night, investigators can get an idea of their target ( if that targets abilites alow them to use a gun, if they have blood on them, if they are a loner. all these can help identifiy their target each night) and so on
Town- your objective is to destroy all evil roles and help the town survive by investigating all those around you, either by using your unique abilities or through a process of elimination.
Mafia- your objective is destroy everyone excluding the mafia (and on rare occasions, witches and survivors) by two primary  methods, killing 1 person each night or convicing the town to kill their own players during the day by means of deception ( one member of the mafia can kill each night and depending on the roles of the others they may be able to investigate those around them, blackmail a target so they cannot speak the next day, block another from preforming their ability ect.)
Survivor/Killer - this class contains many roles, they are usualy by themselves excluding vampires. the serial killer role can kill each night, is immune to being killed at night and can kill those that attempt to either role block them or place them in jail. the arsonist douses their targets in fuel and can ignite them the following night or douse as many targets as they want and ignite them all in one night. the werewolf can rampage at a targets house every second night and kills anyone that visits their tagert that night. the survivor is neutral and can win the game simply by surviving untill another team prevails. the witch can controll one target and force them to use thier ability on another ( the ability is unknow to the witch ). the vampires can bite a person every second night ( exluding the mafia and anyone else in this catagory ) and can turn them into vampires and join forces. the amnesiac can claim the role of someone that has already died exluding unique roles like serial killer.
executioner/jester- executioners want to get their target killed, preferably through hanging during the day, this wins the game for them regardless of what happens after, if their target is killed at night they become a jester. a jester's only goal is to be lynched and hanged during the day, this also wins the game for them regardless of what happens after then they may kill one person that night from the list of people that sent them to their death
this game is the perfect game of deception, no one wants to appear important, either for fear of death from a killing role at night or death by the town if they are in fact an evil role. but to win, they need support. a jester ( that wants to die by hanging ) will try to get hanged while seeming to not want it. this leaves many opportunities open to those that want to appear to be a jester to avoid suspicion by the town, and an uniterseting target for the killers.
accusations will fly, people will lie, you will die.

Hello Ladies and Gentlemen!
Today I will write a review about a first person tower defense game called Sanctum 2.
Sanctum 2 is a sequel to a quite famous first person tower defense game called Sanctum. Both games have been developed and published by a well known company called Coffee Stain Studios. They stand behind many well known titles. The most recent one is Goat Simulator. Yes, they made Goat Simulator.
Sanctum 2 is a first person shooter game in which the player has the ability to make a tower maze that will help him defend the core from a lot of numerous enemies. There are a lot of different weapons, towers and enemies in Sanctum 2, every one of them having different strengths and weaknesses. And to be able to experience the game fully, the player should have full party of people with each of them having a different character. I feel the question "why?" coming up next, so I'll just answer it to you now. Each character has his / her own weapon. One has shotgun, one has sniper, one has rocket launcher, one riffle and the newest character has a crossbow. Shotgun character is good against bigger enemies that come running at him. Rocket launcher is good versus swarms of enemies since his damage does not only go on one enemy. Sniper and Crossbow characters are best versus game bosses, since they deal largest amount of damage in one hit. And riffle is good versus pretty much anything, but of course it has smallest damage rate.
Each character can have a secondary weapon. There are many various secondary weapons so the player can fit exactly what they want to fit. There are also different perks in this game, so even those help out. So you could even turn slow, but powerful weapons into very fast, even more powerful weapons. Of course, there are many towers that help you in your victory. There are those towers that are fast, but deal small amount of damage, and then there are those that are slow and yet deal massive amount of damage. Each tower is good for something, and it's up to player to find out what is the best way to make the towers fit in with their game style. There are also a lot of different types of enemies. Some are small, numerous and fast, while others are big, slow and hard to kill.
Unlike the first game, Sanctum 2 feels a bit more open. It feels like you have more space to move, more space to build and more possibilities. On the other hand, this game also introduced leveling system. Each level unlocks different weapons, perks or towers to the player. Leveling is quite easy at start, but that changes later on. And the leveling system actually gives a replay value to the game, since you can always come back to old maps and redo them with your newly unlocked weapons, towers and perks.
Unlike in many other games, DLC's in this game are actually quite good. I am not a fan of DLC's in general so I still think that they are overpriced, but for the amount of money you put into them you get quite a few things back. With the DLC's you get tones of new maps, new characters and quite a few weapons. So the Complete Collection is a pure go from my end.
Honestly, I was a bit disappointed by the graphic. It does look prettier and there are more details than in the first one, but I just feel like there's many more things that the developers could do to make the game prettier. Audio on the other hand is amazing, and I just enjoyed listening to every song or background sound that the developers put into the game.
Pros:
- Many different maps.
- Characters to chose from.
- DLC's that give an actual new content.
- Various different unlockables.
Cons:
- No ability to change primary weapon until final level.
- Sometimes towers feel useless.
Final Grade: 7.5/10
Extra info: If you are a fan of first person shooters, or maybe tower defense games, then this game is for you. You just can't go wrong with Sanctum 2. You can buy Sanctum 2 over Steam.
In case you like my reviews, please head over to my blog and read the other reviews

Some years ago I ran a L4D clan.  After hundreds of hours, it all got a bit boring... but now a few years later I'm back on it, and finding it still holds its own against other online MP games of today, and better than even its own sequel.
Campaign mode follows the four survivors as hey battle towards escape, via helicopter, boat, whatever.  It's a lot of fun, especially in co-op with some good mates.  The game is made for speedruns, but manages to slow the pace at various "event" spots where you must stand off against hungry hordes of zombies.
The game comes into its own in versus mode.  Two teams of four take it in turns to play as the survivors, earning points for each % of the level they manage to cross before their doom.  Making it to the end of the level is an intense experience, for one reason - the other team play as the zombies!
Playing as the special infected requires its own skills, separate to the survivors'.  The attacking team must work together to create mayhem and kill off the humans.  A good team will coordinate attacks the AI couldn't dream of, and in turn the survivors must up their game to defend against the onslaught.
If you haven't played this game yet, it's not too late.  There are still active servers, and plenty of people to play against, although many of them seem to prefer L4D2 which, to be fair, does have all the levels from this game.
Got three friends?  Buy the four-pack and welcome to the best game of the last few years!

Ok so, I used to play this game in the past and enjoyed it a whole lot back then, and even if I'm gonna try to be as fair as possible in this, do take my words with a grain of nostalgia salt. (also tl;dr version further below)
The game has aged surprisingly well with the graphics being maybe not that great, but not horrid either; the combat is pretty straightforward and it has a pretty interesting skill leveling system where you build up skill experience to achieve new a new rank and acquire new skills or the ability to strengthen old ones. Classes are interesting and the skills that you can get on the higher levels often look pretty cool. Dungeons can be pretty fun to do with friends and especially from he halfway point onwards (which is level 100) dungeons can get pretty intreguing with puzzle-like bits. As you may have guessed from an old game there is a lot of grinding to be had, though the premium you get with a new account makes this a whole lot easier and quicker. (I'm not sure if the premium is gonna be for every new account or just as a one-time thing because it went over to steam)
That however, is where the good points kind of end with the game; grinding is very much a problem once your premium runs out, as you will have to walk everywhere and lose the ability to teleport around the maps; as well as losing a lot of inventory space. At the higher levels you can also run into money problems, as quests stop giving money for some reason and leveling passive skills becomes really expensive. Even with the blessing beads you're given with every new character (gives +200% exp for a month) the grind just becomes a chore. The game also has a lack of variety in armor, having only 3 types of armor and every new tier of armor basically looks the same but with a different color or slight changes (until you start reaching the level 130+ gear). The weapons are okay mind you, but other than for stat purposes I never found myself looking forward to getting new gear. Questing is dull and repeatitive as all quests basically fall into the category of kill things, loot things, talk to things or re-enter this place you just left... things.
Now I know that all things I spoke of are PvE related, but that's the point; even if I'm not a fan of PvP anyway, it takes a lot of grinding to get to the point where you can join PvP events (random dueling aside), let alone stand a chance because everyone and their mom is likely level 200 in there and can one-shot you. (do note I'm not sure about that as I never indulged in pvp with the steam version, but if I'm to believe how it was back in the day, that's how it goes.)
Sooo tl;dr. (for PVE things)
What I recommend with this game is give it a shot (preferably with friends); and if you find it to be fun, play it until the free premium runs out (if that's not a limited event thing). If you can look past all the things you lose after that, good for you, but I wouldn't recommend investing in new premium unless you really really like this game. If a game deliberately becomes horrible without premium I wouldn't support it, but that may just be me.

Despite a rocky launch, this is a unique but solid entry to the SF franchise. However, keep in mind this is very, very different from its predecessors, so it is important to purchase with the right expectations. For those in doubt, I recommend waiting purchasing when on sale.
PROS:
1) Battle mechanics are simpler, which is not necessarily a bad thing, especially for those new to the franchise. Combos are WAY easier to execute than in USFIV.
2) While slow to respond to fan feedback, CAMCOM has steadily addresssed issues that plagued the game at launch, such as:
-adding a free, DLC, expanded Story Mode "A Shadow Falls," which is equivalent to a two and a half hour animated movie interspersed with fights where you get to role play as every character (even the six season one characters you must purchase to play otherwise).
-adding more way to win fight money via Daily Challenges.
-adding a "versus CPU" mode.
-adding the option to purchase additional character color packs via fight money rather than enduring the grueling Survival Mode.
3) Stronger rage quitting penalties have been introduced to level the playing field.
4) Online matchmaking (for ranked and casual matches) is more objective because the system always matches you to an opponent so you do not constantly get matched to the same opponents.
5) Unlike USFIV, which had several similar characters, every character feels unique and has their own V-Skill, V-Reveral and V-Trigger.
6) This game really rewards you for defensive skills, which enables you to turn the tide of battle quickly.
7) You "pre-select" your favorite character and their attributes before you are even matched to an online fight, which reduces time needed to select a character each time you are paired with an opponent. Obviously, this is a disadvantage for players who switch characters frequently but a definite win for those players who stick with one favorite character.
8) Priceless storylines, e.g. Ryu ponders the meaning of his fist (yes, really) while Zangief tutors R. Mika on "Muscle Spirit" (which is NOT a brand of cheap Russian vodka).
9) Cross-platform support for PC and PS4 greatly increases the player pool for matches.
10) Guile is cooler than ever, Cammy is hotter than ever and Birdie is uglier than ever (wait, I guess that last one's not really a plus!)
OPPORTUNITIES (HINT: CAPCOM, here are ways you can transform SFV into a truly AMAZING game):
1) 2x2 Online Tag Team matches: Two players face off against another pair of players with similar skills. Players can tag their partner to help them out during a match and the team with the last player standing wins.
2) Faster Online Match Launch and Loading: It seems to take at least 60 seconds from the time you are paired with an opponent until the time a match actually starts. By comparison, USFIV takes under 30 seconds.
3) ALL additional content should be purchasable with fight money.
4) At least one new, free DLC story mode introduced every six months.
5) Launch at least four new characters every six months (I want to see Fei Long, Akuma and Poison soon!)
6) The current Critical Arts system (Critical Arts are akin to Ultra Combos in USFIV) is somewhat underwhelming because each player only has one Critical Art (and some do not look as flashy as they should - yes, I am looking at you, Zangief). CAPCOM needs to give players a choice of at least two Critical Arts (similar to USFIV where yopu could select your Ultra Combo).
7) Vibration support for equipped controllers - this would be a great feature to increase game interactivity i.e. a player can actually "feel" the punches/kicks landed if they have a controller equipped with vibration support.
8) More taunt options and win quotes needed for each character, as in USFIV. Having just one taunt option per character seems woefully lacking!
CONCLUSION:
Was this game worth paying for at launch? Don't ask me, I did not buy it then - but judging from other reviews, it did not sound like a bargain at that time. Is this game worth buying now, especially if on sale? YES!

. Every armor is class locked now. No more heavy bladers or heavy mages, you have to wear what's meant for your class now. This cuts alot of what you could do with stat customization.
-
. To progress in a dungeon you have to do quests, and they consist of "Talk to this bookshelf" "Now go back and talk to this statue" "Now go and talk to a lamp".
-
. They have an english and spanish client, which is awesome. The problem is that it is not client based, but server. This means that if someone links a [CRITICAL RING +2] in the chat with a spanish client you'll see [ANILLO DEL ATAQUE CRITICO +2] even if you're playing with the english client. Same thing for the class names, if someone posts something like "Need AA  for dungeon last spot!!", you have to guess that AA is "Arqueiro Arcano" which is Spanish for FA "Force Archer".
- No more 42 minutes maze dungeons in the story quests.
- Quests now give skill exp, no need to leave your character in the training dummies.
- Skills are grouped in "attack skill" now. No more Attack/magic separation, and grindind those 2 to transcender.
- Good leveling up event. You get free premium, free boosters and free items. If you level at a good pace you have everything to enjoy all the good things that the game has to offer.
-The graphics are still pretty. The skill effects are still up to the best in almost any mmo.
-Combo mode. This game is known for the combo mode, and It's still fun and challenging as it was years ago.
-Amazing soundtrack. It goes from chill music in the cities, to hard rock in action zones, it's awesome.
-GM's appear quite often. They usually show up, announce "GM buff channel9 BI", and you go and get a buff that increases HP and attack for an hour.
-PVP mmo. You can basically PK or PVP anywhere, which is something that every mmo lacks nowadays. It even has a nice nation system between player factions (Capella vs Procyon), and a channel that allows you to kill people literally anywhere, even in the cities.
-Frequent Events. So far. since it launched on steam, there is always an event going on.
I do not recommend this game. Although I have put lots of hours in it, I can assure you it's just nostalgia and the level up event. As soon as the free boosters and items run out, It will be the end for me.
The event will end on the 22nd of march, and if you didnt play and get to atleast level 150 by then, or if you're not thinking of spending hundreds of $ in Cabal, you'll be completely destroyed by the game.

Once you have leveled up your pet, (Common -> Uncommon -> Rare -> Legendary -> Divine), it is virtually impossible to get past a maxed legendary pet without dropping some cash into this game. Overall, this game is hard to get into, but offers some incredible game play that can last you for years.

Where to start with Starbound? Well, I would describe it as a 2D adventure-sandbox game, like Terraria or Minecraft (except it's not 2D). Similar to its predecessors, it has several bosses, procedurely generated terrain and worlds, and BLOCKS. However, while Minecraft focused on the 3D and survival aspects, and Terraria was a king of variety and exploration, Starbound is looking to be a less fantasy, more Sci-Fi version of Terraria on STEROIDS. While I would remark that yes, I prefer Terraria over Starbound currently, the big differences are that Starbound is more Sci-Fi (which I like better) and that its early access, meaning that while yes, it falls under the terrible Steam Early Access curse, it has room to grow, as oppossed to Terraria's developmental silence as of late.
In other words, Terraria is better than Starbound, but only for now. Starbound is still improving, and it's only a matter of time before it usurps the throne.

The game itself is good, it's basically the Lego movie told in a video game and that's a great idea, also, because it's a Lego game, some cinematic moments are really fun and this is cool !
I finished it at 100% with all achievements in 18.5 hours but I took my time so it can be easily finished in 15 or 16 hours only, so the lifetime of the game is really short and poor for a game that was released in 2014...
I got this product for free, one of my friend have gifted me it, but I'd not have paid this game 20€, it don't really worth it.
-The graphic quality is really good actually.
-The character diversity is good, there is many types of abilities for every characters, some can hack, shoot lasers, dynamites or even fly... (and there is way more abilities). And there is, like in a lot of Lego games, some customizable characters which is nice but not really usefull.
-The fact that you can choose your characters in the full character grid whenever in a level is awesome (free play), in older games like Lego Star Wars The Complete Saga it wasn't possible.
-The red bricks are only in the lobbies which is nice so the lobbies are not only here to walk around and the previous "in level" red bricks are replaced with pants which is a good reference to the movie with the "
" show. The other things to colect in the levels are the golden instruction pages which are used to, at the end, build special things in the bonus room.
-Every pants that you can equip has their own effects, like destroying everything, exploding, dancing, etc...
-Sadly on some stages that I found too long, I was a bit bored but I felt that only in 1 stage out of 15 so that's still ok.
-The free camera system is well made for lobbies but not in levels, and that's really pity.
-The bonus room is fun to build your things with the golden instructions, the 10 gold bricks are fun to get but the 1 million studs things is honestly too easy, for example, I had fun completing the 2 similar levels in Lego Star Wars TCS, they took me 30 minutes each.
-Sometimes crashes (still rare).
-It don't really worth 20€.
-15 levels,
-96 characters,
-20 red bricks,
-70 gold bricks,
-75 gold instruction pages,
-15 pants.
I can highly recommend you playing this game with a controller because of some phases like when Emmet need to do constructions following instructions, it can really be easier than with a keyboard.
The Steam achievements with this game are also nice to achieve, some are fun and are references to the movie (48 achievements).
And for the peoples who wants to do speedruns of this game, you can but it will be hard to do in short times because of unskippable little cinematics and construction phases.
I had only some problems while doing alt+tab twice, the game crashed but that's not really frequent.

Sometimes when you delve into the relics of a bygone era, you find amazing masterpieces long forgotten. In other cases, you find games that are so unintentionally funny you can't help but reccomend to everyone you see. In Amerzone's case, it's a surprising mixture of both; hilarious cutscenes with some of the hammiest, cheesiest acting I've ever seen in a game, followed by a genuinely engrossing narrative and dated but impressive artstyle.
The game truly shines when you actually travel to the titular continent with Morrowind-esque enviornments and fascinating creature designs, but even before that, when you aren't listening to the cringeworthy dialogue, the atmosphere build and setup is utterly fantastic. I spent more time than I would like to admit pouring over the comprehensive journal of the explorer, filled with gorgeous artwork and introspective footnotes. I don't want to give too much away because it's such a fascinating Myst-like, but the reason for your journey is actually...decent. The amount of optional lore you can read about from the notes and journals you find are butter on bread, and while this game hasn't aged well visually, there is something endearing about the campy atmosphere and hammy dialogue that managed to enhance my over all intrigue.
This is not for everyone. At all. I would dare say that you would have a far better time if you kept a walkthrough open, but I'm trying to get as far as I can without one. It's about as old school as a point and click can get, but for once I can say the puzzles actually follow a form of logic. If you're curious about the relics of the not-so distant past, this is definitely a gem lost in time. The asking price is insanely cheap as well. It's definitely worth picking up just to form your own opinion of it.

With over 100 hours on record I think I can give a good review on the game.  Please note, I did take some pro's and cons from another review. I wanted this review to be most accurate, and unbiased in order to give the best perspective on the game. Finally, please note, in the "cons that may turn some players off" I am not bashing anyone, but I want to be clear that some things may turn others off form the game, and I would hate to see someone download the game and waste their time ons something that they would hate.
This game most certaintly brings back memories, but it still has its ups and downs. I will be straight forward with pro's and cons and what I beleive they could do with the cons' to fix the game. Before I begin, I beleive that this game has been dummed down so anyone that gives it a solid 5-10 hours can easily get the hang of it especially since they give you 200% exp and skill exp boosters for 20 days.
Pros:
-Decent music
- Class variety
- Cute female outfits
- Unique weapons not usually seen in other mmos (Gladiator Chakra)
- Easy to use combat system
- Dated Graphics, so anyone on just about any platform can play
- Easy to play
-Level up quickly
-Easy to make money
- added quests (from orginial game)
- more players ( since added onto steam)
-Unique combo system
Cons:
-"Clunky UI, couldn't really find everything I needed and most of the windows were almost too big."
Observation- this hasn't been an issue with the acutal version of the game. This will probably be fixed with an update later on.
-"Simplified Questing, In 2 hours of play, only one quest was a fetch quest, the others were nothing but hunt this and dungeon that or warp here."
Suggestion- the game has always had this problem.  I would love to see differnt types of quests, but due to how the game is formatted I do not believethat it would be possible without a rehaual of the game. Since Cabal II has been released I do not see it happening. The only thing I could reccommend is doing daily's, dungons, and grinding if questing isn't doing it for you.
-Bugs specifically crashing- A lot of the time the game crashes, it is incredibly frustrating when I am in the middle of a quest and it crashes.
Observation- EstSoft is really good at fixing their game. I beleive that this will be fixed in due time.
-Everyhting will attack you- Something that turned me off while I played the Wizard class was that I needed to spend an immense amount of Alz(money) on hp potions becuase everything is hostile towards you. I hope they fix it in the future.
Suggestion- I think this is obvious, make less monsters attack you.
Cons that may turn some players off:
- "Automated fighting, when I played as a Shielder, my skills worked automatically, I don't know how I got it to work but it made the game even harder to enjoy. Some might like that, but I didn't."

I wish I could say something good about this game, as it made up between 5 to 8 years of my life playing in EU's Mars server, but I sort of can't.
Despite this being a pretty little mmo that has some flashy graphics, mildly interesting story, and ok pvp (which you can't say about many other mmos), its riddled with problems.
Graphics are pretty ok, they look good enough along with the visuals, the sounds are pretty good to be honest, but the game takes a bit hit in the gameplay.
People who play the game might convince you otherwise, but the truth is that the only way to be good at the game, is with good gear. Nothing else.
Sure there might be a few things you need to know, like tips and tricks for the dungeons, which some might need practice for, but in the end, gear will dictate wether you can do anything at all. Both in PvE and PvP. Especially in PvP.
The second, is that if you're rich, you can pretty much buy all your equipment. By buying game store gear with real life money and selling the stuff on the auction house, you can pretty much make a ton of money and buy almost anything you need. I even shamelessly admit I did it myself, because...
Problem No.3, and personaly the biggest problem with it, the game is a severe grindfest based PURELY on luck.
Remember how I said PvP is very based in gear? Critical hits are dictated by critical hit ratio, and if you have none, you're screwed, and if you have the average (between 45 and 51%) it will pretty much be a "if you crit, you win" situation, which sometimes comes in bags of 9 out of 10, or 2 out of 10. Same goes for enchanting armor, where you'll spend BILLIONS of ingame money to upgrade something ONCE if you're really unlucky, and the same also applies to drops, where you're either lucky enough to enter a dungeon and get a good piece of gear that you can sell (don't fool yourself into thinking you'll easily find good stuff you can wear) or unlucky enough to do the same dungeon 1000 times and never get anything good whatsoever. I've seen it happen, and funny enough, the game has titles for people who go into dungeons that many times.
There are also botters, hackers, and gold sellers ingame as usual.
The conclusion?
Despite a fun little game, its chalk full of problems. You CAN have some fun in it, but after a while, it will most likely get on your nerves.

First off, I want to start off by saying I have had a great time playing this game. I used to play games like Age of Empires and Age of Mythology back when I was a kid, and this brings back some nostalgia. Overall, the gameplay, graphics and soundtrack are very satisfying even for an Early Access Game.
Pros:
-Graphics are crisp and clean, with a very unique feel.
-Gameplay is engrossing and I enjoy the territory system where you are only allowed to build a certain amount of buildings in a given territory, I feel this increases the level of strategy on where to place your buildings.
-Surrounding areas on start up change you style of gameplay and strategy as you must adjust to the resources that are around you. Each territory provides an advantage to colonizing it and provides certain resources that you need in order to progress with your civilization.
-Season changes create scenarios in which you must make sure you have your resources allocated correctly in order to survive. Winter increases the consumption of wood to keep your villagers warm and decreases the amount of food production so you must prepare in advance.
-Random events such as blizzards and earthquakes provide scenarios that you must be prepared for in order to thrive.
-Clans seem to be rather unique and have their own advantages/disadvantages.
Cons:
-Game lags out from the transition to summer to winter and from winter to summer.
-Lack of military units makes combat very linear, would like to see introduction of more units and maybe introduction of clan specific units.
-Victory conditions seem way too easily achievable. I never even get a chance to win by domination because the other victory conditions are always achieved by accident before I can even wipe out other clans. This always leads to me clicking the 'keep playing' button because I feel like I had just started and was no where near achieving victory.
-No game modes that allow you to choose what victory conditions are available. This would be especially useful in multiplayer I feel because some of the victory conditions are just too easy.
-Not much depth to the gameplay, wish there was more upgrading features with both the buildings as well as the villagers. A leveling system of some sort would also make the game much more addictive.
-No campaign and multiplayer at the time of writing this review but the developers stated this will be coming soon.
-Only three current clans but this is also something the developers stated they will creating more of in the future.
All in all, I would recommend this game to my friends. If you are a fan of RTS games or are just looking for a new game to get into. At this time of review, at only ~$17.00 I believe I have already gotten my money worth and the developers are supposedly coming out with more content within the coming months. This game has a lot of potential and I am excited to see where it leads. I hope this information helps the development of this game.

Well, considering the first wave of updates has come, I think it's time to make a complete review out of this game. Let's divide pros, cons and also neutrals apart to make things clearer.
First of all, on many points, principal or secondary, Street Fighter V (SFV) looks really different next to Ultra Street Fighter IV (USFIV) which was for me and a lot of other people, a reference in terms of fighting. But anyway let's roll.

►Graphism ; More colorful, smoother and even better animated than USFIV. Let's also notice the camera and effects improvements especially on Critical Arts.
►PC Gear required ; Well when they said NVidia GTX960 recommended I wasn't excepting to run this game at 60 FPS Max with 50°C degrees. It's quite overrated, so logically, you should be able to run it easily with NVidia GTX570.
►Cross-Platform ; Great idea, nicely executed. You can play with you PS4 friend online even if you play on PC.
►Soundtracks ; Absolutely awesome, brand new progressive metal theme and orchestral revisited themes make some really nice quality music. Let's still note that some characters or stages themes are still bad but, ugh, music taste lawl.
►Cinematic story mode ; Well I recommend you to check reviews on the Cinematic story mode's Steam page because you will access to more detailed statements about it. I will just say I really enjoyed it and it was a pleasant experience for the SF universe.

►Story mode ; Still, no arcade gamemod, which is kind of, ugh, bloody weird. So the story mode is basically a chain of 3 super-easy fights including fixed image cut-scenes and some animations where you can learn your character prologue to introduce him into the cinematic story mode.
►Menu ; I got a bit lost a first, I looks like Windows 8.1 Welcome screen with the apps, so if you used to USFIV and classic menus don't jumpscare on it lawl.

►Options saving ; In other games, when you set up setting for a gamemod it normally will be saved next time you will use it. In SFV, all colors, costumes, training settings will not be saved so you a to set them up every time. Take note that this saving system was featured in USFIV.
►Survival ; Salty is my second name but this game mode made me so salty. Why ? Because you need to complete the easy, normal and hard survivals to unlock colors, even you bought the costume on the shop for a few dollars. This is one of the biggest mistakes they made in SFV. If you don't want to bother with this mode, you have got to stay with only two colors on your costume no matter how much time you played with your main character. The problem is that this concept is awful for casual players (I am not a casual but intermediate level player - only on USFIV-), it means they can't unlock those colors for their favorite character. But check the following con and you will understand my salt, and your future salt, about this gamemode.
►AI difficulty ; One of the worst thing with SFV. Going to 8 types of difficulty modes from 1-3 potato, 4 advanced potato, 5 weak, 6 somewhat balanced, 7-8 input reading competitive pro player. So basically you will have to fight input reading AI in survival to unlock colors during 50 rounds straight with no second chance! And no I am not exaggerating considering the other day at a french competitive tournament, a really advanced Vega player said unlocking the Vega's colors was an absolute hell of difficulty. The AI, it's like having a “No Fun Allowed” robot in front of you that just want you to change game. You will on the one hand destroy them too easily or getting destroyed my them. There's no middle
►Colors system ; You heard it earlier, it's awful, Capcom could have do way better because the awful survival is the only way to obtain some colors. But you're now able to buy those colors with huge packs for your money or FM of course.
►No support for keyboard inputs rebidding ; What a banger, rare are the games were you can't change your buttons so you have to play with “GHJK-BNM,”. You can use third part script program but use at your own risk, just like me. "FOOK DA POWLISE".
►QWERTY keyboards club only ; If like me you own a AZERTY keyboard you have to swith between AZERTY and QWERTY when you're about to play SFV because some button will not exist like Heavy Kick.
►Local PlayerVSPlayer ; You can't basicly on PC use your keyboard and your friend using his controller because the two controller will be set as Player 1. A lot of people seems to have this issue on PC like I saw on Reddit. You can still check Reddit for a soft called XBOX360ce.
►Fighter profile ; Creating an account is your first step. But, my big "meh" about it, is that you can't change back your country and also your time zone, nor (at least one time) your ID. It's a detail but make sure you made no mistakes during the time you create your account.
►Fight Money and Premium content ; Fight Money is the in game currency you win by completing part of the solo part of the game and wining ranked matches. That's simple. With those you can buy story costume, alternative costumes, exclusives colors, titles and characters. Each characters like Juri and Ibuki-san ;3, will cost 100,000 FM or nearly 6$. Costumes cost 40,000 FM and 4$. Considering in USFIV, 5 costumes with a big load of colors was 5$, it's overpriced. Notice the ranked matched won't help you win FM cuz' you will win only 50 FM per victory.
►Overall Gameplay ; Salty and frustrating. Balance do exist between characters but some of them have been nearly dead last the whole time like F.A.N.G. or Juri. Meaty system is so important it sucks and V-System is a big "meh". Overly offensive gameplan. Way way way way to much setup based and, don't forget what Floe (pro gamer from the fighting game community) said "You now start to worry on the guy who has the more health left"
►Online experience ; Annoying and randoms Cammy, Guile, Laura and Mika every time. Awful netcode. No details needed about rollbacks which happen when your opponent got a sightly unstable connexion.
►Characters ; Except the balance problem I already said, they picked the best of the best. Which basicly means the worst and the most annoying to fight against (even a CPU) like Mika, Rashid or Laura. Let's not forget the lame ones like Alex. Thus, Capcom wants to put only new characters like Ed which is completly lame. To note the new redesgin for most of the existing fighter who turned up to suck like Alex Ibuki Akuma Vega and Birdie
►Support ; Asked for a name change directly and kindly to the support. Told me they will absolutly take care of it, never ragequitted, and my name were never changed.

It's time for another Zup! installment.  In this Zup! there's less achievements than 3, but still a lot of them.  Also there's a new block, but it's not too earth-shattering.  If you haven't played Zup! before, you could start with this one, but there isn't much for people that played the last three installments.  It's still fun though, so I recommend it.

Zup is a sort of junk food that also happens to be very high in vitamins.  Of course, by junk food, I mean video games, and by vitamins I mean achievements.  Now, Zup 4 is rather conservative with its 555 achievements compared to Zup 3 with 1708, but the Zup experience has always been about lots of reward for little effort.
Imagine you go to work in the morning.  If you actually do go to work in the morning, you won't need to imagine this part, but just play along, ok?  You sit down at your desk and start writing an email.  The twist is, that with every word you write in that email your coworkers shout “Hooray, you did it!”  and shower you with confetti.  If that's how your work day actually goes, well, don't quit your day job, but for most of us, that would seem like overkill.
Yet this is the way of the Zup.  Just about every click is rewarded with at least three achievements, each an everlasting testament to your total mastery of video games in general.  Does that cheapen the meaning of achievements as a measure of skill?  Oh, you bet it does.  Is it still fun?  Yes.  Yes it is.
So sure, you can play Super Meat Boy for months trying to get that most elusive achievement.  Meanwhile, I'll be here getting 2610 of them from my Zups.  Guess who wins?  That's right.  No one.  Play what you want and just be glad you don't have to shovel confetti off of your desk every day.

Amerzone is one of those gaming experiences that will stick with me probably for the better part of my life. It's a point-and-click adventure game a la Myst, but it's pretty different. It's not puzzle heavy at all, in fact I think there are only 5 major puzzles in the entire game. It's all about the story and the people in it. And it's a beautiful story about a story:
You start off by happening upon a dying man's last request. He asks you to return a sacred egg to Amerzone. All other agencies have turned down his requests for an expedition to go back to Amerzone. Not only that, but the country (or continent? not totally sure) is going through a dictatorship with a lot of bad results. There's a dash of steampunk and a dash of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle influence in the game, but this game really does feel like a story on its own. I didn't have any problems with how old the game is (I didn't play it when it first came out). The only rela problems I had with it were the parts where you had to traverse the jungle or a swamp and I'd get lost a bunch of times, but not enough to stop me from playing.
You, of course, end up completing the old adventurer's request, but the real special thing about this game is that while you are going on your adventure to finish his, you're basically tracking his footprints from decades ago and seeing how much things have changed. Instead of a busy town with lots of people in a trade market, you come upon a barren desolate town, a ghost town, where a couple of policemen drink their meaningless lives away. There's a lot being said here about culture and knowing your roots. The country is basically trying to fast-track itself into the developed world but by doing so is completely ignoring its rich heritage.
TLDR:
This game is like a quiet poem that was whispered to you by someone old who passed away, and  you never really know if what they said was real or just a story. If you like games that are all about atmosphere and don't mind that this game is old then I recommend it. Also of course if you like Syberia you'll enjoy this. It's not very long, but I found the experience very rewarding.
Cheers.

While not inherently a bad game per se, this is easily the worst of all the latest iteration of LEGO games (i.e. those with voice acting and an open-world-ish structure).  It's still a LEGO game, so it's still fun, but it suffers from major issues that other games in the series don't have (or don't have in such proportions):
- The Hub worlds are pointless and confusing.  There's nothing to do save for a few easy puzzles that allow you to collect the prized red bricks.  Otherwise, there are no side-quest, no races, nothing else to do.  The highest challenge is to try to navigate their preposterous structure, for which the camera and aribtrary invisible walls will be a constant problem.  You'll hate Cloud Cuckooland the worse.
- The two-hour movie is painfully padded to fit a 10-15 hour game (depending if you're hunting for achievements or not).  In consequence, if you haven't watched you'll soon forget what the story is about.  Terribly, a major plot twist of the film is absent from this game for no explanation, which renders the entire thing into a generic adventure.  Again, those who haven't watched the film will be at a loss.
- Free Play is broken.  Even though the entire point of Free Play is to be able to breeze through a scene with any character of your choosing in order to get all the hidden items, many times you're forced to play entire parts the exact way you'd do it in normal play or the stage will lock and won't advance.
- This is probably the buggiest of the LEGO games, and that's saying a lot, because they're all incredibly buggy.  Expect being forced to restart a stage or maybe even the entire game if you want to 100% it.  Speaking of which, if you're going for all achievements, expect to waste a lot of time doing stuff that's not fun, just repetitive.
- The game is confusing in several areas besides camera movement.  Character unlocks happen without rhyme or reason.  Even with the proper red bricks unlocked you'll still have trouble trying to find all the secrets, since some of the arrows don't actually point at what you're supposed to do, or even at where the secret will appear.  The game doesn't bother to explain the point of the unlockable pants or how some abilities are used (and what characters have them).  There's a lot of trial and error.
- This might be a nitpick, but the game's main theme music is completely uninspired.  While generally LEGO games beat you with a musical theme until you get sick of it, this one gets you sick of it almost as soon as it starts.
Still, there are some good things.  Gameplay is as good as ever, with a lot of interesting new abilities.  Dialogue-wise, this is one of the funniest games in the series (and it retains the same voice cast from the film).  Instruction building is a neat way to get some money early in the game (though it quickly becomes a nuisance as soon as you got any multiplier red brick).
So, despite all its flaws, I still recommend the game... provided it's at a hefty discount.  Don't even think to pay the current (as of this writing, $19.99) price.

This isn't a bad game, although definitely dated.  It perhaps hasn't aged as well as some older games, but it's worth a play if you like the genre.  It did seem rather short to me and the story fell apart a bit in places, so I would recommend getting it in a bundle if possible or on sale.
Graphically very pretty for the time period it was created in, although somewhat fuzzy/pixelated on a modern system in places.  Nothing game breaking.  There was some minor annoyance in some parts that seemed too dark to see what was needed to progress, but that was very few places.  Character models probably aged the worst, but there are very few of them so no matter.  Animal models still look quite good; for example, the critters playing fetch with my grappling hook late in the game were delightfully well done.
The format is point-and-click in what I like to call "freestyle Myst" style, in that as you move around from spot to spot, you stand still in a static location as you do in Myst or Dark Fall, but you have free 360 degree freedom of view and click the movement arrows to move from spot to spot.  There is limited inventory and the interface is a little clunky, but again, nothing that is game breaking.
The story is straightforward but does leave a few holes and has some sketchy logic, but it was enjoyable.  While I do normally like games that leave me some room to mull over what happened and what it may mean, this one could have used some more detail and fleshing out of story and characters.  I had some questions that were more than just "give the player something to think about" problems and more "I think the player should have this information" problems.
Anyway, I will recommend this because there is no "in the middle" option.  Given a choice between yes or no, I'd say yes, even though it hasn't aged as well as other games, because the story is interesting and the fantastical pseudo-Amazon setting is pretty fun to experience.  If you like the genre, give it a shot especially if you can find it on sale.

The first time I got Starbound I managed to "finish" the game so quickly that it didn't last an saturday afternoon. Expected from early access. Now, years later, it doesn't seem to have changed much other than it takes slightly longer, because now there are missions between the tiers. They aren't difficult nor are they that interesting.
The first game of this sandbox type I played was Terraria and I played that in it's early stages too. The difficulty was higher but not torturing but more importantly, you felt the need to connect with your world. If you went to far in one direction or too deep you ended up fighting monsters outside of your current combat strengh. In Starbound the transition from a weak explorer to a stronger one is very clearly cut. It's switching the planet you're exploring. And it's not like you can go to higher tiers earlier to seek out a challenge because you'll end up dealing with constant health loss due to artificially giving the next tier of planet something you later deal with passively by progression.
Starbound had the need to stay warm in early stages and it slowed you down. Apparently enough people complained for this to be removed. But that's exactly what made Terraria great and Starbound badly designed now: You explore too quickly. In Terraria you had little means of moving around until you were well into higher tiers. In Starbound you get doublejump, anti-fall damage and grapple hooks (good idea but it speeds up everything) and then you blast your way through worlds. No need to build anything either. You put the crafting stations on your ship and that's that. Either you love spending time on housing and then do it or you completely skip it. That might sound like a nice thing. Do what you want and skip everything else. But one of the most important parts of a task is to have a purpose. Good design creats the need
desire to do something, which Starbound fails to do. If you enjoy housing building there are better ways to do it. If you enjoy exploring there are better ways to do it. If you enjoy combat there are a lot better ways to do it.
Starbound had potential and probably still has. But it doesn't seem like the developer is moving in a direction which attacks there points. The ease of access to everything doesn't make for a good game. It makes for a good level editor but that's not what Starbound wants to be or would perform well at either.

To be frank, this game is not for everyone, and this game is simply not for me.
And before commenting, please read the full review first.
Before getting this game, I played the first binding of isaac and I had many of issues with the game. One of those issues was the randomization feature of items. While randomizing the room layouts in the game is a very cool touch, I was not okay with how the items were arranged at times.
Beating the game required luck and dodging skill, meaning you would need to get really good items if you wanted to finish one your the many playthroughs. As for me, I am terrible at bullet hell games, but the first binding of isaac wasn't that bad in that department. The whole luck mechanic the game revolves around though is ridiculous.
The worst feeling I get is trying to beat the final boss after countless losses before, only to die and start over again. It took me several tries before actually beating the game the first time, only to find out I have to beat it several more times to unlock more stuff. At the time of making this review, I've beaten this game about 9 times.
Then later, a friend bought me and the afterbirth dlc for this game, encouraging me to give this game a try. I did, and I enjoyed this game for about a month until I just stopped playing it.
There is a lot of things fixed in this game comparing it to the first, but as well as more problems.
One lingering issue is how there are more bullet hell-like bosses in this game at which I have more trouble with than I should be.
Many things that were added to the game were unneeded and put in for the sake of the game's difficulty. And with the luck factor still in play in the game, I was constantly discouraged to play this game after a lot of my losses. And at the moment, I've only beaten this game about 4 times (including 2 challenges).
This is by all means not a bad game, but I feel like too many people come to this games made by Edmund McMillen expecting to have a grand time. That's not what I got. I'm betting Edmund's a cool guy, but I haven't really liked his games all that much because of their absurd difficulty.
If you want to be frustrated and try to beat a really hard game, this game is for you, but if you are think you aren't built for it, wait till you think you're ready.

However, like many have said, it needs a campaign. I don't agree that it's a cost issue. It doesn't need to be theatrical cut scenes and voice overs and scripts. It just needs to be progressive with longer battles. The current Galactic War mode is just repetitive skirmishes. And each skirmish ends just as your starting to get into it. Far too quick.
What I would have loved to have seen is a campaign that...
*got progressively harder, more complex
*new tech unlocks as you work through each mission (this happens in Galactic War but the unlocks are completely random)
*longer battles that require you to dig in and hold your ground, maybe starting small against a large enemy base.
*varying mission types which encourage/force you to try diferent strategies and different unit types
It is a shame, because this type of gameplay is my favourite, But I enjoyed Total Annihilation (1997) and Supreme Commander (2007) much more.
A neutral  score option would work for me on this however, as I can't, it is negative. This is more because the game falls short of what it could have been and what I wanted it to be.

Northgard is a real time strategy game with some twists on the genre. At this time it only includes one play mode - singleplayer scenarios versus 1-3 bots. This does not fare well with replayability, but I'm sure it will be improved as the game develops (there are two aditional modes greyed out, campaign and multiplayer). This and (only) three clans are also the only real factors that show the early access status, as I haven't encountered any real bugs and the game ran completely smoothly at all times (except for a small hiccup every time seasons change).
First off, despite looking kind of like Banished, Northgard plays completely differently. It's much more fast paced, with shorter sessions that last around 2 hours each. How does that work out, you might ask. Quite well, actualy. The goal isn't that much building your settlement and slowly expanding, like typical town building strategies have you do. Instead, each structure has a purpuse and you can build a limited amount on each area you conquer. This is another interesting thing about Northgard, the map isn't "open", but instead seperated into small zones, each with its own resources and (sometimes) enemies. This does limit freedom for people that like slowly building towns, but as I've mentioned, Northgard isn't about that anyway.
There are different resource nodes scattered around the map and you use those to improve your production. There's a forest for wood, stone and iron deposits for stone and iron, food nodes (such as fields, fish and sheep) for food and ancient "holy" grounds for lore. There is some other stuff you can discover, but I won't get into detail. Food and wood are the most important resources, as you need both to survive during winter. If you run out of either of them - good luck making it till spring, you're most likely fu****.
In the style of the Civilization series, there are different ways to win. You don't simply need to eliminate every opponent (you can do this, of course), but can also win trough trade, lore and fame. There are also some victory conditions that you can capture. What does this allow? Every game will be unique, since the map is randomly generated each time. You will sometimes get lucky and have rich areas around your starting area, or get extremely unlucky and barely get any food. You will need to base your strategy around this and it makes winning very satisfying.
Let's get to combat. It's really barebone at the moment, with only one type of melee units (alongside two other "hero" units) and four neutral monster types. I do hope that monster variety increases over time and I would love to see some other interesting units, such as archers and new monsters. If you're all about combat, you won't really enjoy what Northgard has to offer (at this time).
As the last thing, I'd like to talk about replayability. Because of a limit in variety, it can get stale really fast for some people. While some will keep on playing for hours on end, others will get bored after finishing a couple of games because you basicly do the same thing over and over and the games are usualy over before you uncover the whole map. The fast tempo and mirror maps could make it a good competitive game too, since randomly generated maps are the only luck factor. With premade maps, I see Northgard as a competitive title, however since scouting is a large factor, I'm not quite sure how that would work out.
Summary:
I really like what Northgard has to offer. It's a fun, fast paced strategy game that gets a lot of things right. This alongside an interesting look and polished gameplay make for a great base game, where the developers will build upon. But some aspects are lacking at the moment. The maps could be bigger, combat system could be improved and there could be more variety. However, the game just arrived in early access. If the developers keep up the good work, I see this as a great game.

Oh dear...this game makes me frustrated.  The game randomly quits and exits every 15-20 mins.  I finally found a solution to the problem by deactivated taptouch.exe from task manager.  Then I come to find out this is a known issue from beta!  I bought the game on sale for $27...and I'm still miffed about the bugs.  I can't imagine players who paid the full $60 and are still dealing with known bugs from the test stage!  I'm not sure who the team at Capcom who is suppose to be on top of this, but I'm a pretty dissapointed SF/Capcom fan.  Make it right...geez.
**Edit** 11/11/16
It seems the random crashes have stopped..  I no longer have to deactiviate the taptouch.exe from my task manager.  I can actually recommend this game for Street Figher Fans....but with a condition.  There is no Arcade mode in this game...at least not in the way it existed in previous Street Fighter games.  There is a character story mode and a general story mode, but they're definitely not the same thing as an arcade mode.  The character mode is about 3-4 rounds each character and really that's it.  It gives you a taste of each character's background and their style.  Since it's about 3-4 rounds long, the only real purpose it serves is to drum up some credits towards purchasing another character.  The general story mode also provides credits, but is significantly longer than the character story mode.  However, the general story forces you to play between different characters after each cutscene and doesn't provide the consistency for you to actually practice your character with.
There is a trial and practice mode....which is great, but once again, they are no substition for an arcade mode.  I liked the arcade mode because it allowed me to fight against multiple opponents without having to surf through the settings menu.
So, if you've always enjoyed the arcade mode in fighting games, I can't recommend SFV to you.  The other modes are excellent tools at honing your skills with the character of your choice....but having an arcade mode was an easy way to test your skills against a variety of character controlled by a PC ai.  I think most casual players would like the comfort of consistently beating a PC ai at a high difficultly level before moving onto human competitors online.  So until an arcade mode has been implemented in the style and fashion that fighting games are known for...this is still a thumbs down.
**UPDATE 03/25/16**
After having put in over 40 hours into the game...I must admit I enjoy it much more now.  The lack of an arcade mode is not a big deal to me anymore.  In fact, I don't even care if Capcom never add an arcade mode at this point.  I never did mention gameplay.  Well, gone are the contrivances of Ultra SF IV...and thank god for that!  SFV has a relatively smooth learning curve and finding an opponent takes anywhere between 5-10 minutes for casual and ranked (in the US).  I wouldn't recommend using the Battle Lounge for the time being.  The connection are typically spotty with other players and you have no way of filtering out players with high latency for you other than turning down matches when your turn is up in the lounge.  I wish there were some way to add friends instead of using the Favorites menu as a means to invite other players into a fight.  I also wish there were a way to just select a player from a list and challenge them to a match.  The good news is that most of my complaints may be addressed with an upcoming balance + CFN update this April.  We'll see how that comes together.  Otherwise, I think I can safely recommend SFV to fighting gamers out there now.  The roster is considerably larger and there is a greater variety of styles to choose from.  Ken, Ibuki, and Guile are my personal favorites....but I'm sure you'll find your own.  The game is also 40 bucks now...still pricey considering the DLC...but luckily, fight money for at least 5 characters can easily be earned without having to play a single bout online.  The online function is still spotty...but it's not horrible.  It's best to filter players who have 4-5 bars for an increased pool of players with decent latency against yourself.  Overall, I will now change my recommendation of this game from a thumbs down to a thumbs up.
**UPDATE 08/24/17**
So it has been over a year since my last update.  I've learned a few new things about this game that has already been voiced by other players.  I'll go ahead and parrot or repeat them here.  The game tends to revolve around the knock-down/wakeup game.  In other words, what you do when you're waking up from a knockdown is vitally important...do you block, do you attempt a throw tech, do you check with lights, do you jump, do you burn a bar or meter?  Oftentime though, you've only got 1 of 2 choices....block or tech?  That's why Street Fighter V is considered widely by many as a guessing game...or fifty-fifty.  If you block, you might get thrown.  If you attempt to tech, you might get smacked by a meatie or crushed.  Therefore, once you're in a position of defense, you're acutally in a position of weakness because control of the situation is afforded to the player who is on the offense.  If you guess right, you're awarded with an opportunity to get back to neutral, stop offensive momentum of your opponent and make a comeback.  I'd say most of your time playing other players will be revolved around this basic mechanic.  I can't say that I'm a fan of it.....but I also can't say that I hate it.  It does make the game harder to enjoy if at the higher levels of play, you're constantly reduced to either making a guess or making your opponents guess.  Although, when you guess correctly, it's glorious.  I wish there were a way to retain the high risk and reward while also centering the game around reaction time, skills, and reads.  That isn't to say that 50/50s are not impressive when players make the right reads....I just want a little less of it.  Overall, I can still recommend this game.  Wish there were some way to take care of the weird Memory Leak bug when exiting the game from Survivial or Training mode.

Amazing game, absolutely worth both your time and money, and the only thing I regret is not buying the full DLC pack right away.
I started out with some missions and had some conversations with a pig mask on my head that made me laugh more than it should. Then I discovered the game isn't just for laughs, although it has that in spades - the story is excellent too. I also had the pleasure of experiencing the awesome Batman: Arkham Asylum style combat in the game, including putting a guy through aquarium glass in a night club, breaking legs and arms, and just generally being a wrecking machine of a fighter. Good times, really good times. But there is more.
Because there are times in the game that are not only good, they're almost transcendental.
One evening, I woke up after a hard day/night before. I had some texts waiting on my phone, from both police investigators and thugs, and said to myself it was going to be alright, even though I was playing both sides. I got out of my apartment, picked up a car and started driving to my next mission. And then...
I found myself just keeping on driving around the city.
Time had stopped.
I no longer sensed the room where my sorry gamer butt was actually sitting because I was no longer there.
I'm in Hong Kong - for real. I can't stop driving. It's raining and the reflection from the neon lights in my car, the fan-♥♥♥♥ing-tastic music from the radio, the streets and back alleys, the people, the crowds - I'm completely immersed.
And like throwing game money on pimped up outfits (that actually gives you bonuses sometimes, so they're more worth than just for "show"), and awesome, fun, expensive cars, I'm looking forward to throw a little bit of real money on United Front again - this time to buy the whole DLC pack to continue my stay in Hong Kong. It's been a journey like nothing else and it has been the best digital vacation ever.
Recommended with all my heart - it rivals some of the best games I have ever played in my life.

Coffee Stain Studious pushes the tower defense series with this brilliant addition to the Sanctum series. Sanctum 2 takes the brilliant aspects from the first one and pushes it further with a much more dynamic and fluid campaign.
On the planet of Loek III an infestation begins. An alien species, which is actually burrowed into the planet has awoken and it is the job your squad to stop them. Skye Autumn, Sweet Autumn, SiMo, Haigen Hawkins, and Tsygan form a squad and work to protect the cores from collapsing. The cores defend and power the cities, but it’s not long till you figure out that they cores are not everything they seem.
The original campaign includes four sectors each composed of four missions. The sectors include: Facility, Rocky Fields, Giant Trees, and Swamp. In each of these sectors you must complete a tower defense on a strategic field, using one of the five playable heroes. The game defaults to open party meaning anyone can join your game, but you can switch it to private if you want to play alone. I always found Tower Defenses to be a single player event, unless you operate separate lanes, as clashing strategies can ruin the games value. The campaign allows you to add “Feats of Strength” which increase the difficulty, but also add to the XP bonus from each round. In order to complete the game 100% you must complete each map with all five Feats of Strength (excluding Introduction). I played Sanctum by myself and found I was rarely playing the FPS portion after the first level, although by adding Feats of Strength you will no longer be able to sit around and watch. The levels have lots of secrets hidden within them including arcade machines or even just random little subsections. The campaign essentially constitutes the entire game as there is no sandbox option.
Unlike traditional Tower Defenses Sanctum offers you the chance to jump in as an FPS to help control creep flow. Each map you complete offers you XP which allows you to level up your squad, unlike in a traditional RPG fashion no matter who you play in Sanctum all the squad members are the same level. As you progress through the game this means you unlock new towers, better weapons, and special abilities. The towers and the weapons are not equal, so as you progress through the game you’ll probably find yourself using the same kit. Eventually when you reach level 40 you unlock both weapons allowing you to select both of the characters weapons making only their abilities matter. Luckily the vast amount of character customization allows you to play the game however you desire.
Sanctum 2 has four game content DLC packs: The Last Stand, The Pursuit, Ruins of Brightholme, and Road to Elysion. These DLC packs include four sectors: Coastline, Brightholme, Outskirts, and Arc Islands. These essentially double the length of the campaign and sixteen new missions. The story of Sanctum 2 is actually not over after the initial campaign is completed and in order to figure out exactly what happens on Loek III you must finish the DLC. After completing sector four, Swamp, you are left off exactly where the DLC begins. Each DLC pack is $3.99, which is actually quite expensive seeing as it adds very little content (a couple enemies and a few new maps). The Last Stand, Arc Islands, offers a level with essentially unlimited waves that get progressively more difficult. If you were looking for essentially a sandbox mode, this would be the closest you can get.
The game is default multiplayer, this means that when you start your campaign anyone can join you on your mission and help you out. I didn’t realize this until after I started and some random person was in my mission. As a result I backed out kicked them out of my part and changed my game settings to private. For those who are interested Sanctum 2 multiplayer offers an incredibly easy multiplayer system that is almost flawless.
If you are a fan of First Person Shooters then Sanctum 2 is a good game for you. If you are a fan of tower defenses then Sanctum 2 is a good game for you. Sanctum 2 is a fun game which offers strategy and action bundled together as you defend a core objective from waves of minions. The DLC adds additional missions to the game, which if you can get on a sale are completely worth it. The character customization and leveling system really allows you to choose how you play the game. Despite not having unlimited blocks like the original, Sanctum 2, requires you to focus on short-term strategy at the start then eventually long-term as you progress past the first few waves. I would recommend Sanctum 2 for anyone who felt like the original lacked in FPS and character development.
Pros:
+Character customization
+Smooth and clean graphics
+Large variety of minions that require you to be diverse.
+Loads of maps
+DLC which adds more levels, story, and enemies.
+Great multiplayer
+FPS as well as TD
+Secrets in levels
+Great level design
+Bosses which change the dynamic of the maze design.
+Various levels which require different strategies (FPS intensive vs TD intensive)
+On map allies (they may not do much damage, but it looks nice to have some teammates)
+You can upgrade towers beyond their maximum level, essentially increasing there damage beyond the upgrade levels
Cons:
-After beating Sanctum 2, The Last Stand, you cannot skip the credits.
-Multiplayer is defaulted on
-There is no just plain simple sandbox map
-You are limtied to the number of base bricks you can place (you get anywhere from 5-15 per wave) but eventually you start geting 0
-You can only place around 15 towers per map (this varies on the map I believe).
-You can no longer upgrade your weapons (although they seem to scale by themselves)
-To get 100% essentially requires co-operative play.

Starbound is an sandbox game that make some of the others look kind of bland in comparison. It has cutscenes(WIP), Lore books, multi-species playable characters, and an entirely infinite universe. In truth, those individuals have just not dug deep enough (so to speak) into the game's mechanics. When you get far enough into the world, the game eventually warps you a few blocks back. Anyway, I'd already really recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a decent, story-driven, fairly lighthearted sandbox. I have never played the original planetary annihilation, and I have only played this one for about two hours but I can already tell you a few things about this game right away:
Pros:
-If you enjoyed any of the Supreme Commander games, trust me, you will feel right at home with this one and you will love it. Welcome home
-Lots of different units, strategies, and mechanics to play and experiment with
-(Mostly) Easy to learn difficult to master
-You can play in short bursts. My recent matches have lasted as short as 10 minutes. I expect that will get longer as I progress, but don't get me wrong, they were very engrossing 10 minutes.
-Soundtrack is excellent. It just complements the space theme so well.
Cons:
-There is no real story. Some history is included with each fight, but no long lasting characters to love or hate.
-The hardest part of this game is the camera. If you want to get really good you have to get the hotkeys down really well. Controlling 3 dimensional camera views around multiple circular objects is just difficult.
The campaign mode is a double edged sword. On one hand, there is infinite replayability, but on the other hand, there is just not as much uniqueness. Overall it feels like a rouge-like RTS, which is both good and bad. Depends how you feel about those kinds of games.
Overall, I would certainly recommend it despite its setbacks. It has been loads of fun so far, and I am genuinely hyped to play more.
*EDIT* So I have played 17 hours now. My initial recommendation still stands. I have not played multiplayer yet because I am not really a competitive person, but playing a full campaign on relentless difficulty was a really fun experience.

Racing games are extremely different from one another. And different people like different racing games because of those differences. Keeping in mind that I HAVE NOT ever played the multiplayer (yes, I know, I am missing some good stuff), let’s start with things that Burnout Paradise does not include and does not have to offer:
- It does not include cops chasing after your or the ability to play as a cop and chase other players;
- It does not include customization or tuning of cars whatsoever (only some futile paint jobs).
- It does not include weaponry for you to take down other cars, like spike strips etc.
So where does that leave us? Burnout Paradise offers you a simple racing experience. The game wants you to have fun and drive other players off the road until they crash their car and turn it into a cube (almost literally).
The cars are easy to drive. They don’t have multiple parts for you to customize and worry about. It’s just “Pick your favorite car and run like no one’s watching”, because no one really is – there is not a single soul in town, not even inside the cars. There is no story about some grownup man trying to be the best racer in town. It’s just you, the car, and the roads, nothing in between.
This game is simple, and that’s why it is loved so much by its fans. It features an open-world city with events in almost every intersection. The various types of events are: Races (you and a bunch of other drivers are supposed to get from A to B, and you need to be the first to get there. Not the third, not the second. The first.), Road Rages (there is nowhere to go, just run and take down other cars before time runs out), Marked Man (similar to Road Rage, except everyone else is trying to take you down), Stunt Runs (do crazy jumps and barrel rolls, smash through boards and security gates to earn points), and specific events to win an improved version of each car.
You won’t miss the missing features. You’ll have fun, and not give a damn about how your wheels look like.
