I enjoyed Fallout 4. The main story isn't the greatest in the world. It's probably on about par with Fallout 3, they're very similar in nature and not really the main attraction of these games for me. What I do think is the main attraction is the world, how fun it is to explore and the little stories you find along the way in this world.
Fallout 4 greatly succeeds in having a well crafted world that is a great deal of fun to explore. The story part is once again a little lacking quest wise than I would have liked. Most of them are short and too simple. However there are many journals and terminals for you to find and either read or listen to that have unique stories all their own.
The gameplay is vastly improved in Fallout 4 as well. Shooting is now much more fluid and fun than it was in the preceding games, the random junk you find around the world now has a purpose in crafting weapon and armor modifications as well as settlement building. Power armor is far more impressive and tank lke, which is another great improvement.
The armor and weapon crafting system was unfortunately a little too limited for my liking. There isn't as much weapon variety in Fallout 4 and even less armor wise and the crafting really didn't do anything to alleviate this in any way as all the modifications are largely the same.
As far as settlement building goes, I didn't care for it at all but I found it relatively easy to ignore so it wasn't a huge negative for me but I definitely wouldn't miss it if it were gone and replaced with more unique settlements across the wasteland.
All in all, in spite of the negatives, I still had a lot of fun playing this game and I'm sure I will again at some point in the future. No apologies.

As far as classic RTS gameplay and modernization, PA: TITANS really hits home.
As far as a recommendation ... See below. I really want to ... but being a long time RTS fan, some the of the issues below are glaring and can deter one from actually enjoying the game.
-being unable to save a game and come back to it
-lack of in-game resolution adjustment
-massive requirement for RAM
All of this could make playing the game a bit frustrating to play, especially if you like taking your time. The minimum requirement of RAM is 8GB and they are not kidding. When I connect to a LAN game, with a fairly robust map (5+ planets/moons/etc), my usual wait time is anywhere from 5-15 minutes; and thats just building the planets in the lobby. Once the game is started, I usually cant pick a starting location because by the time I am fully loaded in, the game has started.
Once in game, the experience could be a mixed bag as well. Most of the time, the game runs fine and no other issues arise. However, there are times when the game will drop to 1 FPS until I can zoom into a world, but even then, theres a chance it will not go back to working properly, or will continue to draw 1 FPS until I hit a "sweet" spot. Sometimes when its at that 1 FPS mark, any clicking with the mouse will cause the game to crash. With the FPS drop comes another problem, viewing the solar system as a whole. Basically the same issues as stated above. Im not sure if this could be because of the lack of RAM, but the HDD is constantly reading/writing. So, theres a possibility that the speed of your HDD will also impact the performance of the game.
All that aside, I will tell you there is nothing more satisfying than crashing a moon into a planet or building a deathstar to obliterate your enemies.

Doom 3: BFG Edition is the last game released by id Software under the technical guidance of John Carmack.
This version of Doom 3 uses a modified idTech 4 engine that takes advantage of a few rendering techniques that were developed for id's 2011 game, Rage.
Doom 3 is a game that was released over 8 years ago, so the price of the BFG Edition can make it a tough sell. But if you've never played Doom 3 then this is the version to get. Even today, it's a solid action-filled game in nearly every respect: great weapons, great combat, and great map design.
If you've played the original release, it's worth knowing that the visual enhancements, modified ammo & health placements, and armor-mounted flashlight turn this into a game that's very different from the one you knew; it now feels like a full-on action game in the vein of the classic Doom games.
(The only thing to be aware of is that this version of the game *does not* have modding or map editing support.)
Lastly, if you have a 120hz monitor (even if you don't, but especially if you do) you need this game! It looks exceptionally beautiful running at 120 frames per second on a 120hz monitor. Seriously, it's breathtaking.

If you're looking for a game here don't bother. If you're even just looking for a story you have significant impact on also don't bother. The goal of TellTale's The Walking Dead is identical to that of a film or television show. It wants you to think and feel. it doesn't present you choices so that you can bend and change the narrative to your will it gives you choices so that you can feel the stresses the characters feel. You need to willfully give into the lie of choice so that you can feel what the characters feel and understand the motivations behind the choices they make. It does all of this superbly and delivers and emotionally affective story through top notch writing and voice acting (some animation does leave a tad to be desired in places). If you want to be told a story and feel like a participant in that story this is the game of your dreams.

Sleeping Dogs is an open world game where you play as Wei Shen, an undercover cop who has been ordered to join The Triads, groups of gangsters who are causing tons of trouble in Hong Kong, where the game takes place. You can buy food items from street vendors, and they have many effects, for example, increased damage. You can also find Jade Statues throughout missions, and they will earn you more fighting moves. You can also enter fighting clubs to earn some cash and a new outfit. Wei can purchase cars, which he can use over and over again when he gets them from parking garages. You can also buy new clothes and customize Wei however you wish. There are also many various addons you can buy (DLC) and those include new cars, new missions, new clothing, new weapons, etc. Wei can also go on dates with a few women he meets through missions. You can find Lockboxes, which sometimes need lockpicked, but when opened, they can contain weapons, money, and clothing. You can also find Health Shrines, which when you pray to enough of them, your health can increase. There are many other things you can do in this game, but those were just a few. This is a very fun game, and I highly reccomend it.

Sleeping Dogs is awesome because it does this: martial arts, immersive open city of Hong Kong, immersive story, and interesting characters.
Although it was sometimes difficult to keep up with the story, as some characters are introduced too quickly and you have limited options in keeping up with who is who, they are very well made and are entertaining, which definetly helps with the story. The story itself is immersive and has lots of drama.
The game otherwise is different from open city games through implementing of martial arts. It is pretty obvious that in this regard Sleeping Dogs brought inspsiration from martial arts movies. It also keeps switching between realism and crazy stupid yet fun arcade action (specifically when it comes to driving).
Hong Kong is built very beautifully: colours, sounds, and the living simulation is interesting to explore and nice to look at and experience.
I strongly recommend this game to anyone who likes a good story game, lots of action, good humour and good drama, and martial arts. For the sake of fighting and driving (which there is a lot of), it is best played with a USB controller. I would however not recommend any of the DLC's for this game, because they are just filled with action, but none of the immersive content that exists in the main game (awesome characters and story).

Town of Salem is one of my new favorite games. If you ever played the game Mafia as a child (I did and I was obsessed), then you will definetly enjoy this game as it has the best aspects of that game. TOS is a bit more complex, but after a few games you will get the hang of it! Now onto the pros and cons
Pros:
-Super fun and easy to play and use
-All roles have the potential to make a difference in the game play
-Great for bringing back those childhood memories
-Plenty of people will play the game seriously (You just need to find the time that works best for you, mid-day is typically the worst time during summer and I would assume that during the school year the worst time would be directly following release from school)
-Many interesting roles and a somewhat fair trial system (Just gotta have people who don't random lynch)
-If you made an account and you want to link it with your steam account, it's easy to do that
-The steam version saves your password (if the account is linked to your steam account) so you don't have to type it in every time
-You don't need friends to play, you play with strangers (which is great because I don't have any friends)
Cons:
-The free version is practically the same but the steam version runs a bit better for me (less glitchy)
-Lots of trolls
-People gamethrow, and reporting doesn't do much in my experience
-People cheat
-People will get very upset even though it's just a game
-Not much customization options
So the game is definetly fun and I truly love playing it and I do recommend it, but play the free version first. It takes time to find the best time for you to play, but for the most part later in the day or early in the morning are the best times for me. And as a final note, don't buy this unless it is on sale; $5 doesn't get you too much in game stuff.

If you are a die hard fan of Street Fighter, you will enjoy this game.  The new mechanics really diversify the characters, making even old stand by characters like Zangief feel fresh again with new tactics.  Each character feels like they have the set of tools they need to achieve victory, and I find the characters are very well balanced.
That is the biggest positive this game has, however, you only can really appreciate the fighting mechanics by doing vs human multiplayer.  If you just arn't that interested in playing human opponents, then you won't really notice it.  Single player speaking, as of this review, you only have a few options to play:  Character story mode, which gives you a little comic story around literally 2 or 3 ROUNDS of gameplay vs very simple AI.  Survival Mode, which you have to face multiple AI opponents in sequence that get progressively more challenging until you complete the 'set.'  The sets of opponents are always the same, and the in-between round bonus you get (Defense increases, Health restoration) are random, which only preserves the frustration of randomness, yet keeps the experience predictable.   Have to beat 50 people in a row?  Well, when you fail the first time on opponent 35, you have to go back and fight the SAME people in the SAME order and they'll turn the AI back down to lull you back into complacency.
The third single player option is the General Story mode, which is a series of cut scenes using the game engine with you taking control of certain characters at certain points and playing a round of combat.  This is very fun the first time through because, for the first time, a Street Fighter game has an actual cannon story with it, and it is filled with things referencing games of the past and future.  If you arn't a long time fan of the series, certain plot points will be lost on you, but overall it was fun.  Watching the cut-scenes I played through in a couple hours, and you end up playing against some interesting unplayable characters.  After you complete it, you can go through it again with advanced AI difficulty.  It was fun, BUT at the end of it all it just wasn't enough gameplay.  The combat is still single rounds, so even if you face an opponent that beats you, you only need to beat them that one round to progress, so while it is a great addition to the game, it doesn't really showcase the game itself.
It is missing a simple Aracade Mode.  The traditional "play a series of opponents in 2 out of 3 rounds, then beat a boss, watch the credits" mode.  A mode where you can adjust the difficulty of your opponent, and then face random ones.  Perhaps this was intentional, because right now your only option for casual play is vs humans, which perhaps will get more people playing online.
Again, the game mechanics itself, I think are the best yet.  Right now, the characters seem very balanced, and it is fun to play people online.  If you want to dive in the online multiplayer, or don't mind it, you'll like the game.  It's excellent, and I recommend it for fighting game fans.  But it does lack many single player features, which they may add on later or may not.  So this game, while fun, certainly isn't what I would call a casual experience.

Doom 3... Has it really been 7 years since it ripped its way into the PC gaming world? I remember it like it was yesterday. Now, my first experience with Doom 3 was less than ideal. A family friend had bought the game to play herself, but found it to be a bit too frightening. So the brand new barely played copy of Doom 3 was passed on to me, and I proceeded to try and play through it on my measly Athlon XP with 256mb of ram and a 128mb GeForce FX5200. At 640x480 and low settings I barely got 20fps, but it still kept me on the edge of my seat. As time went by I managed to get my hands on some better hardware, and was able to experience Doom 3 the way it was meant to be played.
Of course now that we've hit the 20th anniversary of the Doom franchise, computers and game consoles are a bit more advanced. Sure, there have been many ports of the various Doom games to consoles, but nearly all of them have disappointed in one way or another. However with Doom 3 BFG Edition, things have changed. Not only do you get the full uncut Doom 3 and its expansion pack Resurrection of Evil, you also get pixel-perfect ports of The Ultimate Doom, and Doom II with its newly added episode No Rest For the Living, as well as a new episode for Doom 3! With Doom 3, none of the graphical detail or level architecture had to be sacrificed this time around (unlike the chopped to pieces ports for the original Xbox).
In fact, the original rendering system has been improved from the ground up with better lighting, and silky smooth constant 60 fps gameplay on normal monitors or televisions, and 120fps support for the 3d monitors and Head Mounted Displays that support it! The gameplay itself has also been streamlined slightly with a new armor-mounted flashlight which eliminates the need to choose between being able to see and being able to frag the hordes of hellspawn that stand in your way. All of the classic weapons are still available to find along the way, from the reliable shotgun to the always-classic BFG 9000. (That's Big F*cking Gun for those who don't know!)
When you get back to the original Doom games, nothing has really changed other than the addition of achievements/trophies, however if there had been any tinkering with them it just wouldn't have felt right. At first glance The Ultimate Doom and Doom II may seem a simple affair by today's standards, with their deceptively simple gameplay. However looks can be deceiving, as the classic Doom titles are known for their twisted mazelike corridors. Gamers who are used to the linear games of today could find themselves lost for hours in a level, searching for the next keycard. In the era that Doom was released the length of a game was provided by actual gameplay, and not by artificially padding the experience with cutscenes every 3 seconds.
With the BFG releases of The Ultimate Doom and Doom II, every little detail from the wonderfully pixellated sprite graphics, pumping MIDI buttrock soundtrack, and all around♥♥♥♥♥kicking style of the originals have been preserved perfectly. The controls are superbly mapped out to take advantage of the dual analogs on the consoles, which makes circle-strafing a breeze. The PC versions have also been upgraded with full WASD controls as well as mouse turning. These are is truly excellent ports of a pair of genre-defining games, and if you have never played these titles in their original forms you owe it to yourself as an FPS fan to try them out.
Doom 3 BFG Edition is definitely an epic package, and should be considered the del-facto collection of all things Doom that id Software has crafted over the years. Some fans may bemoan the lack of Final Doom and The Master Levels, however they were never actually developed by id themselves, they were fan works compiled and published officially. No matter if you are a console gamer or a PC gamer, you should seriously pick up this package. It is the definitive way to experience the Doom saga, and an all around good value. Hopefully if Doom 3 BFG Edition is a success then we'll see id and Bethesda release a similar compilation for their other famous series, Quake. But for now kick back, dig out your BFG, and keep on fraggin!

This game in my opinion is very fun if you are wonding wether to get this game i will try to make a decent review on the pros and cons of this game
Pros:
The game concept is one of the coolest ive ever seen, you can invade entire planets with colossal armies and wipe out all of your enemies or just activate the metal planets doom laser and zap the whole planet with a single shot but the scariest thing to do is to build the halley thrusters on a moon or asteroid and sling it right into another planet.
The base building and invading is very good in my opinion, in order not to get invaded you can build orbital defences to take down enemy scouts or invasion fleets, anti nuke luanchers incase they decide to go north korea on your *** and fire a nuke at your base you can even use giant cannons to fire your whole army to another planet and wipe it out.
The titans in this game are very fun to use there are 5 titans that you can unleash upon your enemy, the atlas is a giant walker mech that slamms the ground and causes earthquakes, the ares which is a giant tank that is near invincable, the zues which is a lighting titan, helios the orbital titan that can fly to other planets and link to a teleporter to transport your whole army there, and my favorite one which is ragnarok, that drills into the core of the planet then drops a nuke into the hole effectively blowing up the planet.
Cons:
If you want to play this game well you need to have a decent pc because if you want to have huge armies and not have your sim speed drop to 50% you will have to have a good pc.
The ai in this game is fairly simple without community mods they are either too easy and just have giant bases or incredibly difficult to beat, there is no middle ground between these.
Overall this game is great but if you want to play it to its full potential you will need a good pc and a few difficulty mods

Town of Salem is one of my new favorite games. If you ever played the game Mafia as a child (I did and I was obsessed), then you will definetly enjoy this game as it has the best aspects of that game. TOS is a bit more complex, but after a few games you will get the hang of it! Now onto the pros and cons
Pros:
-Super fun and easy to play and use
-All roles have the potential to make a difference in the game play

-Plenty of people will play the game seriously (You just need to find the time that works best for you, mid-day is typically the worst time during summer and I would assume that during the school year the worst time would be directly following release from school)

Cons:
-The free version is practically the same but the steam version runs a bit better for me (less glitchy)
-Lots of trolls
-People gamethrow, and reporting doesn't do much in my experience
-People cheat
-People will get very upset even though it's just a game
-Not much customization options
So the game is definetly fun and I truly love playing it and I do recommend it, but play the free version first. It takes time to find the best time for you to play, but for the most part later in the day or early in the morning are the best times for me. And as a final note, don't buy this unless it is on sale; $5 doesn't get you too much in game stuff.

Bastion is a brawler from a top-down perspective with a cartoony look. I saw this game on sale, and I heard good things about it, so I decided to spend my hard earned 2 dollars on it. The game is not hard to run, it never crashed, the framerate did not decrease and it still manages to look very nice. Gameplaywise, the game is quite simple. You walk with the w, a, s and d, dodge with space, block with shift, which also locks on targets and aim and attack with the mouse. You can carry two weapons at once. There is a set of melee weapons and ranged weapons, which you unlock through the game. You can equip two melee weapons or two ranged weapons, but I mostly stick with one melee and one ranged. You attack with your primary weapon with left mouse button and secondary weapon with the right mouse button, and you attack in the direction you point with the cursor, unless you are targeting an enemy. But the targeting system seriously bugged me. I thought that pointing at the enemies was a little dumb, so I tried to target the enemies, but the targeting system seems to target enemies randomly, maybe it targets the enemy closest to the cursor, but I am not really sure. Anyway, back to the weapons. My favorites are the machete, hammer, pike, pistols and shotgun, but I hate the rifle and mortar, but the worst thing about this is that in some levels, you get a new weapon, and the game feels that you just have to try it out and half of the level is just a weapon tutorial, which I thought was kinda dumb. But you get the option to switch your weapons about halfway through, which is neat. Throughout the game, a narrator tells the story, and he has an awesome voice, but most of the time I cannot hear him, due to all the noises in the game, but you can mute the sound and turn the voice volume up, which helps. And the story is awesome, listen to it. The game takes about 5 hours to beat, not counting the optional weapon challenges, where you can win materials to further upgrade your weapons. There are also survival modes if you're in that kind of stuff. Anyway, I think Bastion was a pretty fun game, and it's cheap, too. I would say it's worth the money, even though it's kinda short and the game isn't perfect. And the soundtrack is for sale, too.

After just recently purchasing this version of Planetary Annihilation: Titans, I have been hooked on this macro heavy, multi-planet, Real-Time Strategy game. It is extremely satisfying to amass large forces, keep tabs on your enemies, expand to multiple planets and build game-ending super weapons.
Mods are easily accessible through main menu. They allow for a wide variety of new maps and add-ons to customize your playstyle. I highly recommend the "Queller-AI" mod and the Legion Expansion.
Performance for the most part on my Nvidia 970 has seen a very stable 60+ fps when in-game on max settings, 100% sampling. When loading into a lobby it can get a bit stuttery. I also noticed that in 10 player matches on max settings where there are thousands of units it can get some slowdown and poor framerates (below 30 FPS). This caused me to experience a crash once from this. Unless you're absolutely positive your system can handle it, I would advise lowering your settings for big 10 player matches.
The learning curve can feel very steep if you just dive into multiplayer, so I would suggest to newcomers to play not only the Tutorial, but a normal game of the "Galactic War" campaign to get used to the controls, units and buildings.
Overall, I really like Planetary Annihilation: Titans and it's easily becoming one of my favourite RTS games.
A solid 4 out of 5 from me.

If you're like me, and tired of modern FPS titles, Doom 3: BFG is definitely a game to consider playing.
Pros:
- Old school health/armor system.  No more bleeding out through one's eyes, then magically recovering a few seconds later!
- Old school weapons system.  No Halo-esque two-weapons-at-a-time system!  You'll end up with a bunch of guns, each with their own strengths and weaknesses.
- Atmosphere.  The game's atmosphere is amazing.  The level design is very good -albeit with some flaws, discussed below-, the sound effects are extremely immersive, and the enemies look great.  Also, the jump scares are pretty fun, and they make the game intense early on.
Cons:
- Level design.  Although I like the look and the feel of the levels, the game is pretty linear and it does involve significant backtracking in some places.  You may end up getting lost a few times as well.
- Predictable scares. Yes, zombies and demons popping out at you is scary at first, but eventually you'll see a pattern to it and be able to predict when and where stuff will be popping out.  Once that happens, the game becomes less intense and more tedious.
- Story.  The story of the game amounts to "Marine, do this! Marine, go here! Marine, find this item!" It's almost nonexistent, and what little story there is is just an excuse to get you to the next area.  The "lore pickups," which reveal backstories and events of minor characters, are pretty bland, and after a while you'll likely just check them to see if they have a locker code.
Overall I enjoyed this game, and I recommend it to people looking for a different FPS experience.

is one of the most enjoyable strategy games I've played in years. It builds on the legacy of games such as
, and the
RTS games, while also learning from more recent entries in the genre such as
and
. The player is tasked with growing a small Viking settlement on a strange and dangerous new island from humble beginnings to a thriving little town. This involves a great deal of micro-management: allocating certain jobs to certain villagers; investing in Lore-research to unlock new technologies; balancing resource production; trading resources for profits; growing your population; preparing for the harsh winters; and the threat of conflict. You can pick between three different 'Clans', each with their own starting bonuses and unique benefits, and the developers are working on adding another two clans to the list.
It's possible to play mostly as a pacifist, and indeed you can win through totally non-violent means, though if you never train any warriors you certainly leave yourself open to being crushed by opponents or having your villagers picked off by wolves or Draugr.
has buckets of personality, particularly through some of the unique victory conditions, such as defending the Gate of Helheim, as well as enemies such as Valkyrie, Wyverns, and Giants. And visually the game is an absolute delight - it reminds me of something between
and
. Visually lush and vibrant, but stylised in an eye-catching way, and with a simple, beautiful interface, I can't criticise the game's visual design. Matches are consistently exciting, while also not dragging on for hours at a time. Usually I can complete a match in between 1-2 hours, which is about perfect.
There are also lots of small features in the game that help it stand out as a unique entry in the genre. For example, various actions such as conquering territory, exploring ruins, and launching raids earn you 'Fame' towards a victory-condition. You can also choose to consume a sizeable quantity of food in a Feast in order significantly increase your productive output for the next in-game month. The weather and calendar systems also affect the gameplay significantly, in particular because at winter food output significantly decreases and lumber consumption rises as villagers use fires to keep themselves warm, so you have to prepare for this. Random events such as the appearance of portals through which dangerous Draugr appear also keep you on your toes. And the game map is composed of individual 'areas' which have to be explored using a Scout before you can enter them. Each area contains various resources, and can be 'colonized' for a quantity of food. Because each area only allows a certain number of buildings to be constructed within them, the game incentivizes you to keep exploring and expanding into the unknown.
It's not
there just yet. It's an Early Access game, and the Multiplayer and story-driven Campaign modes haven't yet been implemented, but the developers have assured us they are on the way, as well as further fleshing out the currently fairly basic trade and diplomacy systems. I've not encountered any major bugs other than occasional performance slow-down. One thing I would say is that it's not the most challenging game - I've won every match I've completed, though a few times some opponents came quite close to achieving certain victory conditions before me.
There's a few tiny flaws with it and changes they could make, but given the development stage this game is at right now, it's looking
healthier than most Early Access games. The inclusion of female character models, slight difficulty/balance tweaks, and ironing out performance sags are hopefully improvements in the near-future. But other than that, I have to say that this is the most fun I've had with a video game in months. If you pine for some of the older games in this genre, particularly the early
games, and if
doesn't quite do it for you, then absolutely give this game a shot. I'm having a huge amount of fun with it, and I expect I'll enjoy it even more once they've fleshed out the core content a little more. I have no reservations about recommending this game.

Bastion is one of the best games I have played and you have no excuse not to play it.
It combines a number of addictive elements that slowly get introduced to you. It has a witty narrator (think Stranger Than Fiction with Will Ferrell) that hilariously narrates everything you do. You get a few weapons along the way and a shield at the start then your favourite RPG tools appear.
Let’s talk about the graphics. Amazing! If you have a higher resolution screen like me (2560 by 1440), checkout the Steam discussions to get a fix for it (look in properties, set launch options… and add -x 2560 -y 1440). It’s like you have been thrown into an artist’s water coloured mind and has painted his brush all over your brain. The music and sounds are fantastic. This is truly what gaming is about.
Bastion is a hack and slash RPG, you get and upgrade weapons along the way, and you have secondary weapons, special attacks, weapon upgrade tree, elixirs to improve stats, shrine to increase difficulty and mini games to master your skills. Even after that, you have a nice loot system that you’re always trying to find and there’s an excitement level because when you get something, it’s good and not just worthless junk!
The only area I can really fault with this game is its story, it’s not as interesting like most games (I want to know what caused the Calamity, but that’s about it), it doesn’t even matter though. You just want to play and have a good time.
Best thing about Bastion is it always had something new to show the player, it’s not tedious, it doesn’t get stale. It’s refreshing to see a game excite so much while having so much strategy to a hack and slash genre which people tend to have a habit of mindlessly playing.
Thank you Bastion, for being awesome! One of my favourite games.

This game was on my recommended list. I wouldn't have paid the money for it, but it came in a package with like 6 other games or something. I thought maybe I would like at least one of them. I was disappointed after three of the games, Verdan Hue, octo-something and Rise. Each of these games, I think, is trying to make a 'message' about the environment which that's fine. I think whatever 'message' they were trying to make about the state of humanity/world issues/environment is horribly lost by the terrible gameplay and frustrating controls/bad UI. The games that I played had little game interface. There was no menu to save, to change the window size, to change the music volume. The game package said that some of the procedes go to help {insert something} and so I at least can pretend to feel like I have made a small impact instead of wasting money. But if I'm being honest still doesn't appease my frustration with this purchase.
I'll focus on this game now Verdant Hue. There is no menu area. There is no exit button. The save mechanics are terrible. If you have 'unlocked' a tool the next time you play that tool may or may not be unlocked. The only way that I can see to 'grow' food is to stay in the game for over 6+ in game nights which is an eternity in real life. Your character does not run. He meanders about his deceased parents farm, possibly from his injuries or from his crippling depression. I don't care. Also if you click on a square accidentally across the field you might as well get up and use the bathroom because he's going to go there 8 hours later (okay, that's excessive) because there is no way to cancel the queue. He will go to that selected square no matter how many times you click or yell otherwise. So you can only get a few things done as the day races on. There are some 'objectives' you can get in game they are requests you get from letters being stuck in your mailbox. I don't think there is a mail service running, I think you're neighbors are just sticking notes in your mailbox asking for items that will take real life years to make. There is a story in this game, this poor child had his family destroyed by rebels/enemies/whatever and now has to make life happen on his own. Is that story sad, yeah, do I feel anything for this character, sure... anger. Move faster, remember the items you had in your inventory and freaking don't take the longest route possible to that stupid square. Again, if there is a 'message' in this game it's lost. I have no compassion for this PSone sprite that moves like a slug. His story is sad, but so under developed and rushed. I would rather sit in a cubicle with the lights off than play this game that has no game play. At least in the cubicle I could use my imagination.

I really wanted to like this title. Sadly, Street Fighter V is heavily bogged down by numerous terrible decisions on Capcom's part, which clouds an enjoyable core game.
New mechanics are introduced such as the V Trigger, V Skill, and Crush Counter. Without going into too much detail, these are all fresh systems that introduce another layer of strategy which in turn can lead to plays involving longer combos or different setups. Compared to Street Fighter 4, the fighting itself is much more "distilled"; so combos are easier to preform, the timing on attacks is much more lenient, and other changes include being able to quick rise off of throws. However, the tradeoff of this is that everything is much less freeform, so you no longer see unique combos or playstyles. Not to say everyone had entirely individual playstyles for certain characters in the previous iteration, but it was at least possible and always an interesting surprise to see it happen.
Regardless, Street Fighter V brings a varied cast and an enjoyable fundamental game. This is where the positives end.
I will not give a complete comprehensive overview regarding all of Capcom's shortcomings with Street Fighter V, but I will discuss the ones that affected my decision to give this game a negative review. First, the netcode and online play. I'm not sure what changes were made to the online system but I can say that they have caused most of my matches to be much laggier compared to the majority of them in 4. In 5, you can sort matches by connection, but even with adjusting the setting to the highest standard, I still encounter laggy matches.
Next, the priority in which Capcom decides to resolve issues. From the start of this game, there have been rage quitters, an absolutely horrid Survival game mode in which you have to endure up to 50 rounds without losing once against AI that reads everything you do beginning at round 20, online bots, and an 8 frame delay for all inputs. Rage quitters were "dealt" with
into development by preventing them from playing online for a short time if they disconnected too much. Survival mode, the only way to unlock character colors 3-10 and one of the biggest complaints most players have, was "fixed" by allowing users to pay $1 each for single colors. Online bots and 8 frame delay still persist. Despite those two glaring issues, Capcom's latest priority was to start punishing players who understandably got around the torture known as Survival mode.
The amount of extra paid content this game has is absurd. A season pass since day 1 for $30, character costumes with no extra colors for $4 each, another DLC package separate from the season pass for $25, and the final one that broke me; a single lone stage for $10. There's also an in game currency system which can be used to buy some stages and characters, but keep in mind you only get 50 points of it when winning an online game. Then consider that characters are 100,000 each, and stages are 70,000. You do get one-time currency sums from beating character stories and doing trial mode, but most of the payload comes from Survival. Formerly, currency could be amassed easily with a mod to beat survival quickly, but that has since been patched by Capcom: faster than the time it took to deliver the rage quitter "punishment", of course. Daily challenges, a feature promised long ago as another method to earn more, has yet to be implemented as of this review.
In order for me to ever consider playing this game again, every condition in this list would have to be met:
Dan and Peter are fully playable characters.
2,500 currency is earned from winning ranked games, less for player matches.
Extra premium costumes are $1 with all colors available.
The netcode stops being unbearable.
Daily challenges are implemented with worthwhile rewards.
Rage quitters are punished on a harsher degree rather than a quick slap on the wrist.
The 8 frame delay is fixed.
Premium stages are $2.
Survival mode has some sort of fair method to make it tolerable.
I don't imagine even half of that list being met, but I can still dream at least. To conclude, I was desperately hoping for Street Fighter V to be a fun and worthwhile new beginning for the series; but instead, it was only an end.
At least Tekken 7 is coming to PC.
12/22/16 edit:
The frame delay was slightly reduced and challenges provide a small fight money boost of around 7,000 for every week, and a new rage quitting system was implemented. These changes are a start but not significant enough to make me like the game. I cannot recommend the game in its Season 2 state either.

I review BoI coming from the perspective of a person who enjoys the crap out of Nuclear Throne and Enter the Gungeon. My initial experince fell short of my expectations, clearly founded upon the pure adrenaline rush provided by NT. My impression was a game that was much slower and casual than anticipated, thus failing to scratch the persistent itch that NT (and later EtG) created for bullet Hell.
I reached out to the community for advice, because 34K people touting the greatness of this game couldn't be wrong (could they?) They said "Don't waiver, stick with BoI and you won't regret that decision." So, ignoring my instinct to simply refund and move on, I have. And while I am far short of the 100's of hours you would want from a reviewer, I can tell you they are right.
BoI is deep...much deeper than either of the two aforementioned games above. Once you accept that it is neither of the other two, BoI's attaction will begin to set in. Hopefully those who are following a similar path as mine will find good advice that BoI belongs in your permanent library. You won't regret that decision, I assure you.

HONEST REVIEW: I would only recommend this game for any person that remembers what it was like to truly win at something and not just be handed a participation trophy. Fighting games and particularly Street Fighter games require 100s of hours of practice to just get good. There are no short cuts, there are no easy level ups. You have to devote yourself to learning how to beat the other person with your character of choice. Playing street fighter is like playing chess and poker in 1/12 of a second increments. You have to make the right move or the right call FAST! There's no easy win here boys and girls. It's a game where it's just you and your opponent, no teams to bail you out or blame for their terrible plays. You have to hold that "L" all to yourself, so if you want to know what it's like to really be a winner then pick up this game and play it. Play it until you hate, then play it some more until you realize how amazing this game truly is. Once you finally reach that level where you can dominant your opponent. That's when you'll know what it feels like to truly be a winner.
Pros:
• Amazing multiplayer with a good list of characters and more to be added (well balanced as of 7-1-16)
• Awesome story mode (4 hours of content with some good humor and surprises)
• Training mode (with recorder) to practice numerous setups. Needs a few more tweaks and online mode to practice with a friend, but taht should be coming.
• Graphic Modding (don't like a skin. Change it)
• Capcom is fully backing this game with updates on a monthly basis so more content will be added all the time. Majority of the content can be earned for free by playing the game or paid for if you wish. Only cosmetic items like premium outifts will cost you.
Cons:
The game was released early as it was rushed to be ready for the 2016 tournament season. The multiplayer was finished, but everything else was not so the game has suffered in reviews. Since Feb. the game has seen a number of additions with more coming so I believe most of these will be addressed in up to a years time with that said as of 7-1-16 there are still a few things that need to be addressed but are not game breaking such as:
• Rage quitting in ranked (no true deterrent as of yet), but can be avoided in casuals or battle lounges
• 8 frames of input delay (this affects your ability to react to punish moves. It's currently under review by capcom to address it)
• Rather long load times between matches. 30 seconds to a minute feels like forever when you are staring at a blank screen.
• The in game recording of your stats is still not functional (It's sort of like a fitness tracker for your character)
• Model clipping that makes the game feel a little cheap and unpolished. (I have a feeling this will be addressed last as it's only noticeable on load screens).

Ahh Fallout 4, a game i've done a total of one playthrough of a character, said I would pick up again, and then didn't do so.
It's not exactly great, medicore even compared to the other fallouts (aside from a certain BoS game), however it still has some charm.
Compared to every other fallout it manages to finally understand that a filter of one kind of color is beyond annoying for the player and it managed to streamline the somewhat tedious loot screens of the old engine and Skyrim. It also had a somewhat nifty settlement system, granted I didn't do much with it, I've seen some pretty impressive ones built by other players.
However it's also regressed quite a bit from the other games to (and goes a bit further than Skyrim). The lack of skill checks (aside from speech) is the most notable and worst part I feel out of this, as it allowed for many many more options and ways to complete quests. This sadly was replaced by the horrible 4 button Yes, (Sarcastic) Yes, Basically Yes, and the No which just exits the dialogue with the character. In the previous games you could get up to several dialogue choices to choose from which would branch into more choices, not so much in this one though.
I also have a major gripe with the idea or legendary weapons since it just feels like I didn't really obtain anything worthy of note. When I first played Fallout: New Vegas I managed to get "This Machine" which was a unique weapon that felt amazing to use and basically became my favourite weapon of the game. Here in this one? Literally nothing as I have to hope a pray to RNG to give me a good legendary effect on a good weapon. It just gets annoying finding another Robot slaying baseball bat when I could have gotten an overpowered 2 shot sniper rifle. Doesn't work the other way around either as you could kill some random legendary raider and get it anyways which feels like you got a powerful weapon for doing basically nothing.
In the end Fallout 4 isn't exactly a great game. I enjoyed my time playing it, and it's not that bad honestly. But compared to Fallout's 1, 2, Tactics, 3, and New Vegas? Just get one of those games. However if your for some reason forced to choose between this one and the horrible Xbox BoS Game? This one for sure.

If you can ignore the "Creation Club" nonsense, the game is pretty good.
But, it just doesn't hold up in comparison to its predecessors. It's not a bad game, don't get me wrong; it's just that, as a Fallout game, it's pretty ungraceful.
The gameplay is smooth; Bethesda did a lot of work on the game in this regard. Definitely an improvement over previous entries in the series.
Sound design is good, especially for environmental ambience. Granted, that's par for the course for games like this, but it's still worth mentioning.
There's *color* here! Downtown Boston in particular has a lot of vivid colors: Reds, greens, blues. No dingy green filter here.
But the game takes lore out behind the shed. The game has completely altered the identity of several weapons, and even eliminated several more. The AEP7 Laser Pistol from other BethSoft games has undergone some kind of fusion with the AER9 Laser Rifle; they're now basically the same gun now (And they both use Microfusion Cells, now.); the same thing happened with the Plasma Gun. The N199 Assault Rifle, a military-issue weapon from the Capital Wasteland, is non-existant, along with its Chinese counterpart, and has been replaced with a massive, art-deco monstrosity. The Gauss Rifle looks like it's homemade, which I can give a pass to, but the military prototype is nowhere to be seen (Until you cave and use the Creation Club, where it's given top billing with another "Operation: Anchorage" piece: The Chinese Stealth Suit.).
The story is fairly par for the course for an RPG of its ilk, which I won't spoil here. A good twist here and there, but that's all I'll say about it. Radiant quests can get pretty repetitive and/or tedious after a while (I'm looking at you, Preston.), so if you don't like spending your time going to the same five or six places (A real turn-off for me, seeing as I play open-world exporation games to, y'know, *explore*.), run the other way.
So, is this a good game? Maybe: if you've been a Fallout fan for more than a couple years, you've probably noticed a lot of things we've come to know from a Fallout game become neutered (Lack of real choice in tackling matters, increased emphasis on gunplay, butchering of the lore, et cetera.) If you're just some average joe looking for a solid Action RPG, this is a good choice (Though I would encourage you to check out other games in this franchise.)

Despite its problems, Doom 3 is still more fun than it is annoying. Taken in small doses, its jump-scare filled corridors can be quite entertaining. And the BFG edition wrapped the entire product in a trouble-free installation, complete with Doom and Doom 2 as a nice added bonus. Its not something I'd ever have bought for full price but, well, you know... Steam Summer Sale.
At first glance, the BFG edition is a huge step backwards, however. Its default level-of-detail seems to be set for XBox-era graphics, and its annoying tendency to autosave interrupts the game flow with a tasteless on-screen reminder. A few hacks remedied these minor issues, although even then the lighting - once the crown jewel of the idTech4 engine - seems less sophisticated than in its original release. Fortunately, the gameplay remains unmolested. True, its endless monsters-in-the-closets are trite and unimaginative, but - so long as I kept my sessions short - still workable nonetheless. The new "Lost Levels" campaign isn't anything to write about; dull, linear levels that tell no story; its saving grace is that it is too short to get upset about.

It was made by Telltale which by now is practically a genre (and a very good one), you have the Quick Timed Events and the exploration (point-and-click) parts but it never gets boring. Sometimes new challenges are introduced that are different from the previous mentioned.

Every time you interact with the characters or make a certain decision (Help character A or B), the plot line develops differently, with consequences in the long run. I've had some of the most difficult decisions in a video game because of how well the possible story lines are written. To make it "worse", most of this difficult decisions are timed and you don't have much time to think them through. You feel engaged all the time and you feel part of the story. You feel sad when some character that you liked died but also feel happy with some character that you saved interact positively with you.
This game is great. The only negatives points that I can think of are that the animations sometimes (although rarely) feel a bit weird (it feels like a few frames are missing or the animation transited too fast or too slow) and the sound quality of the speech in certain scenes are not perfect.

- the game needs more content (building types, building upgrades, military units, maybe resources)
- remove annoying notifications about clan size limitations (when population limit is achieved housing icon turns red and a notification will pop-up from time to time, indicating that more houses need to be built, which in fact might be a tactical mistake at that point)

"Simple gamplay with surprising depth, a storyline that leaves you wondering until the end, good mechanics, and a perfect musical score that fits so well."
To expand upon this, the gameplay mechanics are pretty simple -- it's an overhead hack-and-slash of sorts. You figure out the basics pretty easily, but over time you pick up new weapons that complicate things in interesting ways. To the very end, even the hammer you start with is a perfectly valid weapon. Powerups come in the form of weapon upgrades and drinks from the "distillery" that give you unique perks.
There is always added challenge in the game, as unlocking effigies of the ten gods over the course of the game will add unique changes to combat -- with a boost to your XP for every statue activated, but the difficulty spike will make you work hard for every single bonus point.
The storyline has a breathtaking depth to it once you start to figure things out. It begins with you alone and isolated, in a room in the middle of nowhere. You emerge to find that, while you slept, the entire world around you was destroyed, everyone turned to stone, yet monsters that were once your city's workforce roaming about. It sounds bleak and desperate, but not very long in you meet your first ally, and his calm, soothing tones will tell you that, with a little work, everything can be set right.
And through it all, through every second of gameplay, is a soundtrack punctuating every line just perfectly. From heart-wrenching arias of doubt and remorse, to jazzed-up tunes to keep you pumped in dangerous zones, it just fits the game perfectly and makes it the single most defining characteristic in this game to me. And, you know what they say, save the best for last.
You can play a portion of this game for free, via the Chrome Browser Store. They have an add-in that is a demo of the game (or maybe even the whole of it, I'm not sure). Test it out for free, and if you like it enough, seriously consider buying it. But really, what's the harm in just trying it out?

You never feel alone and it adds a destined outcome kind of vibe to all your actions, regardless of how trivial. This is amongst the best rpgs I've ever played, because there is very little more I could possibly want from this title.

Sanctum 2 is a very robust game, it provides a lot of fun and challenge in equal measure.
The graphics are first-rate, the landscapes and scenery in the game world are breathtaking, Leonard Hummer's soundtrack is gorgeously composed, the game's characters are full of personality and have very nice designs, and the consistantly different levels means there's never a dull moment.
The level of customisation in the game is incredibly diverse, even without DLC weapons and 'Perks' (abilites that provide buffs and other useful effects in-game) - there are a lot of different loadouts one can equip. Difficulty level is also customisable, instead of a traditional 'Easy - Medium - Hard - etc.' setup, this game employs the 'Feats of Strength' system, allowing you to customise how hard to make the game, options to increase enemy health, speed, and strength are all seperate, giving you a more gradual difficulty slope as you get more confident.
Multiplayer is another fantastic part of this game, allowing you to create or join a server at the touch of a button. You can create a private server and invite your friends to it, or make a public one and fight alongside complete strangers, or browse the public server list and help other players.
As someone that's obtained every achievement for this game, I can say there is still plenty more this game has to offer, different loadouts to try, different tower combinations, different maze layouts, I now spend time on public servers, helping them to progress through the game and I'm always fascinated by all the new and interesting approaches to the levels that I'd never even considered in my playthrough.
Overall, very well polished, very enjoyable game with loads of content and replayability. I highly recommend Sanctum 2, you won't be disappointed with it.

+ Graphics are "improved" over the original game (they are in a different style entirely, but I prefer the newer style)
+ Runs significantly faster and smoother compared to the original; doesn't crash or lag between level changes anymore
+ WAY more items, WAY more enemies, WAY more rooms. In short, lots of new stuff has been added when compared to the original
+ A saving system. Finally! A definite improvement over the original in that aspect. Different games files are a nice touch as well.
+ LOTS of trophies, LOTS of collectibles, LOTS of unlockables. As soon as you beat this game for the 50th time, you realize you still have SO much to do.
+ Playing as Azazel is a surefire way to have fun. Azazel's "mini-brimstone" tears combine and pair with a multitude of other tear types, allowing for crazy and scary-powerful combinations
- Ultra-repetitive; it's not a joke when I say that you WILL do the same thing over and over and over and over and over.
- "Randomly generated levels" seems like a gigantic joke when I fight The Dark One three rooms in a row in the The Dark Room
- Randomly bugs out to where I'll simply stop moving and shooting completely. This problem immediately goes away if I simply let go and then press the keys again, but it's an ENORMOUS, and possibly fatal, hassle when in the middle of a fight or when navigating through certain traps. This problem never occurred in the original for me.
- You're either overwhelmingly overpowered, mowing down entire rooms of enemies at a time in less than 5 seconds, or you are so overwhelmingly underpowered that it takes you 3 minutes just to pick away at the boss at the end of a level. There is no in between. Period. There's only one option or the other.
- "Practically impossible" is not a valid difficulty for a game, ever. Spammy attacks, lack of telegraphs from certain bosses, excessive amounts of creep (especially at The Womb and later), and, especially, a huge and frequent amount of exploding enemies don't make the game difficult, they make it frustrating, and being frustrated isn't fun. On top of that, I've had FAR too many times where I'll open a locked chest after bombing away a rock and losing health to the enemies in the room only to get a single penny in return. The ratio of "risk:reward" involved in the game is WAY too disproportional.
- MANY of the items are effectively automatic game-enders. I have had FAR too many instances where I'll be very near the end of a playthrough, and a SINGLE item will make it to where I simply cannot progress in the game (many, if not all, of the "cursed" items do this), or cannot avoid killing myself ("Bob's Brain" is the biggest culprit. It's a ridiculous item). especially since there are many times where you don't even KNOW what item you are getting.
- Playing as Azazel is the only surefire way to have fun. Azazel's flight, immunity to creep, and mini-brimstone tears are all highly advantageous, which only evens out the game, not make it easier. I absolutely despise playing as any other character because, with any other character, it is entirely too likely to have a dud of a playthrough where you either stay underpowered or die early on.
I've been trying to figure out how to rate this game for a while. There are some things that are enjoyable about it, absolutely, but, all in all, I guess I would discourage others from buying this game. It's fun at the start, on the surface, but then you realize how repetitive and unfair it is. It's disguised as a "difficult" game, when really it's just frustrating. Any progression you make story-wise is largely up to chance, considering you have almost no influence over what items you will get. On top of that, MANY aspects of the game are not explained in the slightest, adding another layer to the pseudo-difficulty; you can't get hints as to how to get certain items, you aren't given any descriptions of the effects of items, and you aren't told how to summon certain enemies, forcing you to rely on the internet for information; a game should have all of the information readily available within it, you just have to look for it.
If you do end up buying this game, I would highly recommend buying it when it's at least 75% off. It's certainly not worth 15 dollars to me, and another 11 bucks for DLC is practically extortion.

I have to say I've been a little disappointed with this game. I enjoy RTS and wargames in general, but here it feels like the WW2 theme has just been bolted onto a pretty generic RTS game.
First off, game design issues:
- When you select the Americans you actually start in 1940, and its really the British! But with US uniforms on the unit cards (not on the actual battlefield though) and US accents for the voiceover.
- Speaking of voiceover, if you play as the Russians or Germans the vocals are in those languages. Nice for feeling in character but I don't speak them, and it makes understanding the constant stream of new objectives and reports hard to follow.
- The scenarios feel very scripted and you have to plod through some from A, to B, to C...etc in order to complete them. If you need to replay any this gets boring very quickly!
- Some "undercover" British units in the German campaign are blatantly not undercover at all but cannot be attacked when you are parked in among them, until the scenario script is triggered. It destroys the feeling of immersion.
Combat:
+ Visuals and sound effects are fine.
- Vehicles seem to be far better than infantry, which appear largely to be waste as they die far too easily and are quite limited in what they can do.
- AI tactics involve infantry waves charging at your tanks and standing in front of them getting machine gunned. Doesn't feel very WW2 to me!
- Nothing here we haven't seen before in countless RTS games.
PVP:
+ On the good side, I never had to wait long to be matched with an opponent.
- Race to the flags and hold to build up points isn't in any way new, and again breaks the WW2 immersion. Plus it doesn't matter if you are caning the other guy's army, its all about those points for holding flags.
Overall, I'd hold off until this drops in price considerably. I enjoyed Company of Heroes far more than this and that game is a total bargain when it comes up in the Steam sales.

Going into this game, I was expecting The Settlers. Many reviews mentioned it, so I got psyched. I love almost every game in The Settlers series, and long for a new one. Purchased this game without a second thought.
I'll start off by saying this: Northgard is NOT a city builder. The tag is, as far as I'm concerned, incorrect. It's nothing like The Settlers, or Anno, or the Impressions series, or any other city builder game. However, I'm pleased to say that, despite not being what I hoped for, Northgard is an incredible game and I'm so excited for its future.
A more appropriate tag for this game would be 4X. A simplistic 4X, to be sure, but a 4X nonetheless.
Explore: You train scouts to scope out territories that are hidden by the fog of war. Think of it like revealing new tiles in Civilization. Until they are discovered, you don't know what's there, and can't plan your buildings. Exploration is crucial.
Expand: Each territory has a very strict building limit, so if you want more than a small handful of buildings, you'll need to expand to other areas. Territories can have special resources or bonuses, as well, so it's imperative to find them and make them your own.
Exploit: The game contains a fair amount of resources needed to build and upgrade buildings, feed and warm your populace, and trade. Each territory can have a different resource or bonus, and it's up to you to place buildings that can take advantage of them.
Exterminate: There is a small combat element to the game. You'll need to rid a territory of predators before claiming it, and defend from hostile NPCs. You may also attack your opponents, and fend of attacks from them.
See? All four X's. Northgard is closer to Civilization than any city builder, and it's a wonderful take on the 4X genre. Games are fast paced and simple, but still require thought, strategy, and planning ahead. Winters are tense times where your resources are drained mercilessly. Skirmishes with NPC or AI units are quick and satisfying. Plus, there are lots of ways to win!
I can't recommend this game as a city builder, because it simply isn't one. However, that doesn't mean it's not a great game! I fully recommend this to anyone who enjoys 4X games or RTS games, and doesn't mind a more relaxed, simplistic style. The graphics, sounds, controls, UI, and gameplay all shine, even in this unfinished state. This game deserves your time, money, and support. Enjoy!

SFV is a great game at it's core, but in constant development, so it has many controverse discussions.
I've been playing SFV since release in February 2016 and still having a lot of fun playing online, against people on the same continent (Europe). Rage quitting has no hard punishment atm. and can be very annoying in ranked, but there is also casual mode and battle lounge, where points are less important.
I can recommend SFV to dedicated players, especially those, who liked to play other Street Fighter series and are willing to adapt to
(V-Trigger/V-Skill) instead of focus attacks / different character play styles for example. Combos are much easier to perform than in SFIV. Competitive players can spend countless hours in training mode, to improve their skill (timing / mixups).
Everyone has own preferences, so my suggestion for everyone, who is still unsure:
.
Just make sure that your PC meets the minimum system requirements, or preferably recommended system requirements (from my experience not older/slower than Intel i5 2500 + 8 GB RAM + GeForce 960 GTX++ for maximum settings + wired internet connection).
Online lag/connectivity problems are mostly reported by people from Latin America, Australia, Africa and Indonesia regions playing people from other continents.
Some Technicolor/Thompson routers have firmware / settings issues with P2P (need to be bridged or modified, because port forwarding does not work properly for them).
Keyboard Button remapping requires 3-rd party software like AutoHokey or Logitech.
PS4 / D-Input controllers have are not natively supported by Windows (drivers issue), because Microsoft has dropped native D-Input support many years ago. At the moment you have to hope that D-input controller developers update their Windows drivers or you need to use a 3-rd party app like "x360ce" or "joy2key"). Madcatz is the only controller manufacturer known to me, who published/updated their PS4 FightStick drivers, and HORI has implemented a hardware X-input switch on some of their FightSticks. XBOX ONE controller, analogue shoulder buttons are not working.
The local input lag is 3 frames higher than in SFIV (50 ms), unless you are a cyborg, you won't notice it. Human reaction time / finger to button distance / device lag and internet latency NOT included, which is usually much higher. Average human reaction time is ~250 ms (1/4 second ~ 15 frames)
Judge your personal reaction time:
Guilty Gear overhead block test:
Controller input lag is local and has nothing to do with internet lag/latency, which depends from too many factors, many people mix this up.

There is also single player content in SFV:
- Survival Mode in 4 difficulty settings
- Character Story Mode
- Cinematic Story Mode with 2 difficulty sets (normal / hard) ~4 hours long with cinematics on normal difficulty.
- Character challenges / Trial mode
- Training Mode which includes customizeable vs CPU/AI in 10 difficulty settings.
______________________________________________________
You can unlock ALL 6 DLC characters (Alex, Guile, Ibuki, Balrog , Juri, Urien***) by playing the above single player modes up to normal difficulty.
BUT earning fight money requires an internet connection, because it is saved on Capcom servers to avoid cheating.
*** Urien will be released later in 2016, but is already playable in some story mode missions.
The above 6 DLC characters + their premium costumes + Guile Stage can also be obtained by purchasing the Season Pass 2016. So you can spend the fight money on other stuff like stages or future DLC characters in 2017.
Some cosmetic content like "premium costumes" or "CapcomPro Tour stage" is obtainable with real money only.
, will always be obtainable with fight money and the announced upcoming daily challenges (targets game mode).

(NOTE THIS GAME IS FREE ON A BROWSER YOU DO NOT HAVE TO BUY IT ON STEAM)
(This review is for the game Town Of Salem (ToS) NOT THE STEAM VERSION IN PARTICULAR)
CHEATING
This is in response to the negative reviews. The most brought up point against ToS is the cheating that goes on during the game. From an outsider's perspective, I might think that this means hacking or abusing something to help the 'cheater'  win. This is not the case at all. When people refer to 'cheating' in ToS it is most likely to do with 'gamethrowing' a trolling type of rule breaking. To gamethrow, one must use their roles abilitys to reveal information against their OWN alignement in order to make them lose. Note that gamethrowing actually does not benefit the 'cheater' in any way. Although gamethrowing is a real issue and can be very annoying, it isn't that common, and all the other forms of cheating never apear to me as a problem, especially not in ranked matches.
RANKED
Another point argued in favor of not playing ToS is the fact that everyone is too stupid and you can never get a game where the town is working together properly. While I can actually kind of agree with this point, ranked matches seem to completely fix this problem. Only players with 50 games played and 10 practice ranked matches played are allowed  to join ranked games. I barely ever play the other game modes any more because ranked games are a safe haven against cheaters and people who don't know what they're doing.
WHY YOU SHOULD PLAY (not buy) TOWN OF SALEM (PROS)
Now enough rebuttle, here's why I think this game is worth your time. To begin with, I'd like to say that this game isn't for everyone. It's not graphically good looking at all, it can apear to be a
slower game compared to others although it's just as exciting. But for the people who don't mind these things, this game is already for you. This is a game of deception for the evil roles, and intellegence for the town roles you need to think and be good at convincing people with words in order to win. I can't really explain why that's so fun, but it is, you'll just have to trust me.
CONS
Despite me loving this game there are a few problems that I have with it.
1. Evil Roles in ranked matches: Although winning with an evil role in ranked gives you more ELO and points, it is almost too difficult to win with a semi-good town.
2.To do good you need to know everything: This point is less important because learning about the game was a fun experience for me, however you cannot be good if you do not know all the little details about each and every role and every game mechanic.
3.Graphics: Graphics aren't that important in a game like this and I know they definetly could have done a worse job with the design but this game isn't very visually apealing in any way.

15 hours played thus far.
Game play begins to make sense after about 3-4 hours of working through the tutorials. I chose Germany first, then Soviets, and finally Allied forces. Whichever nation you choose first will suffer a lower research gain rate; but that's less of a problem than spending hard to get research on less-worthwhile upgrades.
B3 plays at a less personal level than COH or COH2. Like Steel Division 44 (on my list next), you have a mission loadout screen. Going blind into missions just killed my motivation to play a lengthy session because of enduring the carnage. However, there's a replay button once you retreat and that allows a much better mission loadout prep (and more likely victory).
The tutorials for each nation are really well done, especially in teaching (baptism by huge losses and retreats) the proper role of each unit type: armor, inf,, and support. My struggles in learning as Germany made playing the Soviets almost easy, though some missions can be tough.
And, the missions have some action of all sorts: offensive (you've got to beat the timer); rescue (heavily under fire); stealth advance to discover tank, mg, and arty implacements; and city/street fighting. In all, I'm pretty amazed at how well all these play out.
I'd definitely recommend leaving the Allied forces to last for learning. Even with a learned proficiency, I failed to grasp several of the early mission concepts (but that's better now).
So far I've only played against the AI and once against Boris (who totally kicked my ***). The AI is not always bright; but it's always brutal and efficient at killing. On missions where I'm aggressively on the offensive, there's less likelihood that the AI will flank me. Boris, however, is flanking nightmare (my experience so far). Bring your A game!
IN ALL, I'm pleased with my purchase of this game. I did start with the free demo offer, which hooked me. Then I bought it on the Steam sale--and I'm glad that I did. It's a solid, if not really good game.

When I was a kid, they told me Doom 3 was a resource hog, lackluster, un-scary, and too dark. These are all incorrect.
Doom 3 is scary. The atmosphere is good as hell, perhaps excellent. I'm never unsatisfied shotgunning demons as I run through hallways (corridors, hence "corridor shooter"). The big machines in the environments impress me. Things slide into and out of place, dealies spin, doodads shift and turn. More of this would have been cool. Character models and animations show their age, though.I looked up all the locker codes because it sucked to stand around listening to audio logs and sifting through emails for a god damned 4-digit number. I think they added motion blur and some high♥♥♥♥♥antialiasing, but the graphics are the same.♥♥♥♥♥♥s widescreen now, so it looks pleasant on your modern displays, rather than you 500 lb CRT.
Did you come to Doom 3 for story? I came for blood. Rivers of blood and fields of broken enemies. Doom 3 is LONG. If you've been playing nothing but CoDpiece: Modern Brofare Superbowl XXIVIXIVIXC, this is like 5 of those. Amusingly, this game kinda rips off Half-Life 2, despite that it didn't: portals, extradimensional invasion, scientists, a gravity gun... You should play both. q = plasma rifle
e = grenade?
f = shotgun
x = special
I must withhold the other keys, as I must conceal my secret professional techniques. I tried playing Doom 3 with a Xbox controller, and it was awful. Playing this on a console is a mistake.
You should play Doom 3. If you pass on it because it's a dumb shooter--I guess you hate shooters. If you pass on it because it has old graphics--it does have old graphics, but at least someone handled all the technical♥♥♥♥♥♥ and your dad's porn box can run it, so you can skip spending $800 on a GeForce Buttcore GTX 9000 (3tb) for performance.
Now I'm gonna play Quake IV since I've had a poster for it in my room for a decade.

Doom: A classic fps with varied monsters, creative levels, and tons of secrets. The varience between the monster weapons (guns, projectiles and melee) is what keeps the monster slaying interesting; Most of the time you will be using the shotgun however because of how the shell boxes are the most abundant ammo pickup (20 shells per box) . You can't look vertically only in a horiztonal axis but after awhile you zone in and don't even notice. 5 out of 5
Doom2: Much like the first doom but with updated monsters and a double barrel shotgun "ohh yeah!".   This was the Doom im most familiar with from my childhood. There are also many secret areas and even secret level in both Dooms. Ammo is often more scarce at the start but the later levels offer more ammo incase you die and need to repeat that stage again (you lose your ammo when you die).
Doom3: A fun run on a space station. The game is pretty good, I tend to enjoy the interactive ingame screens and the audio logs; these were new concepts at the time. However the areas look so similar it gets monotonous just trying to run through the level. They also try to scare you relentlessly with voices and things poping around. This game just lacks the complexity and level design compared to halflife 2.

Great game. Got it on it's release date and played it with one of my friends. For the longest time it became the game we played the most, Co-Op is great and so was the map design.  However at the time of writing this, Left 4 Dead 2 has become the superior game, plus all the Left 4 Dead 1 maps have been ported over to 2. So if you haven't played Left 4 Dead before, head on over to Left 4 Dead 2's page and pick that up instead.

Is the game under-further development? Yes
Is the game currently playable and enjoyable? Yes
Does the game have achievements? Yes
Does the game offer multi-outcomes? Yes and No.
- No, being that once you learn the core of the game, regardless of difficulty you can master success under any option, military, trade, wisdom/lore, or key objective victories.
- Yes, as in out of the 8 games I currently have played, I did indeed find myself defeated in a 1v1 Hard difficult, but I honestly was playing for the long game, AI decided to dash for the easiest win (lore/wisdom victory).
Would I recommend the game? Yes
Do I want the campaign for the game? Yes, as its all I have left..Oh, and multiplayer. They mark it's coming soon.
Overall, if you've ever had the chance to play Settlers 7 Online, this game mirrors the core base building/resource gathering aspect. The game is enjoyable, though I played several games in 2 days (15+ hours) just simply to earn all the achievements. If you're like me and enjoy games more like Total War or other titles that require vast strategy this is a much simplier title strategy game. As I write, the game is enjoyable and exactly what I needed for the weekend. Look forward to more updates and future content.
