I love this game with all my heart! I bought it in early 2014 and it was great!
TLDR: Kind of like the Titanic, great starting product that was sunk by scatter-brained devs...
Imagine a procedurally generated universe with countless planets, monsters, dungeons, weapons and NPC towns that are well built and well decorated! It sounds like a great game. Add seven very unique races with interesting stories (even though the lore is shallow the ideas that are there are great!) You can do almost anything to planets wether building amazing structures or killing everything in sight. It was a great standalone game with a Terraria base but a massive universe! The weapons were interesting even if they were a bit samey...same with monsters. Unique creatures that played well in the game! All around a solid game in early access that was headed for great things!
Why do I not recommed it?
The best discription of this game's dev cycle is the Titanic. A great thing headed for greatness that sunk in a slow and agonizing way...
Chucklefish had a golden ticket with Starbound. A nice looking game with a tried and true formula with a massive universe. Yet they ruined it...my big question is why or how!! After the second to last or last character wipe update (I cant remember which) They removed a great sector by sector "levelling" system. They removed interesting biomes for generic cookie-cutter ones. A previously exploration based game is turned into some awkward quest system which features almost only fetch-quests. The monotony breaks with "missions" that feature easy bosses at the end. These missions are a ho-hum affair that can either be fun or a chore. Said bosses are an improvement to the old-summoned bosses but their missions are very lacklustre. Interesting dungeons in the undergrounds of planets are all but removed being replaced with iffy and somewhat boring new ones. Mining and caving used to be interesting but now are just a chore. The pacing is horrific (snail slow to lightspeed with some progression in the middle). The pickaxe durability is like trying to mine stone with a pick made of glass. The interesting NPC towns are very sparse. The dungeons even more so. They were an interesting element that added life to the universe but now they are so rare that finding one makes you think that they are the last surviving members of their race. The new colony system is interesting and adds to the life of the game. It keeps you working towards something so that endless grinding isn't the only thing you do. I'm semi-interested in the newly added vehicles but am overall left wanting the real Starbound with an identity of its own. Not some fetch-quest based Terraria with a "procedurally generated universe." The sad thing is that it isn't even that anymore. Each star is neutral, radioactive, hot, or cold. With the planets ranging from worryingly easy grassland and desert biomes to generic volcanic planet. Tundra planets, semi-pretty(over saturated or almost green in colour)  "alien planets" and asteriod fields. The ocean planets are intresting for the first two times you visit then they get boring like the rest. You feel like you are exploring the exact same planets after a while with the occasional micro-biome underground or towns.
I feel horrible for giving such a promising game such a bad review but Chucklefish shredded their golden ticket. I miss the old Starbound that had a living, explorable universe that felt new and exciting everywhere you went! The unique monsters native to each planet being completely random and each biome unique and fun to explore. I'm sad this is what became of Starbound.
Long story short: Pick it up with an 80% discount or not at all honestly...sorry Chucklefish...

If you're looking for a classic Burnout game this is NOT it! My overall critique for those that don't want to read the whole Review is, Buy it on sale! The price, at date of review, of $19.99 CAD is too much for what this game is. There are better racing games for the price and I suggest you look at some of them first!
This is an Open World racing game with Burnout-like mechanics. Road Rage is still one of the funnest game types you can play, with Marked Man following a close second, but becomes progressively harder the more you do it. This wouldn't be a bad thing if it allowed you hit as hard or defend as well as the NPC cars. It goes from NPC cars wondering into walls, basically taking themselves down, to almost god-like AI that knows exactly when you plan to boost and/or ram and reacts to you. I fine with a challenge but this is a pathetic substitution for skill/balance.
Navigation in Paradise City is Hit or Miss, mostly miss as in oops I missed my turn! There's a compass/navigator that tells you when to turn but sometimes it doesn't activate until your on top of your turn. It's like driving with that one cousin that points out the side window as you pass your turn to say, "that's the street we were supposed to turn onto!" which blows a substantial lead as you end up in a close 2nd. About as annoying/frustrating as it gets! Also, the races are bland and feel forced. You race because you have to in order to progress and don't get me started on the "Stunt Runs". They are the worst part of this game. There is so much they could have done but didn't do. It's sad really!
I didn't play much of the online portion of the game, as I just don't care for that sort of thing, but from what I could see there was no Party Games which I remember fondly from previous Burnout games. The lack of game modes like Eliminator or Party Crash was a big let down and what is in game for online multiplayer is lack luster at best.
One annoying feature I found is the fact that your car looks half destroyed all the time. After you repair the car it looks nice for about 10 seconds and one bump later it looks like crap again. All this with no penalty outside of Marked Man or Road Rage. Your car never reaches critical and never blows up outside of those two game modes. Also, miraculously, your car seems to auto repair on the fly. How? Why?
That's just one in a long list of annoying features that I won't list. There is one other that I can't ignore and is by far the most annoying thing about this game. As time goes on, and you start progressing your licence, you come across cars in the Open World that you can take down to add to your collection. They get sent to your Junk Yard and can be switched there. This is a cool idea that I like, in fact, I wish there were more cars and that they were harder to take down. Now for the annoying part. During one playthrough I was able to collect 5 unique cars before, progressing to the next level of my licence, and was required to go to the junk yard to switch cars. A crane drops your newly collected car and begins to pan around it to showcase it in all its wrecked glory. Cool I think. Then it does it again for another car, and again for another. All this is unskippable for about 10 seconds each. I want to get back to racing not watch the same cinematic play for 5 different cars.
In conclusion, if you're still reading this, this game is good with some annoying features. It just doesn't feel like a burnout game in many ways. The Overall Racing is bland and the Stunt Run is just not worth mentioning, in fact I wish I could forget it even exists. Road Rage and Marked Man are the most fun and most challenging game modes. The lack of party games, which I fondly remember from previous Burnout tittles, hurts my rating of this game severely! Your car looks like trash all the time and sometimes repairs without reason which is beyond weird. Little annoying features pile up to make a real love/hate feeling.
This game is fun in many ways but because of the little annoyances present in the game plus the lack of other Burnout features make it too hard for me to recommend. The current price of $19.99 CAD is just too much. I suggest waiting for it to go on Sale, until then this game should be avoided.

I was a big fan of C&C: Red Alert 1 and 2 and SC1 back in the day. And it has always bothered me how RTS games haven't really progressed or added many novel ideas since then. The biggest "innovation" was probably WC3, which just fused some light RPG elements in that ultimately became the MOBA genre. But really, RTS didn't change much since the '90s.
THIS game adds a lot of new and very interesting ideas in a way that ends up being quite fun and epic. Spherical maps, controlling units on multiple planets simultaneously with orbital units travelling between them. Even on a single map, there are 5 layers of units: land, air, naval surface, underwater, and orbital. They all have strengths and weaknesses, and you have to pay attention to them all.
As a result, playing this game can be quite demanding on your attention. Fortunately, to simplify things, the developers really emphasized "macro" over "micro"(management of units). The game is about large-scale economy and grand strategy instead of having a quicker mouse finger, a problem Blizzard RTS games suffer from. Even so, traditional notions of RTS defense change drastically when units can come at you from any direction on a planet, or even from orbit. The end result is a game that is very offense and expansion oriented. Resources are scattered throughout the map, so a typical game usually involves some attrition and warring over territory before a direct assault on the opponent's base, which is as it should be.
The music is absolutely amazing and fits the game very well. It greatly adds to the "epic" quality of massive army battles or even planet-destroying laser beams.
The multiplayer scene is active but very small. It's not hard to find a game but you might find yourself playing with the same people more than once.
The  main flaws of the game are:
- The "campaign", called Galactic War, is not well thought-out and is not really a campaign, more of a tutorial really. There is no story whatsoever.
- Only one faction. I don't really mind this as the basic faction has quite a few units and possible strategies, and is overall well balanced. There is a "Legion expansion" mod that is popular that adds a second faction.
- Games with lots of planets tend to lag late in the game. A lot.
- There is a type of planet in the game, "gas giant", that is really broken balance-wise.
- The base AI is not that good, even the hardest modes are not very aggressive or challenging to an experienced RTS player. There is a "Queller AI" mod that improves it considerably.
Overall, I am sad that this game didn't have a better launch, because it's really a fresh breath of air in an otherwise fairly stagnant genre. As others have mentioned, $40 is a bit high. Before Steam, that price would have been justified, but now that there's so much more competition and alternatives for players, I'd put it in the $20-25 "Steam premium" range. If you're an RTS fan, you might wait until it's on sale again, but don't miss it entirely.

Burnout Paradise, oh where to begin...
(Controller Review, I've never touched this game with my M/KB)
This game is wonderful, from the up-to-date(ish) graphics to its still perfectly functioning engine and controls.
You start off as a rookie driver, starting license, starting car... which happens to be a piece of junk.
You complete different kind of events from Road Rages to Marked Man, Stunt events and Casual Races where you get to choose your own path because the entire darn island is your track, your paradise.
You unlock new cars, which will be roaming around Paradise city and you have to take them down before you own them and get the option to drive them.
You get rewarded some new cars instantly when you upgrade your license by completing multiple Events.
This rewarding system makes this game in no way possible... "Boring", it makes it beautifully and generously amazing.
after a few hours of gameplay you can already feel yourself getting better, see yourself getting better, you can gradually see each new car going faster than the previous one which slowly but surely improves your driving skill, guaranteed no matter how bad you are/used to be in racing games.
all in all, this game is a 10/10 would recommend to anyone, fan or not of the Racing Genre.
Also, DLC Related:
If you own the game on Origin, you can buy the DLC for a $1,70 or something... and this will instantly link it through origin to your EA account in Paradise City.
Afterwards, when you run Paradise City through steam and log in to your EA account.. the DLC will be on your game, even on Steam.
So if you ever bought the Humble Origin Bundle, use that Origin key because it's still working! I just tried mine 1-6-2016.
Otherwise you should buy the game on Origin as well, sorry :(

Perfect example of a greedy publisher (Bethesda) rereleasing games to make money off a relatively newly acquired developer (id Software).
Basically nothing is changed or remastered, Doom 1 & 2 + Expansion run on Dosbox instead of upgrading them at all (even though there are OpenGL ports but whatever). Doom 3 & it's expansions include an annoying bug where you can't take screenshots otherwise it disables achievements (because it thinks you are cheating in console) which requires exiting the game and restarting.
Doom 3 Multiplayer is non existant, gone is the server browser and replaced with a poorly implemented Quick Match option, but it doesn't matter because there is nobody playing online (except for like a few servers in Europe)
This is supposed to be a proper Steam release and "BFG Edition" but it's clear that Bethesda & Zenimax wanted to milk as much money out of id Software while spending as little time & money doing QA as humanly possible.
It is possibly the most disappointing title in my library, not only because I love the Doom series and have been playing them for years, but also due to lazy development and lack of potential/polish.
I can only recommend this for nostalgia, as your money can buy multiple indie games or one whole decent retail game for this price.
The BFG in this "edition" stands for Big, Fat & Greedy which is what Bethesda & Zenimax should consider themselves for rereleasing such a nostalgic game series in such a poor state, without a care in the world for what fans may think.
Doom deserves better than this.

Northgard is a live action civilization, with charming visuals, music and game mechanics. Love it. Can't wait for future updates.

Updated Review:
"I am Vegend" is a poor attempt at merging the concepts of two widely viral games: Angry Birds + Plants vs. Zombies. Don't let the cartoon graphics fool you, this game was poorly designed and executed. It lacks even the most basic of functions such as the ability to adjust volume. You may either mute or unmute, that is all.
Gameplay remains unresponsive and laggy, especially as the game progresses and more units flood the screen. Ultimately, there is no strategy to gameplay. The launching of units does not require hard precision (as compared to Angry Birds) and the replenishment of units makes placing them simply a timing-response function. In other words, I found myself just clicking furiously rather than employing any real game tactics. I cannot recommend this game as it was not enjoyable to play.

Here's the rundown of Starbound and why it's getting a negative review. This will perhaps change in the future.
The first, big reason is due to the state of early access. It's been two years now since it was released to early access on Steam and nothing major has really changed. Some will argue against that but no, nothing big has changed. It's the same ship designs, the same races and the same idea that is, in basic, Terraria in space. The same bosses have mostly existed since it was released as have the modules that the player uses, the weapons, the way NPCs act and monsters.
What has changed?
Pros?
Cons? There's quite a few IMHO
False advertising how? The starbound website boasts of a sandbox game with quests scattered around the universe. This of course is not true. While playing the game, encountering various towns of NPCs, I found not one offering a quest. The towns themselves were intriguing enough and had a few merchants vending different items but nobody offered any quests. The only way to find a quest is to go to the central hub. The most in depth the quests get, however, are "Help, I lost my paper" or "oh no the mine is under attack go get better armor and fight the thing" followed by expanding your ship. The website also boasts of a story, but the most in depth the story goes is "You're ship crash lands".
As this is a sandbox game and a crafting game how well done is said crafting? Crafting items is about as linear as you can get here. "Get better metal to make better armor and weapons" rinse and repeat. What differs from Starbound and Terraria is the tools, though. In Starbound making tools such as a diamond pickaxe is worthless, you have matter manipulator that does everything for you and is more powerful than any of the tools you can craft by the time you are finding any sort of ore. There is VERY little difference from Terraria crafting and Starbound crafting; Though you do need more supplies and parts in Terraria whereas you don't in Starbound.
TL;DR?

The game is immense and easily my favorite car game of all time.
75 cars in the basic pack, each with a basic "Type" which is how it accumulates boost. You'll be doing a lot of boosting. And they all feel a little different than one another. They have since added several different packs of cars, so many that I honestly can't count, with their own challenges. Every stoplight in the game is a different mission.
The game itself is pretty straightforward, there's a location at each compass point of the city at which all the challenges end, and they come in a few different flavors loosely coinciding with the car types.
Beyond that, drive around a big♥♥♥♥♥city at enormous speed, creating breathtaking car crashes and listening to classic rock and trying to get your next car unlock.
Cons: Not gameplay related, but rather EA's ♥♥♥♥♥♥ port programming. You will probably need to configure your own controls, although the game makes it pretty painless. I also had a problem caused by the game's attempt to take my picture for my driver's license (don't bother, it's VERY glitchy, but a cool idea)--every time I tried to open the menu it would crash. Fixed it by turning off the webcam driver (I don't have a webcam) in my control panel and it's been running smoothly ever since.
Anyway, technical problems aside, this is the Skyrim of car games and you should get it if you have even a passing interest. I don't like racing games but I love this damn game. For 5$ in a sale, it's a no-brainer.
Edit: in case you were concerned that my playtime is too low to be this positive, I have at least 30-40 hours on the XBox version. I was very happy to return it to my library on steam by buying it a second time.

The game first off is simply epic, especially later on. The longer a match lasts the more epic the clashes all throuout the map become. If you last REALLY long sometimes entire planets become a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥of explosions and mayhem. Which is fantastic, its visually entertaining to watch and also entertaining to be a part of. Another brick in LEGO’s wall of games. In my opinion, The LEGO Movie Videogame is just another LEGO game; and thus has all the fun things you’d come to expect from one. Everything is good, well written and fun. The story is basically the same as the movie with a few minor changes to fit the game format. The gameplay is what you would expect, fun co-op, puzzle solving and of course, smashing everything in sight. The game has a semi-open world, that is very diverse, ranging from literal sunshines and rainbows to the desert heat of the wild west.
The most defining feature of this game is the visual style, borrowed from the movie. Most LEGO games tend to have a mix of brick built objects and non-brick objects. However, this one stands out; due to being visually represented entirely by LEGO elements (save for the bonus level). Even the character animations are decisively LEGO, differing greatly from how characters move in other LEGO games.
Unfortunately, aside from its distinct style, The LEGO Movie Videogame is just another LEGO game. It doesn’t change much from the formula and as such feels like an almost copy and paste from other previous games. There’s nothing wrong with the game, it’s just… average. There’s just not enough to make it stand out in the crowd of LEGO games. It’s not bad or below standard, just… average.
All in all, if you like LEGO games then, let’s face it, you’ve probably already bought this game. If you don’t mind the occasional LEGO game then there are better LEGO games to play. That’s not to say i don’t recommend getting this game, it still has its merit and is just as good as any LEGO game before it. So if you see it on sale, just give it a go; you won't be disappointed.

This is one Lego-@ssLego game. I say that very deliberately. I love Lego games. I played every single one to 100% up until LoTR and have played a smattering to 100% since then.
Lego games are a blast. They're super formulaic. Destroy, build, run around collecting stuff and find hidden things. I love the cutesy sense of humor that these games bring to the table. Before the days when the Lego games included voice acting, there was such a great charm in the way the characters moved around to convey the mood. Despite voice acting, that is still there. This game is no different. They took a great movie and turned it into a full length lego game.
The HUB world is huge, but this game followed the LoTR and Harry Potter style of adding ghost coins to follow in order to know where to go. The vehicles handle beautifully. The character purchasing is done from a menu in this game instead of running around on a wild goose chase.
Now the bad: This IS a Lego-ey Lego game. Which means it will feel that no one ever beta tested it. When I played Lego Potter (1-4), I had a game breaking glitch. I restarted the game. I had a completely different game breaking glitch. Same That's the only Lego game I have ever played and not played to 100%. The bad news: While playing this, I have hit almost a dozen glitches and I have not even finished story mode yet. Cut scenes won't load, areas don't register so I can't enter them, it will show I have to kill enemies but none will spawn. Worst of all, when I save and exit the level, it doesn't remember my progress. The good news is these aren't game breaking problems (yet). Each time I find these issues, I quit out and the bug is gone the next time I play.
I recommend this game as a Lego game. It does exactly what you would expect from this style of game. It's light hearted, fun, charming and addictive. It is also incredibly glitchy, like most Lego games. Play this at your own risk!

If you're still considering L4D then read on (if anyone will see this review now :/ )
Left 4 Dead is a FPS set in a zombie apocalypse.
The game is split into campaigns whether you're playing, VS mode, co-op or single player. It's a FPS where team work is paramount regardless if you're playing as one of the survivors or the zombies.
There are four difficulty levels for single player and co-op; Easy, Normal, Advanced and Expert. Be aware that friendly fire is activated on normal, and that it reaches deadly levels on expert.
In single player and co-op you pick a campaign that acts like its own mini story of escape. There's no actual story to speak of, just get to the finale, hold out against the horde until the escape vehicle arrives and get on it without dying. The lack of a story is not a bad thing as the aforementioned objectives are so much fun in a team. You need to stick together as there are special zombies that can incapacitate you, and only another survivor can push them off/kill them when this happens. Those who run ahead quickly become easy prey so stick close to your team mates. At the end of each level prior to the finale your objective is to reach the next 'safe room'. This is a room stocked with weapons and medical items that will prepare you for the next level.
On the levels leading up to the finale there are 'panic events' you can't avoid that help up the pace of the game so you don't get to comfortable. Like on the No Mercy campaign when you activate a lift. The noise calls a massive, continuous horde of zombies that you have to gun down while huddled in a corner and then make a run for the lift.
The 'AI Director', as its called can also call hordes based on how well/badly your team is doing. It also does nice things like placing med kits if you're having bad luck. This variety of item and zombie spawning is part of what gives the Left 4 Dead series its amazing replay value. 'Special Infected' rarely appear in the same places, items are found in differing areas and the thrill of being one of the survivors to escape keeps you coming back again and again. This and the hordes coming in at different times each play through, means that you'll have to keep your guard up just as well on the 100th time you enter an area, as you did the first time. This is why the replay value is so great.
Multiplayer see's two teams of four players take turns as survivors and zombies (or 'infected') on each level. Points are scored when it’s your turn to be the survivors. Your aim is to get the end of each level. The further you get, the more points you get. The special infected you play as are well balanced. There's the Smoker who has a super long tongue that he can wrap around survivors, dragging them back and choking the life out of them. The hunter is fast and agile and pounces directly onto survivors, causing massive damage. Then there is the boomer. If he vomits on or otherwise explodes on any number of survivors a horde is called. While survivors are blinded by puke. Nice. Finally we have the Tank. A huge brute of a zombie which can rip up the ground to throw and has super powerful punches. He is a much rarer spawn. There is also the Witch but you can't be her in multiplayer.
I have to say the one and only let down in multiplayer is the community. It’s awful. The kick feature is abused for genuine mistakes (even if you only make a single mistake) and it’s become a haven for the most anti social internet cowards. You have been warned.
Survival mode is your basic horde mode. Survive as long as you can against never ending waves of zombies. There are a large amount of maps on offer.

I have to say this is the type of RTS i've been waiting for.  Only issue is no dong slider. Lets get right into it.
Pros
Strategic game play requires you to not only fend off the enemies but you are also suriving against your own economy. Your buildings will burn, your people will startve, your clan will freeze and all new members will cease to join your clan if you cant manage this.
Beautiful game play and graphics. You dont have any down time you will always have an objective to take or something to be mindfull of.

Cons.
Game pace is a little slow but I can understand the reasons behind it. This is much more micro involved once you get your inital food hold.
Lack of hotkeys afik
The more land you control the more expensive it is to conquer a new zone. Meanwhile when you are pushing in an enemy if you cant afford to conquer it they can for relatively no cost once you get closer to their base so a lot of time is wasted recapping zones back and forth between you and them so you can push in. You can however leave a unit in the zone and they cant cap it until that unit dies.
Lack of combat units. Only 1 meele unit aside from the beserker and the warlord.
lack of technology upgrades to counter play your enemy.
Healers heal many zones away as long as its inyour territory allowing your unites to get healed in battle when pushing as long as you are in a friendly zone.
Resources do not deplete except for mining nodes. Once they are used there is not getting more on the map. You can buy more from a market but it takes a while to generate the resources.
Unit growth seems slow in terms of gaining more units.
nothing really offputting just some balancing issues.
Suggestions
Increase unit production 20-30% This will increase the speed of gameplay. Currently 1 map can take nearly two hours.
Healers should only heal the zone they are built in much like towers only defend their zone.
Add weapon upgrades in game aside from the lore tech.
Add more units to allow for counter play. maybe a trifecta of sorts.  1 beats 2 but two beats 3 and 3 beats 1
WIll be adding more.

After playing a few skirmashes, I can pretty much tell you this : it's a downgraded Civilization except it's in real time.
Here's why
-Very buggy AI.. you make friends only to find out your friends will randomly attack you for no good reason, yet after the war is over, you maintain good relationships with them
-Wait, did I say war? war only lasts about 2 minutes because the AI runs out of warriors and decides to concede.
-There are only 3 clans so far (which isn't bad, I promise) But AI doesn't depend on the clan they have, it's all completely random.
-I love the idea of having neutral tribes that you can eventually develop a friendship with so that they join you, but it takes ingame years, good luck actually getting them before someone else (or you) achieves victory.
-The game even reuses some very obvious Civ sound files, like when your villagers get angry.
-The lore system doesn't really make any sense (this is basically your technologies that you upgrade) because you can go all over the place and each branch doesn't have a common theme, it's just random traits placed in a row.
For an early access game, I can tell you that I really respect what the devs are doing here, but A LOT of it feels like a rehash, I found myself longing for other top-down strategy games like Rome, Supreme Commander, Command&Conquer etc. because they did the job first and they did it right.

Fun game for those who enjoy war strategy and economy balance. You have the choice to play in random matches but with friends is where this game's fun truly lies. Being able to creat teams and work together to plan massive armies is an experience that is worth your time. The troops are varied enough to keep things conplex and interesting, and with the map varieties, certain troop classes will excel above others. One issue to be had is when you play with someone competent enough to drag the game out into the 40 50 60 minute mark. If you like Doom - DON'T BUY THIS BFG EDITION !!! JUST DON'T!
The BFG Edition includes:
- Doom 1 and Doom 2 playable fom the startscreen of the game.
- Doom 3 Console Edition which is less creepy and brighter than the original.
- Doom 3 Resurection of Evil (The Addon)
- Lost Mission (7 or 8 new SinglePlayer maps)
- A few Achievments for Doom 1, 2 and 3 + Multiplayer
The first thing i notice during playing the first chapter of Doom 3 is that everything is brighter and the textures don't look as good as they are in my memories. Also a shotgun mod I used years ago diden't work so I did a research on the BFG edition. The BFG edition is a port of the Xbox and PS edition of Doom 3. They portet the game to a newer engine that is also used in the game RAGE. I guess that's why the models are not as good as the 2004 PC edition, thats why everything is brighter ergo less creepy and thats why it's maybe not possible to mod the game after all.
That means no Hi-Def Texturepacks or any other graphic booster mod will work. The source code of the BFG edition was released but that don't change the fact that the beautifull graphic mods won't work at all.
So if you really like DOOM, buy the original PC edition and the Addon + the Doom 1 and 2 pack and you get a creepy game, modable that it looks like modern games and the classic DOOM levels PLUS you safe yourself some money!
About Doom 3 itself:
----------------------------------------
In the year 2094 or so supplies on earth runns out and humanity is trying to convert moon sand or in this case mars sand into water and fuel. They build a large station on mars with research facilities, fuel and water generators and so.
The crew somehow begin to act crazy and some rumors are all over the station, so you, a marine, came along to find some guy that is missing and the game begins.
It's like a merge of Half Life, Deadspace and SystemShock 2. At the end you carrie more than 9 weapons. the PDA system allows you to read e-mails or listen to audio-logs of many PDA's you (need to) find. Many of them contain information to open key-coded doors or lockers. The flashlight is your best friend since the station is falling apart. The enemy spawn system is a bit oldsql but with the dark levels and the near invisible enemies, it's creepy like Deadspace.
The story is pretty solid and reminds a bit of Half Life 1. So you start with no gun at a "normal" day of work and it turns all into a big action loaded horror game. There are also noticeable Doom 1 elements in Doom 3. For example the fireball throwing enemie and the marine-zombies.
If you like horror generes, if you liked doom and if you are willing to download some extra texture packs, this is classic egoshooter game for you that brings really fun and can easely be moded to look like actual shooters. but DON'T buy the BFG edition like I did ;-)

The LEGO Movie Videogame is another game in the prolific Lego Platformer series. Just like with most of them, they are simple, fun, and easy. This is the optimal "feel-good" game in my opinion. One that you can quickly beat in a few days, and complete shortly after. One thing I've always enjoyed about this games are the way they let you break the game with the strongest characters the game has to offer. This game is no different, and is still quite enjoyable.
However, if you do not find the characters charming in any way, you will be quickly annoyed by how often they talk during levels. Offering quips, moral support, and hand-holding throughout each of the 15 levels. I personally found it a little much near the end, but it is a children's game after all.
If you're looking for something new from the Lego games, this one isn't the one you are looking for. But if you are looking for a fun, simple, and enjoyable game, then this is for you. It's a bonus if you enjoyed the Lego Movie as well!

After playing a few skirmashes, I can pretty much tell you this : it's a downgraded Civilization except it's in real time.
Here's why
-Very buggy AI.. you make friends only to find out your friends will randomly attack you for no good reason, yet after the war is over, you maintain good relationships with them
-Wait, did I say war? war only lasts about 2 minutes because the AI runs out of warriors and decides to concede.
-There are only 3 clans so far (which isn't bad, I promise) But AI doesn't depend on the clan they have, it's all completely random.
-I love the idea of having neutral tribes that you can eventually develop a friendship with so that they join you, but it takes ingame years, good luck actually getting them before someone else (or you) achieves victory.
-The game even reuses some very obvious Civ sound files, like when your villagers get angry.
-The lore system doesn't really make any sense (this is basically your technologies that you upgrade) because you can go all over the place and each branch doesn't have a common theme, it's just random traits placed in a row.
For an early access game, I can tell you that I really respect what the devs are doing here, but A LOT of it feels like a rehash, I found myself longing for other top-down strategy games like Rome, Supreme Commander, Command&Conquer etc. because they did the job first and they did it right.

It has its fairly fun moments though. I mean, it's decent and solid, but it's just not a game I'd personally put on a pedestal, as something that people really should experience. Plus Left 4 Dead 2 includes everything here and has more going for it in general, so if you're interested in buying one of these games, it might as well be that one.

Gameplay-wise it is exactly what the newer GTA games are: you have an open world game where you go wherever you want and you can do whatever you want. Of course, doing some hit-and-runs will only anger local police so they'll be after you pretty quickly. You can approach icons scattered throughout the game that launch missions - those that are essential to the main story progress are indicated by a different icon than those who serve to be side missions only.
There are TONS of things to do in Hong Kong: you can participate in racing games, sing at karaoke parties, date girls, bet on cockfights, join a fight club. You also have hundreds of collectable items. It's worth participating in all these activities as the game rewards you with experience points that let you level up only to learn new abilities.
In GTA you you had an assortment of firearms available for you to use. Here, emphasis is on hand-to-hand combat. Learning new abilities makes martials arts even better. Carjacking is also available but can happen much faster than in GTA - you can jump into vehicles and there are also car chase sequences in the game.
Story-wise you play Wei Shen, an undercover cop, who climbs the criminal corporate ladder only to get closer to the bad guys he needs to expose. There are some nice surprises here and there and just like GTA this game can also steal around 40 to 50 hours from your life.
A highly recommended game if you liked GTA IV or any of its third-person shooter predecessors.

Sleeping Dogs is truly one of the best games I have ever played and I look forward to its sequel.
The melee combat is combo-based and has devastating moves, such as "environmental attacks", you can literally use anything around you: Pick someone up and throw them into a tank of electric eels, smash them into a glass fish tank, throw them against a bare industrial fuse box, hang them on a meat hook, burn their face on a barbecue/stove, push their head towards a table saw and even brutally impale them onto a pallet loaded with upturned swordfish heads.
It is all very dynamic and fluid and the graphics are stunning and really portray both aspects of Hong Kong, rich and poor, in a very astounding manner with its neon signs, parks, restauarants, clothes shops and other things. The gun combat is very fun as you can slow motion vault and jump off anything whilst getting those crucial headshots. The plot is very deep and leaves you hanging on the edge of your seat all the time and there are a lot of side missions too, where you can upgrade both your face level (respect, public image), your police level (by completing drug busts and police missions.), your martial arts skills (by finding jade statues scattered around Hong Kong and bringing them back to your old martial arts teacher in exchange for learning new fighting techniques) and even compete in illegal street races and get faster cars. You also get emotionally attached with the characters like you actually know them and everything seems familiar after a while.
I would strongly recommend you buy this game, whether you've played other titles like it (True Crime series, what the game was originally going to be made part of but then it was fully changed) or not, I think everyone can love this game <3

IMPORTANT UPDATE: Capcom implemented (and already removed) an update that installed what is essentially a rootkit in your system32 folder. Sure they removed it pretty fast after the whole thing blew up in their faces but this goes to show they're not above doing something as questionable as this.
I would further emphasize to think long and hard before giving money to developers like this.
On top of this the netcode still hasn't improved from when I last tested it out.
---------------
Street Fighter V has the potential to be a great game but currently it's just far too broken to recommend unless you're SPECIFICALLY buying it to play offline only with friends and/or a local scene.
The netcode is just flat out broken; opponents keep warping around the screen, animations don't play out and you get hit out of nowhere. You can hit an opponent and confirm into a combo and the game will roll back and suddenly you're the one eating a combo. This doesn't happen for me every game but FAR too often to be acceptable. Even when the warping isn't quite as bad, it still makes for a very annoying experience.
I was also hoping the story mode would add something fun to do but it was a chore to play through and even there the game kept freezing for the first few seconds of every match and in a few select places I saw some of the worst texture quality since the 90s even on maxed settings. The texture complaint is very very minor but it really makes me wonder did Capcom even try? With that said the plot itself was nothing to write home about.
Apart from the broken online mode and seriously lacking story mode you have:
The training mode which is very well implemented in my opinion, offering options I haven't seen in many fighting games such as recording an action for the CPU to do after it blocks or gets knocked down.
Survival which you can play to unlock colours for all the characters you own. It should be mentioned that this mode redefines the word 'grind'. You choose a difficulty and then beat all the stages in it, for example the 10 stages easy mode has and after you complete the difficulty, you unlock the colours. The problem is that if you lose at any point (the matches are only 1 round), you have to start ALL OVER. This becomes incredibly frustrating when you're trying to fight up to level 50 when the CPU starts blatantly reading your inputs at level 30. The game mode does nothing to teach you how the game works, apart from how to abuse the AI.
And finally the biggest culprit apart from the messy netcode: the loading times. There is no reason this game should spend so much time loading different screens. If you chain online matches together as fast as you can, you're still spending a quarter of your time staring at a loading screen and this is what the game installed on an SSD drive.
Soon you won't even want to go to the training room while searching for a match because loading into it takes about as long as finding a match would.
Unless Capcom fixes the netcode issues (bonus points for doing something about the loading times) I cannot recommend this game unless it is - as previously mentioned - solely for offline play.

Town of Salem is a great game about trust and betrayl between a group of random strangers with differeing goals. Much like the actual witch trials, suspicion and fear drive the motives of the sheep towns folk while the killers try to slaughter everyone that stands against them.

Fun and easy to get the basics

CONS-
The biggest con and huge flaw of this game is that once you die there is no exit button from the game. It is not 100% that there is a Medium (the character who can talk to dead players) so sitting and waiting for the game to end is boring. I see why keeping players in the game would be crucial (in order to make the Medium role not completely uselss by all dead people leaving) but this game matches players with people who play the browser version as well. The players who play through the browser simply refresh the page and get out of the game.
Small suggestion-
I would suggest a purgatory turn mechanic. Once a player dies, they have to stay in the game as a dead person for 3-5 turns before they have the option to exit. That way, Medium and Retributionist roles aren't useless but people don't have to stay for the full game if they get killed early. This small change would make this game much better.

Here's the rundown of Starbound and why it's getting a negative review. This will perhaps change in the future.
The first, big reason is due to the state of early access. It's been two years now since it was released to early access on Steam and nothing major has really changed. Some will argue against that but no, nothing big has changed. It's the same ship designs, the same races and the same idea that is, in basic, Terraria in space. The same bosses have mostly existed since it was released as have the modules that the player uses, the weapons, the way NPCs act and monsters.
What has changed?
Pros?
Cons? There's quite a few IMHO
False advertising how? The starbound website boasts of a sandbox game with quests scattered around the universe. This of course is not true. While playing the game, encountering various towns of NPCs, I found not one offering a quest. The towns themselves were intriguing enough and had a few merchants vending different items but nobody offered any quests. The only way to find a quest is to go to the central hub. The most in depth the quests get, however, are "Help, I lost my paper" or "oh no the mine is under attack go get better armor and fight the thing" followed by expanding your ship. The website also boasts of a story, but the most in depth the story goes is "You're ship crash lands".
As this is a sandbox game and a crafting game how well done is said crafting? Crafting items is about as linear as you can get here. "Get better metal to make better armor and weapons" rinse and repeat. What differs from Starbound and Terraria is the tools, though. In Starbound making tools such as a diamond pickaxe is worthless, you have matter manipulator that does everything for you and is more powerful than any of the tools you can craft by the time you are finding any sort of ore. There is VERY little difference from Terraria crafting and Starbound crafting; Though you do need more supplies and parts in Terraria whereas you don't in Starbound.
TL;DR?

Sleeping Dogs is truly one of the best games I have ever played and I look forward to its sequel.
The melee combat is combo-based and has devastating moves, such as "environmental attacks", you can literally use anything around you: Pick someone up and throw them into a tank of electric eels, smash them into a glass fish tank, throw them against a bare industrial fuse box, hang them on a meat hook, burn their face on a barbecue/stove, push their head towards a table saw and even brutally impale them onto a pallet loaded with upturned swordfish heads.
It is all very dynamic and fluid and the graphics are stunning and really portray both aspects of Hong Kong, rich and poor, in a very astounding manner with its neon signs, parks, restauarants, clothes shops and other things. The gun combat is very fun as you can slow motion vault and jump off anything whilst getting those crucial headshots. The plot is very deep and leaves you hanging on the edge of your seat all the time and there are a lot of side missions too, where you can upgrade both your face level (respect, public image), your police level (by completing drug busts and police missions.), your martial arts skills (by finding jade statues scattered around Hong Kong and bringing them back to your old martial arts teacher in exchange for learning new fighting techniques) and even compete in illegal street races and get faster cars. You also get emotionally attached with the characters like you actually know them and everything seems familiar after a while.
I would strongly recommend you buy this game, whether you've played other titles like it (True Crime series, what the game was originally going to be made part of but then it was fully changed) or not, I think everyone can love this game <3

This is a Doom trilogy of games that spans more than a decade. It includes Doom 3 HD, Doom 3: Resurrection of Evil, the Doom 3 Lost Mission (8 level pack), Doom 2, Doom 2: No Rest for the Wicked and Ultimate Doom 1. The major focus on this is the HD version of Doom 3. For those of you who don't know, its an action FPS, but with how dark, slow and gory it is I'd say its more of a survival horror FPS. This version plays better than the original Doom 3, just with the tweaks such as using a gun and a flash light instead of one or the other. The movement speed has been improved, an autosave function is in there too as well along with numerous other things you'll never notice. Even these small tweaks make the game just seem more fun and less challenging. The downside is no mods like the original Doom 3. Sure people will still complain about how pitch black it can be without a light, the weapons not having an impact and the numerous monster closets, but this is a good game in my opinion.
As a game, Doom 3 has more of a story to it, which it didn't need. You're the new guy on Mars and within a level or two of getting acclimated, eventually fit hits the shan and you'll be battling zombies, mutants and creatures from Hell or Mars. Whichever. The game really stands on its horrific graphics, even after all of these years. While the action is slower than the old Doom games and it does feel like a very straight forward game with far less linear levels than the original, there are places to explore and puzzles to solve.
Since it is Mars, you'll get to walk the surface of the planet where you'll need Oxygen to survive. You'll also experience a really awesome level in Hell, but mostly you're inside of futuristic bases. With such a long 20 hour game, the metallic walls, dark ambient lighting and pipes all begin to feel the same. Sure there are different colors, med labs, offices, boiler rooms and scenes of blood and mutilation, but its over and over again. A lot of it feels like you're in a diesel submarine fighting creatures.
You'll start with a pistol and move on to a machine gun, shotgun and a chaingun. Eventually, you'll find the rocket launcher, plasma launcher, BFG and grenades. The weapons don't feel that good or impactful. Shooting a shotgun close range will do far more damage than long range, unlike the original Doom 1 that you could snipe with it. The grenades don't feel that good to use, because they are their own weapon not some secondary weapon like in most games where you throw it. That makes the grenades feel useless unless you need to drop a grenade to a monster below. Eventually you'll find 'the Artifact' that can be thrown as a bladed weapon, bouncing off of walls and shredding through enemies.
Enemies come in a variety of sizes. Big bulbous cacodemos fly around shooting balls of lightning, mancubus are fat and take a lot of bullets while their dual cannons bellow fireballs. A towering, rocket shooting horn headed cyberdemon. Flying skulls, six legged human head spiders. A boss that is half man half tank and little half baby half insect creatures. It is all beautiful, grotesque horror that debuts each creature with a brief cut scene. That's something the first game didn't have. Cut scenes. There are a few story cut scenes, but thankfully they are less and less frequent.
Each of the enemies has a revamp. Enemies are somewhat intelligent, while zombies will just come shambling toward you, smarter enemies will hide and take cover. They'll eve awkwardly sidestep your bullets. The levels just never really accentuate the enemy intelligence. Most levels are straight forward, so everything will be dead with no chance to flank you or get behind you organically. There are still monster closets, doors that open up behind you and have enemies or some enemies like imps will just teleport in behind you. Some found it annoying.
BFG Edition also comes with the expansion pack Resurrection of Evil for Doom 3. This is a good sized campaign that introduces the double barreled shotgun and a grabber gun, similar to the Half Life gravity gun that will allow you to grab barrels and enemy projectiles to throw at enemies. That's not the only similarity between the Half Life games, the wall health and Doom 3's story seems to have been inspired by Half Life 1. The expansion pack also offers more abilities that will allow you to slow time, give invulnerability and give berserk which doubles your weapon power. Each ability will help you deal with the new bosses in the game and traverse the levels.
Now for the big reason Doom 3 fans would get this game, the new expansion / level pack called 'the Lost Levels.' Is it worth $20? no. Is it worth $10? Probably not, but there is still a lot of value with the whole package.
Next up are the first two Doom games all the way back from 1994 and 1995. The Ultimate Doom is 4 episodes of Doom 1. The first 3 episodes of 8 - 9 levels each and a bonus episode. Its still every bit as fun as it was back then. Bright, vibrant, you move like a racecar, great enemy variety and weapons. The levels feel open and offer a lot of variety. You'll collect keys and open doors, pull switches. You can do everything easily and freely. You can snipe with a shotgun or pistol. There is no vertical mouse aim. If you are horizontally aimed at an enemy and shoot, your bullets will go up or down toward the enemy.
Doom 2 is also the same engine as Doom 1, but with more enemy types and 32 levels all in 1 episode. But wait, there's a bonus episode of 8 levels from 2010 made for X-Box Live. This 8 level pack has great detailed maps with a good challenge for veterans.
On top of that, the original 2 Dooms, there are 20 levels of extra levels, some of which are awesome others.... not so much. While there are mods for Doom 3, for whatever reason, mod support IS NOT IN DOOM 3 BFG. Not sure why, but whatever.
In all, its worth $10, maybe even $20, but wait for a sale. Chances are anyone interested in Doom has already had the first two games. This is a quick cash grab from iD. Everything is still a lot of fun to play especially with Doom 3's tweaks, but just wait for a sale.

Normally I don't care too much about tower defense games. I always felt helpless during the waves as I watch the enemies go through the defenses and I'd lose. I'm certain the developers had a train of thought similar to that when they made this game.
Sanctum 2 perked my interest, and I picked it up on sale. Without a doubt it is the best game purchase I have made so far this year. Every stage has countless strategies you can try on it. One can easily spend hours tinkering around with different tower strategies. On top of the countless tower strategies are character builds. With the variety of characters, guns, and perks one can create a character build that would suit their play style. The stages themselves are breathtaking. Each one has so many nooks and crannies to explore while building. Sometimes I pause between waves just to admire the scenery.
The game also has a simple, but interesting story with it that does a good job of fleshing out the world and characters.
My adivce to others is to definently play this game with others, it is much more enjoyable experience. That goes double for when you are playing with all 5 Feats of Strength. Beating stages with 5 FoS alone is a challenging endevor. Many hours I have spent trying to beat a single stage; the slightest slip up can force you to start over. Sometimes I even had to rethink my entire tower build. All together it can easily drive you insane. Honestly if it wasn't for the Tactical Juxaposition + Drone Launcher combination, I don't even think some of these stages are possible to beat with 5 FoS alone.
I'll admit I have never played the original Sanctum, so I have nothing to compare it to, but from what I see the 'FPS' portion of this game takes a little more active role compared to the original.
Coffee Stain Studios has done a fantastic job crafting this unique Tower Defense/FPS hybrid game. I'll be following their future projects closely.

---=Original=---
After enjoying the gorgeous and insanely fun prequel, I bought this game as a 4 pack. After the tedious downloading of 8GB across 500kB/sec, we finally get to play.
Storyline: 8/10
It goes without saying that CoffeeStain has done a stellar job at creating characters and art. Being the writer that I am, I felt cheated by the fact that the gameplay masked the plot holes I broke my neck falling into.
You start off saving the day as Skye. Obviously something horrible happened to her to have such a scar across her face. No clues or hints as to what happened there.
We're intoduced to 3 more of the cast, Sweet, SIMO, and Hagen. Each have a primary gun perk and attitudes to match.
Game Play: 5/10
Maze game, cant get any simpler right? WRONG!! We started off thinking this would be cake. New guns, towers, etc.
-You're capped at 10 turrets per map. Yes TEN!! You're then left to fend off the waves of Lume's with you, your guns, and your friends guns.
+With the limited number of turrets available, all you can do is direct traffic.
+Crushing your friends with your deployables? Priceless
+New turrets are wonderful. They're a bit more intelligent at what to shoot.
-Bosses are interesting, but a few are just OP. Many of them you have to shoot them in what looks like their mating orifice! Eeww! Just wrong. Minus one point.
+Perks are a nice touch, but many just dont make a toot worth of difference.
-You have to wait to reinforce. No more instant respawn.
-Turrets and walls can be destroyed
-TIME LIMITS!! If you hate deadlines, then you're going to hate this. Every checkpoint is time-limited. You have 100 seconds or so to do something, then get to a defensible position. The few 2 or 3 waves between are not limited. No option to turn this off.
General notes:
To say the least, the game was absurdly more difficult than before. Now you have to think about diagonal connections, not just left or right turns. The AI controlled minions that you'd typically find cowering in their bright orange suits, are actually taking up guns and doing something other than looking like static scenery and poor typists.
We did not finish the game. We were left demanding 'm0ar!!', if not a partial refund. Shortly after, DLC was released. At its (still the same) price, it was simply not worth it. The first was more fun.

TL:DR: Avoid this game at all costs. For now.
So, I really liked Starbound. I love the CONCEPT of Starbound. The idea that you can look around countless worlds and find new and weird randomly generated stuff is such a great concept to me. The races are appealing too from a character design standpoint, and the worlds (at one point at least) were fun and interesting. It was the makings of a perfect game, at least for me.
So, why am I not recommending it?
In short, the problem is that the developer, Chucklefish, has seriously mismanaged the project. Let me be clear, it's only the developers that are holding this back. The concept and world they've built is strong. They just seem to enjoy pulling anything unique out and making the game bland and generic. I would strongly recommend this game when Chucklefish either goes bankrupt and sells the assets or if a new development team comes in. Let's go through a list of changes.
1. Monsters are no longer all randomly generated. They added "hand-crafted" monsters to most worlds. If the ridiculous hipster name didn't turn you off, the mundane attacks will. They add nothing to the game, but they were heralded as a great feature.
2. Damage on contact. This was in the game when I first started and it was annoying. They removed it in favor of combat using tells from the monsters and dodging attacks. They then added this back in for no reason. This is the biggest reason I have for abandoning the game. The game is not built for damage on contact. You have to move the (barely visible) cursor to one side or the other of your character, otherwise moving backwards makes you crawl like a snail. When the combat was all about dodging, this was great because it meant you could jump out of the way of an attack and use that time to get yourself back under control. Now, that's impossible because, if you jump, you then have to spend all your attention trying to NOT land on the stupid thing. Keep in mind that almost all monsters are faster than you and will run to your position making this a futile endevour. FUN!
3. They're taking the exploration out of the game. What used to be a fun trek to see what you could find on a planet's surface has devolved into exploring a world to see what micro-"dungeons" (loot rooms) have spawned there. Given that there are only a handful of potential microdungeon themes, you're done pretty quickly. As a minor side note, they went over random weapons and turned them from cute rusted weapons that made sense... into a series of pallate swaps. "Oh boy, I found a random axe! Unlike my current random axe, this one has a blue spiky head instead of a red swooshy head."
4. They've taken out interesting summoned bosses and have given us bland, fairly easy boss "quests". Don't get me wrong, the summoned bosses were terrible. Mostly because you could cheese them really easily. But they needed tweaking, not removal.
5. Content removal. There used to be tentacle planets. There used to be a lot of things in this game. But it's just gotten blander and more generic every update. The races are even getting blander. They SHOULD have had racial traits that made each one interesting to play. They don't. In fact, in the next update, you're losing racial themed weapons. So, you're losing anything identifiable about the race outside of the sprite, and even that's covered up by armor most of the time.
Verdict: Get this on sale for >80% off.

Just Cause 2 Multiplayer
For anybody unfamiliar with Just Cause 2 here is a brief summary. You are Agency operative Rico Rodriguez and have been dispatched to the wondrous (albeit mythical) isle of Panau in order to overthrow the reigning dictator Pandak “Baby” Panay using a wide variety of weapons and vehicles but mainly blowing♥♥♥♥♥♥up and using your grappling hook to break the laws of physics along with your instantly respawning parachute. Okay? Good.
Suffice to the say when the game came out in 2010 it was pretty well received but it lacked any form of multiplayer or online experience. 3 years later and one small team of passionate develops later and now you can terrorise the island of Panau with thousands of other players, or you can just run them over with a neon pink bus…
Good Stuff
This game was a lot of fun just playing on your own, when you add a server of hundreds of people to that mix it’s 100% unbridled chaos. Each server hosts a different style of the mod, at it’s base level the multiplayer mod features a system where kills earn you cash and cash buys you weapons, vehicles and player skins. In addition to straight up murdering fools for cold hard cash you can also participate in events that take place all over the, quite frankly, gargantuan map such as races and demolition derbys. Not every server is the same however, some will force the charge for weapons and such whereas others will have the store completely free, some will have god mode and others will have the ability to alter the mass of your vehicles. All of this alone is enough to make this mod great, but its true greatness comes from the players. There’s no doubt that this game is best played with a friend because it allows you to wreak havoc upon other players and each other, a personal favourite between my friends and I is throwing buses at each other at high speeds using the overly hilarious “boost” feature which is activated when shift is pressed and dramatically increases your speed to ridiculous levels (even allowing boats to fly across the map).
It’s not all about harassing though, it’s the random events that people create that drive the fun in this game. Starting a convoy of trucks and driving up a mountain to a ski-resort sounds like something you would find in Euro Truck Simulator but when it involves 10+ people all talking to each other in chat and occasionally hurling cars at each other on the way it stops feeling like a server with blank names and starts feeling like a community having fun which tends to be lacking in multiplayer experiences as of late. The norm tends to be people informing you that they have slept with your mother several times.
Bad stuff
This game has a huge map full of diverse and interesting locales and in the singleplayer it’s also vastly populated, in multiplayer however there are no npcs to come after you when you blow up a power plant, no civilians to hang from trees. I can’t really complain about this too much because the fact that the mod exists as it does is a great thing. I’m no modder and can only imagine how hard these guys worked to create this mod so I can’t hold something like this against them especially as the mod is somewhat in its infancy in terms of large scale play.
So…
There are some things I would love to see make an appearance as I said, NPCs would be a huge addition that would really have an impact on the way the multiplayer works and could lead to some great in game events like overthrowing a military base. Also if I could grapple other players to stuff that would be fantastic. Besides those two very minor things that are 100% personal I can’t really fault it, this is a fantastic mod that has breathed life into a game most people had forgotten about and hell if it leads to Just Cause 3 with a multiplayer like this built in I will be bloody ecstatic.

I played Blitzkrieg 3 during the free weekend, and found it to be an underwhelming RTS experience that’s hindered by its 'always online' requirement.
The game clearly suffers extended loading times and constant disconnections as a result of requiring a constant connection to their servers (yes, even during the single player campaign). In my relatively short time with the game I’ve had around 5-6 length disconnects – one of which occurred after completing a lengthy mission and my progress lost. At this point I decided to uninstall.
The game itself finds itself in an awkward space with existing WWII RTS titles doing things better. Company of Heroes features a far more polished experience while the Men of War series tops this title if you're looking for something more realistic mechanics (in fact even CoH manages to top Blitzkrieg in this regard).
I get the impression that this game wants to be a deep strategy game
However tactics mostly revolve around scouting effectively in order to gain the first strike advantage over your opponent. This isn’t helped by the maps that’re relatively simple and are on the small side. There isn’t much room for micro and often engagements are most efficiently dealt with by blobbing units to overwhelm opponents in smaller numbers. The a.i. is pretty basic despite claims to the contrary – I didn’t have any problems beating the ‘hard’ a.i. despite still being a newbie.
Single player offers a nice sense of progression as you unlock units to bring into battle, gain veterans and upgrades for your units as well as commanders. Although this could have been much better if units gained more gameplay altering abilities rather than minor stat buffs. The game doesn’t look great, but apart from a few wayward animations it’s not offensively bad. The maps have a nice amount of environmental detail – though you’d expect this since you can’t rotate the camera.
It's not terrible, but overall there are better (and far cheaper/older) options out there. Despite this as an RTS fan & history buff I may have been tempted to pick this up on sale if it wasn’t for the always online requirement. Hopefully this is something that will change in future.

Do NOT buy this game if you're a fan of the Total Annihilation or Supreme Commander games.
1. The game has only 3 modes you can play: Galatic War, AI Skirmish, Multiplayer
1.a) Galactic War is complete garbage. It sounds good in theory but it's extremly badly implemented and it feel slike the devs rushed it out just to get it over with (quite the same feel you get for the entire game too). I won't get into the details of why it's bad because it would make this review huge, just take my word for it, Galactic War is basically a feature that you will try out for a couple of hours (if you're really forcing yourself) and at the end of the day you'll realize it's just useless and you'll never touch it again.
1.b) AI Skirmish is complete garbage. And this is not the mode itself, it's just the game design. The game itself is bad because of the whole planet system which (again as with pretty much everything in this game) sounds good in theory but it's horrible in reality. The AI is garbage on lower difficulty settings, it does nothing, it just sits there. However, if you take it up, the AI becomes unmanageable and the ONLY way to play is to, you've guessed it, out-rush it. Which takes the joy out of everything. You can't really take any time to enjoy anything, you just have to rush rush rush rush everything. Defense buildings? Useless, rush units instead. Nukes? Useless, rush units instead. Tactics? Useless, rush units instead. Strategy? Useless, rush units instead. And after you rushed the whole freaking planet and cleared everything and you've got extractors all over the planet, think you can relax for a while and enjoy yourself? Think again! NO, the rush is not over because the next thing you'll know is that the AI will throw another planet at you and whipe you out. So you have to pick another planet to invade, and do the whole rushing thing all over again while at the same time pray that you don't get slammed by ANOTHER planet in the face while you're busy invading your second planet. Or, for extra stress and miserable gameplay, you can rush extra hard and invade all the enemy planets at the same time just to make sure nobody planet-slams you. OH the joys of clicking around through 4 planets between hundreds of units in a complete and utter indistinguishable mess, just mindlessly throwing piles of units at the enemy in order to out-rush their mindless throwing of units at you. LOVELY!
1.c) Multiplayer is pretty much the feature around which the game was built, the other 2 mods were just added so the devs can sell the game to more players (unsuspecting fools). IF you have some friends and you want to play the game with them, then maybe you'd get something out of this. Personally I hate RTS multiplayer, I like to call it RTRs which stands for RealTimeRushings. In multiplayer an RTS game is nothing but a race on who clicks faster, that's all it is, nothing else. Multiplayer removes tactical thinking, strategic planning, the joy of designing and building your base, planning and setting up defenses, it pretty much removes all the things that I like about RTS games, and it boils everything down to that one single feature that I don't like about RTS games, which is micromanaging butloads of units and frantically clicking. SO, if you enjoy that, then great, you're getting a game with 1 mode, multiplayer, otherwise, don't bother. Or at least if you buy it, don't make the mistake of going over the refund criteria like I did. (I already refunded the first PA game a year ago since it was unplayable due to bugs, now I got this thinking it's better, and the bugs are gone but now I got to experience the game and the game is crap... aand too late for refund, so I got punked!)
2. RTS games already put a huge amount of stress on the player and drain the player's attention on boring, repeating, micro-management chores. Any half-decent game designer would have the common sense to balance that out with game features that alleviate this stress, like for example unit grouping where instead of having 10 billion individually controlled units, you instead control unit groups with features like auto-reinforcement and other game systems that take away the need for micro-management in order to free up the player's concentration so the player can enjoy the POSITIVE aspects of RTS, like, you know... STRATEGY and TACTICS, and DEFENSES, and ECONOMICS, and BASE BUILDING.
This is where PA fails the most. Unlike other games that manage to reach a balance between the tedious process of micro-management and everything else, PA drops the player into a micro-management hell. Unlike Total Anihilation and Supreme Commander where turtling was a viable strategy, which allowed players to fortify themselves into a gigantic, extremely well defended base, which gave them the time to plan an actual strategy and require some sort of minimal level of tactics to be employed, in PA there's none of that.
PA does have a lot of defensive structures, but the game design itself makes those structures useless. Early game your commander can defend itself quite well so early game defensive structures are just a waste of time. And yes, since the game is a rush-fest, time is your only REAL resource, and wasting that resource on defensive structures that would do nothing to help you out-rush your enemy, would mean you're just setting yourself up to get out-rushed. Instead, just build a factory and start mass producing tanks, let them pile up a bit, then throw them at the enemy and repeat. That's pretty much the core game mechanic right there. Crank out units, pile them up, throw them at the enemy, repeat. It doesn't matter what units you crank out, it doesn't matter where you send them, as long as you do it faster than the enemy, that's all that matters.
To top things off, PA has... planets... And a whole extra layer of units, which is orbital units. So it massively ADDS to the micro-management hell adding even more units you just HAVE to use (if you play multi-planetary maps) while at the same time forcing the player to jump around between multiple planets and multiple bases and multiple layers of focus zooming in-and-out of surface/orbital/system views and planets. IT IS HORRID.
And to top things off... you may think "that's fine, I'll just play single-planet maps"... WRONG! The single planet maps are boring as hell. Even the largest planets are just tiny balls. Besides getting ball-syndrome from the constant claustrophobic feel that you get when you zoom out and constantly have to spin around this tiny ball which is your map (not to mention the disorientation that causes), there's nothing in the map itself to provide any foundations for tactics. The terrian features are mostly non existent, there are surface level movement impediments, out of which water is the largest one (IF you're on a planet that has water) but there just isn't enough and the maps are way too tiny for them to matter in any way, especially considering there are 2 layers that are not impacted by land at all, which is air and orbital, which delivers a final blow to the concept of tactics in this game, completely shattering any form of it.
I think I'm gonna stop here, this review is already huge. BAD GAME. Worst RTS I've played in my whole life, and I've been playing games since the 80s. This is the FIRST RTS I ever pick up and NOT "finish" (there isn't even anything to finish /facepalm).
